'''Rodrigo Antonio Isgró Alastra''' (born 24 March 1999) is an Argentine professional [[rugby union]] player who plays as a [[Wing (rugby union)|winger]] for [[Harlequin F.C.|Harlequins]] and [[Argentina national rugby union team|Argentina]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Rodrigo Isgro |url=https://www.world.rugby/sevens-series/player/mens/66776 |website=world.rugby |access-date=7 December 2021}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Isgró was born on 24 March 1999 in [[Mendoza, Argentina]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Rodrigo Isgro |url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/athletes/rodrigo-isgro-29199 |website=www.nbcolympics.com |access-date=10 September 2026}}</ref> He started playing rugby at the age of 4 at Mendoza Rugby Club, having been introduced to the sport by his uncle, who was also a rugby player.<ref>{{cite web |title=El esfuerzo y el entrenamiento valen más que el talento |url=https://infomendoza.info/un-cafe-con/el-esfuerzo-y-el-entrenamiento-valen-mas-que-el-talento |website=infomendoza.info |access-date=10 September 2026 |language=es |date=21 December 2021}}</ref>

== Club career ==
In September 2024, he signed for [[Rugby Premiership]] side [[Harlequin F.C.|Harlequins]] for the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{cite web|website=BBC Sport|access-date=4 September 2024|title=Harlequins sign Argentinian international Isgro|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/rugby-union/articles/cdjwpjm1en1o|date=3 September 2024}}</ref> In October 2024, he made his debut for the club scoring two tries against [[Bath Rugby|Bath]] at the [[Twickenham Stoop|Stoop]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Harlequins fall to agonising defeat against Bath |url=https://www.quins.co.uk/article/harlequins-fall-to-agonising-defeat-against-bath |publisher=Harlequins |access-date=27 October 2024}}</ref> The following week, he scored on in his first away game for the club in a 36–19 win against [[Exeter Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Match report: Five tries secure a bonus point on the road |url=https://www.quins.co.uk/article/match-report-five-tries-secures-a-bonus-point-on-the-road |publisher=Harlequins |access-date=27 October 2024}}</ref> In April 2025, he was banned for three weeks, with the option to reduce to two weeks upon the completion of tackling safety course, after a head-on-head contact with [[Bath Rugby|Bath]] winger [[Joe Cokanasiga]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pilnick |first1=Brent |title=Harlequins winger Isgro banned for dangerous tackle |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/rugby-union/articles/c4g8pj38j63o |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=4 April 2025}}</ref> In May 2025, after returning from his suspension, he scored two tries against [[Gloucester Rugby|Gloucester]] during a 38–19 victory in the Big Summer Kick Off fixture.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lanigan |first1=Adam |title=Gloucester's play-off hopes hit by Quins thrashing |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/rugby-union/articles/cz95zg09pneo |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=12 May 2025}}</ref>

== International career ==
He played for Argentina in junior rugby and played 15 a side [[rugby union]] for Mendoza Rugby Club, and also appeared at the [[2019 World Rugby Under 20 Championship|2019 U20 World Championships]]. He was named in the [[Rugby sevens at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's team squads|Argentina squad]] for the [[Rugby sevens at the 2020 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/en/results/rugby-sevens/athlete-profile-n1362773-isgro-rodrigo.htm |title=Rodrigo Isgro |publisher=Tokyo 2020 |access-date=27 July 2021 |archive-date=29 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210929053913/https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/en/results/rugby-sevens/athlete-profile-n1362773-isgro-rodrigo.htm |url-status=dead}}</ref>

He was part of the winning Pumas team at the [[Rugby sevens at the 2022 South American Games – Men's tournament|2022 South American Games]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.elciudadanoweb.com/los-pumas-7-lograron-nuevamente-el-oro-en-los-juegos-sudamericanos-con-aporte-rosarino/ |website=elciudadanoweb |accessdate=28 July 2024 |title=Pumas 7 won gold again at the South American Games with Rosario's contribution |date=10 October 2022}}</ref>

Isgró made his fifteens [[Test match (rugby union)|test]] debut for [[Argentina national rugby union team|Argentina]] against [[Australia national rugby union team|Australia]] in the [[2023 Rugby Championship]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=25 July 2024 |title=Rodrigo Isgró Free to Play vs France in Olympics Quarter Final |url=https://www.americasrugbynews.com/2024/07/25/rodrigo-isgro-free-to-play-vs-france-in-olympics-quarter-final/ |access-date=6 August 2024 |website=Americas Rugby News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=29 October 2023 |title=Rodrigo Isgró Named World's Best Rugby 7's Player |url=https://www.americasrugbynews.com/2023/10/29/rodrigo-isgro-named-worlds-best-rugby-7s-player/ |access-date=6 August 2024 |website=Americas Rugby News |language=en-US}}</ref> He was later selected for Argentina's [[2023 Rugby World Cup|World Cup]] squad.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> He was named [[World Rugby Men's Sevens Player of the Year]] in October that year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 October 2023 |title=Ardie Savea named World Rugby Men's Player of the Year 2023 |url=https://www.world.rugby/news/884118/world-rugby-awards-winners-2023 |access-date=6 August 2024 |website=www.world.rugby}}</ref><ref name=":3" />

In 2024, He was named as a traveling reserve for [[Argentina national rugby sevens team|Argentina]] at the [[Rugby sevens at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|Summer Olympics]] in [[Paris]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=28 June 2024 |title=Argentina Roster for Paris 2024 Olympic Games |url=https://www.americasrugbynews.com/2024/06/28/argentina-roster-for-paris-2024-olympic-games/ |access-date=25 July 2024 |website=Americas Rugby News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2024 |title=Argentina - Rugby Sevens Olympic Games Paris 2024 |url=https://www.world.rugby/tournaments/olympics/paris-2024/participating-nations/argentina |access-date=26 July 2024 |website=www.world.rugby}}</ref> He was free to play against [[France national rugby sevens team|France]] in the Quarter Final after completing his suspension, he also replaced [[Germán Schulz]] who suffered a grade 2 sprained knee.<ref name=":2" />

In November 2025, having been 21–0 down, he scored a try as Argentina beat Scotland during the [[2025 end-of-year rugby union internationals|2025 Autumn Nations Series]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=McLaughlin |first1=Luke |title=Santi Carreras orchestrates stunning Argentina comeback against Scotland |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/nov/16/scotland-argentina-rugby-union-test-match-report |publisher=The Guardian |access-date=17 November 2025}}</ref>

'''Claire Cory''' (born September 11, 1998) is an American politician serving as a member of the [[North Dakota Senate]] from the 42nd district. She assumed office on December 2, 2024, succeeding [[Curt Kreun]]. Cory previously served as a member of the [[North Dakota House of Representatives]] for District 42 from 2019 to 2024.

== Early life and education ==
Cory was born on September 11, 1998, in [[Grand Forks, North Dakota]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Legislative Action Center |url=https://app7.vocusgr.com/webpublish/Controller.aspx?SiteName=AIADA&Definition=ViewLegislator&LegislatorID=160957 |website=app7.vocusgr.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ncsl.org/state-legislatures-news/details/ready-for-the-world-8-of-the-nations-youngest-state-lawmakers|title=Ready for the World: 8 of the Nation’s Youngest State Lawmakers|publisher=[[National Conference of State Legislatures]]|first=Kelley|last=Griffin|date=October 3, 2022|access-date=June 26, 2026}}</ref> She graduated from [[Grand Forks Central High School]], and earned a Bachelor of Science degree in public administration and political science from the  [[University of North Dakota]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wenzel|first=Korrie|title=District 42 selects Claire Cory to fill vacant House spot|url=https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/government-and-politics/4719132-District-42-selects-Claire-Cory-to-fill-vacant-House-spot|url-status=live|access-date=2021-08-24|website=Grand Forks Herald|date=12 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191012181445/https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/government-and-politics/4719132-District-42-selects-Claire-Cory-to-fill-vacant-House-spot |archive-date=2019-10-12 }}{{failed verification|date=September 2024}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 2018, Cory worked as an intern for the [[North Dakota Republican Party]] and [[United States Senate]]. She also volunteered on [[Kevin Cramer]]'s re-election campaign.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kautzman|first=Alex|title=Despite contentiousness, young North Dakotans continue to engage in politics|url=https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/government-and-politics/6875864-Despite-contentiousness-young-North-Dakotans-continue-to-engage-in-politics|url-status=live|access-date=2021-08-24|website=Grand Forks Herald|date=8 February 2021 |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210208121549/https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/government-and-politics/6875864-Despite-contentiousness-young-North-Dakotans-continue-to-engage-in-politics |archive-date=2021-02-08 }}</ref> She was also an election worker for [[Grand Forks County, North Dakota]]. Cory was selected to succeed [[Jake Blum]] in the [[North Dakota House of Representatives]] in October 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Claire Cory|url=https://ballotpedia.org/Claire_Cory|access-date=2021-08-24|website=Ballotpedia|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Mook|first=Sydney|title=New Grand Forks legislators Claire Cory and Zachary Ista adjust to life in Bismarck|url=https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/government-and-politics/6863186-New-Grand-Forks-legislators-Claire-Cory-and-Zachary-Ista-adjust-to-life-in-Bismarck|url-status=live|access-date=2021-08-24|website=Grand Forks Herald|date=30 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210130143704/https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/government-and-politics/6863186-New-Grand-Forks-legislators-Claire-Cory-and-Zachary-Ista-adjust-to-life-in-Bismarck |archive-date=2021-01-30 }}</ref> Cory assumed her office on October 11, 2019, and was subsequently elected in November 2020. She is the youngest female ever elected to the legislature in the state of North Dakota.{{citation needed|date=September 2024}}

In August 2021, Cory created a [[Change.org]] petition demanding that the University of North Dakota remove its policy on face masks amidst the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Petition launched to remove UND's mask mandate|url=https://news.yahoo.com/petition-launched-remove-unds-mask-003100781.html|access-date=2021-08-24|website=news.yahoo.com|date=24 August 2021 }}</ref>

In August 2022, Cory was revealed to be a member of a [[Telegram (software)|Telegram]] group called the North Dakota Young Republicans which "frequently featured bigoted slurs and [[white supremacist]] tropes" in its messages between members, including personal attacks against gay public figures, such as House member [[Joshua Boschee]], as well as [[Antisemitic trope#Controlling the media|anti-Semitic conspiracy theories]].<ref name="port">{{cite news|url=https://www.inforum.com/opinion/columns/port-republi-message-group-posted-slurs-while-candidates-activists-and-elected-officials-looked-on|title=Republican message group posted slurs while candidates, activists, and elected officials looked on|work=[[The Forum of Fargo-Moorhead]]|first=Rob|last=Port|date=August 19, 2022|access-date=September 9, 2024|archive-url=https://archive.today/20220819210910/https://www.inforum.com/opinion/columns/port-republi-message-group-posted-slurs-while-candidates-activists-and-elected-officials-looked-on|archive-date=August 19, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> Despite claiming she had the group muted and did not read the messages, she was shown to have posted messages in the group.<ref name=port/> "The statements in question do not represent my values or those of my district," said Cory. "Representative Boschee is a legislator who serves his district admirably, and while I disagree with him politically, his sexuality should not be used as a personal attack."<ref name=port/>

On February 26, 2024, Cory announced a campaign for the District 42 [[North Dakota Senate]] seat being vacated by [[Curt Kreun]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-26 |title=Rep. Claire Cory announces bid for North Dakota Senate |url=https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/local/rep-claire-cory-announces-bid-for-north-dakota-senate |access-date=2024-06-05 |website=Grand Forks Herald }}</ref> Cory would go on to win the primary and secure the Republican nomination for the seat in June,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-12 |title=Claire Cory takes District 42 Republican Senate primary; Osowski, O'Brien win in House primary |url=https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/local/claire-cory-takes-district-42-republican-senate-primary-osowski-obrien-win-in-house-primary |access-date=2024-06-17 |website=Grand Forks Herald }}</ref> before winning the seat over Democratic challenger Rodney Gigstad in November.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-06 |title=Cory and Meyer win Grand Forks Senate seats; Vetter and O'Brien retain House positions |url=https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/local/cory-and-meyer-win-grand-forks-senate-seats-vetter-and-obrien-retain-house-positions |access-date=2024-11-06 |website=Grand Forks Herald |language=en}}</ref>

== Legal issues ==
Cory was arrested and charged with [[driving under the influence]] (DUI) on May 7, 2024,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-07 |title=Grand Forks state Rep. Claire Cory charged with driving under the influence |url=https://www.inforum.com/news/north-dakota/grand-forks-state-rep-claire-cory-charged-with-driving-under-the-influence |access-date=2024-05-17 |website=InForum |first=Sav |last=Kelly }}</ref> with a reported [[blood alcohol content]] of 0.186%.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-07-10 |title=Grand Forks Rep. Claire Cory pleads guilty to reckless driving |url=https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/local/grand-forks-rep-claire-cory-pleads-guilty-to-reckless-driving |access-date=2024-07-10 |website=Grand Forks Herald |first=Sav |last=Kelly }}</ref> She initially pled not guilty,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-21 |title=Grand Forks Rep. Claire Cory's DUI arraignment canceled |url=https://www.grandforksherald.com/news/north-dakota/grand-forks-rep-claire-corys-dui-arraignment-canceled |access-date=2024-07-10 |website=Grand Forks Herald }}</ref> but later plead guilty to an amended charge of [[reckless driving]] on July 2, 2024.<ref name=":0" /> Despite her BAC being over twice the legal limit in North Dakota, she was not charged with aggravated DUI – which comes with a mandatory jail sentence under state law – since she was charged at the municipal level.<ref name="video">{{cite news|url=https://www.inforum.com/opinion/columns/port-rep-claire-corys-dui-arrest-video-raises-some-interesting-questions|title=Port: Rep. Claire Cory's DUI arrest video raises some interesting questions|website=InForum|first=Rob|last=Port|date=July 17, 2024|access-date=June 23, 2026}}</ref> Cory was fined $901 and given a [[suspended sentence]] of 12 days in jail.<ref name=":0" />

In the body cam footage of her arrest, the police officer said: "North Dakota and North Dakotans don't really put that much of a stigma on DUIs," to which Cory replied: "Yeah, but I'm an elected official".<ref name=video/>

He represented the United States at the [[2020 Summer Paralympics]].{{cite web |url=https://www.teamusa.org/usparatrackandfield/athletes/Hagan-Landry |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210830045645/https://www.teamusa.org/usparatrackandfield/athletes/Hagan-Landry |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 30, 2021 |title=Hagan Landry |website=TeamUSA.org |publisher=[[United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee]] |access-date=August 30, 2021}} ==Athletic Career== Landry attended [[Delcambre High School]] in [[Delcambre, Louisiana|Delcambre, Louisana]] where he competed in track and field events shotput, discus, javelin, and the 100 meter dash.{{Cite news |date=2013-05-05 |title=Track |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/abbeville-meridional-track/202121175/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |work=Abbeville Meridional |pages=11}} Landry represented the United States in the [[Athletics at the 2020 Summer Paralympics – Men's shot put#F41|men's shot put F41]] event at the [[2020 Summer Paralympics]] and won a silver medal.{{cite web |url=https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/paralympic-games/en/results/athletics/athlete-profile-n1662461-landry-hagan.htm |title=Hagan Landry |work=Tokyo 2020 Paralympics |publisher=[[Tokyo Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games]] |access-date=August 30, 2021 |archive-date=August 30, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210830044140/https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/paralympic-games/en/results/athletics/athlete-profile-n1662461-landry-hagan.htm |url-status=dead }} At the 2023 World Championships in Paris, Landry won a bronze medal. == Coaching == Landry was an assistant coach of the throws for the women's track and field team at [[West Virginia State University]] for the 2025 season. In early 2026 he was announced as the throws coach for [[Grambling State Tigers track and field|Grambling State University]].{{Cite web |title=Grambling State Track & Field Adds Landry to Staff as Assistant Coach |url=https://gsutigers.com/news/2026/1/8/mens-track-and-field-grambling-state-track-field-adds-landry-to-staff-as-assistant-coach.aspx |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=Grambling State University Athletics |language=en}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Landry, Hagan}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:1994 births]] [[Category:American men shot putters]] [[Category:Athletes (track and field) at the 2020 Summer Paralympics]] [[Category:Medalists at the 2020 Summer Paralympics]] [[Category:Medalists at the World Para Athletics Championships]] [[Category:Paralympic medalists in athletics (track and field)]] [[Category:Paralympic silver medalists for the United States]] [[Category:Track and field athletes from New Orleans]] [[Category:Parapan American Games medalists in athletics (track and field)]] [[Category:Medalists at the 2019 Parapan American Games]] [[Category:Parapan American Games gold medalists for the United States]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:People from Delcambre, Louisiana]] {{US-Paralympic-medalist-stub}}

'''Rosie Tucker''' is an American singer-songwriter from [[Los Angeles]], [[California]].<ref name="guitarworld">{{cite web |last1=Doria |first1=Matt |title=Spotlight: Rosie Tucker |date=7 June 2021 |url=https://www.guitarworld.com/features/spotlight-rosie-tucker |publisher=[[Guitar World]] |access-date=27 October 2021}}</ref>  ''[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]'' has acclaimed Tucker's "surging [[Pop music|pop]] [[Hook (music)|hooks]] and sharp lyricism".<ref name="pitchfork">{{cite web |last1=Philo |first1=Katie |title=29 Great Records You May Have Missed: Spring 2021 |date=28 July 2021 |url=https://pitchfork.com/features/lists-and-guides/29-great-records-you-may-have-missed-spring-2021/ |publisher=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |access-date=27 October 2021}}</ref>

==History==
Tucker is a native of the [[San Fernando Valley]]. Tucker's mother grew up on a [[farm]] in [[Illinois]], later becoming a [[Programmer|computer programmer]], and their father was a [[United States Marine]] who served in the [[Iraq War]]; the two met in a [[Self-service laundry|laundromat]]. Tucker started singing as a toddler, studied music at the [[University of Southern California]], and in college grew disillusioned with organized religion.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://open.spotify.com/episode/4EB5iArZeYIZyivn80bov8?si=xa07c3bgS5680cih189Mhg|title=Episode 398: Rosie Tucker|website=[[Spotify]]|date=31 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://15questions.net/interview/fifteen-questions-interview-rosie-tucker/page-1/|title = 15 questions | Interview | Rosie Tucker | the Myth of the Unwell Genius}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/rosie-tucker-la-based-singer-songwriter/id1543825536?i=1000533056004|title = Roadcase: Rosie Tucker (LA-based Singer Songwriter) on Apple Podcasts}}</ref>

Tucker self-released their first full-length album in 2015 titled ''Lowlight''.<ref name="stereogum">{{cite web |last1=Rettig |first1=James |title=Rosie Tucker – "Gay Bar" |date=15 January 2019 |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2028547/rosie-tucker-gay-bar/premiere/ |publisher=[[Stereogum]] |access-date=27 October 2021}}</ref> In 2019, Tucker announced their second full-length album, ''Never Not Never Not Never Not'', which was released on New Professor Music.<ref name="stereogum"/> In 2021, Tucker announced they had signed to [[Epitaph Records]].<ref name="brooklynvegan">{{cite web |last1=Hatfield |first1=Amanda |title=Rosie Tucker signs to Epitaph for new LP, 'Sucker Supreme' (watch "Habanero" video) |date=24 March 2021 |url=https://www.brooklynvegan.com/rosie-tucker-signs-to-epitaph-for-new-lp-sucker-supreme-watch-habanero-video/ |publisher=[[BrooklynVegan]] |access-date=27 October 2021}}</ref> They also announced their third full-length album titled ''Sucker Supreme''. The album was released on April 30, 2021.<ref name="allsongsconsidered">{{cite news |title=New Music Friday: The Top 7 Albums Out On April 30 |newspaper=NPR.org |url=https://www.npr.org/2021/04/27/991243810/new-music-friday-the-top-7-albums-out-on-april-30 |publisher=[[All Songs Considered]] |access-date=27 October 2021}}</ref> The album was listed on [[Pitchfork (website)|''Pitchfork'']]'s list of "29 Great Records You May Have Missed: Spring 2021".<ref name="pitchfork">{{cite web |last1=Philo |first1=Katie |title=29 Great Records You May Have Missed: Spring 2021 |date=28 July 2021 |url=https://pitchfork.com/features/lists-and-guides/29-great-records-you-may-have-missed-spring-2021/ |publisher=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |access-date=27 October 2021}}</ref> Tucker released a fourth album of songs no longer than one minute and 16 seconds, ''Tiny Songs Volume 1'', in September 2023.<ref name="kelati">{{cite news |last1=Kelati |first1=Haben |title=Singer-songwriter Rosie Tucker goes big with tiny songs |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2023/11/08/rosie-tucker-concert-dc/ |access-date=November 28, 2023 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=November 8, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231128182634/https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2023/11/08/rosie-tucker-concert-dc/ |archive-date=November 28, 2023}}</ref> Their fifth studio album, ''[[Utopia Now!]]'', was released on March 22, 2024.<ref name="bv UN">{{cite news |last1=Hatfield |first1=Amanda |title=Rosie Tucker announces new LP & tour, shares 'All My Exes Live in Vortexes' |url=https://www.brooklynvegan.com/rosie-tucker-announces-new-lp-tour-shares-all-my-exes-live-in-vortexes/ |access-date=March 18, 2024 |work=[[BrooklynVegan]] |date=January 23, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240126031750/https://www.brooklynvegan.com/rosie-tucker-announces-new-lp-tour-shares-all-my-exes-live-in-vortexes/ |archive-date=January 26, 2024}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Tucker identifies as [[queer]] and uses ''[[Singular they|they/them]]'' pronouns.<ref name="guitardotcom">{{cite web |last1=Baines |first1=Huw |title=Introducing... Rosie Tucker, the underground darling crafting songs about sweetness, grit and queer self-discovery |date=3 August 2021 |url=https://guitar.com/features/interviews/introducing-rosie-tucker-the-underground-darling-crafting-songs-about-sweetness-grit-and-queer-self-discovery/ |publisher=[[Guitar.com]] |access-date=27 October 2021}}</ref>

'''Anzelo Tuitavuki''' (born 10 October 1998 in New Zealand) is a professional [[rugby union]] player, who currently plays as a [[Wing (rugby union)|wing]] for Welsh club {{rut|Dragons}} in the [[United Rugby Championship]].<ref name="Dragons to sign Tonga ace Tuitavuki">{{cite press release | url=https://dragonsrfc.wales/news/2026/march/dragons-to-sign-tonga-ace-tuitavuki.html | title=Dragons to sign Tonga ace Tuitavuki | work=Dragons RFC | date=16 March 2026 | access-date=20 July 2026}}</ref> He previously played for {{Rut|Hawke's Bay}} in New Zealand's domestic [[National Provincial Championship (2006–present)|National Provincial Championship]] competition<ref name="2023 Magpies squad release">{{cite web | url=https://www.sporty.co.nz/magpies/newsarticle/130396 | title=2023 Magpies squad release | website=Hawke's Bay Rugby Union | language=en | date=5 July 2023 | access-date=6 July 2023}}</ref>, {{rut|Moana Pasifika}} in [[Super Rugby]]<ref name="Azelo and Joe join Moana Pasifika">{{cite press release|url=https://moanapasifika.co.nz/azelo-and-joe-join-moana-pasifika/|title=Azelo and Joe join Moana Pasifika|work=Moana Pasifika|date=9 November 2021|accessdate=9 November 2021}}</ref> and {{rut|Colomiers}} in the French [[Pro D2]].<ref name="Signature – Anzelo Tuitavuki">{{cite press release | url=https://colomiers-rugby.com/signature-anzelo-tuitavuki/ | title=Signature – Anzelo Tuitavuki | work=Colomiers Rugby | language=french | date=25 July 2024 | access-date=1 August 2024}}</ref>

On 27 May 2022, Tuitavuki{{Snds}}who is of Tongan descent and [[International rugby union eligibility rules|eligible]] to represent [[Tonga]] internationally{{Snd}}was named in the [[Tonga national rugby union team|Tongan]] national team for the [[2022 World Rugby Pacific Nations Cup|2022 Pacific Nations Cup]] and the [[2023 Rugby World Cup – Regional play-off and Final Qualification Tournament#Asia/Pacific_play-off|Asia/Pacific]] qualification match for the [[2023 Rugby World Cup]].<ref name="Our Ikale Tahi squad for the Pacific Nations & World Cup Qualifier 2022.">{{cite web | url=https://www.facebook.com/TongaRugbyOfficial/posts/3565454967014949 | title=Our Ikale Tahi squad for the Pacific Nations & World Cup Qualifier 2022. Congratulations to all the players who have made the team. | publisher=Tonga Rugby Union – via Facebook | date=27 May 2022 | access-date=28 May 2022}}</ref> He made his international test debut for Tonga on 2 July 2022 against [[Fiji national rugby union team|Fiji]].<ref name="Israel Folau, Charles Piutau and Malakai Fekitoa named for test rugby returns">{{cite news | url=https://www.rugbypass.com/news/israel-folau-charles-piutau-and-malakai-fekitoa-named-for-test-rugby-returns/ | title=Israel Folau, Charles Piutau and Malakai Fekitoa named for test rugby returns | work=Rugbypass | date=1 July 2022 | access-date=2 July 2022}}</ref>

{{short description|Australian politician and climate activist (born 1985)}} {{Use Australian English|date=November 2022}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2022}} {{Infobox officeholder | honorific_prefix = [[Australian Senate|Senator]] | name = Steph Hodgins-May | image = Steph_Hodgins-May.jpg | caption = Hodgins-May in 2023 | office = [[Leaders of the Australian Greens#Federal deputy parliamentary leaders|Deputy Leader of the Australian Greens]] | term_start = 30 September 2026 | leader = [[David Shoebridge]] | predecessor = [[Mehreen Faruqi]] | office1= [[Australian Senate|Senator]] for [[Victoria (state)|Victoria]] | predecessor1 = [[Janet Rice]] | term_start1 = 2 May 2024 | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|df=y|1985|8|23}} | birth_place = [[Ballarat, Victoria]], Australia | occupation = Political activist
Lawyer | relations = [[William Hill (Australian politician)|William Hill]] (great-great-grandfather) | website = {{URL|greens.org.au/vic/person/steph-hodgins-may}} }} '''Steph Hodgins-May''' (born 23 August 1985) is an Australian politician and [[environmental lawyer]]. She was elected deputy leader of the [[Australian Greens]] since 30 September 2026. She has been a [[Australian Senate|Senator]] for [[Victoria (state)|Victoria]] since 2024, representing the Greens. She was previously a Greens candidate for the [[Australian House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] on four occasions. Prior to entering parliament, she held roles with the [[United Nations]] and [[Greenpeace]]. == Early life and education == Steph Hodgins-May was born on 23 August 1985 in [[Ballarat]], Victoria.{{cite web |title=Senator Steph Hodgins-May |url=https://www.aph.gov.au/Senators_and_Members/Parliamentarian?MPID=310860 |publisher=Parliament of Australia |access-date=10 June 2024}} She was raised in [[Blampied, Victoria|Blampied]] in rural Victoria on a farm.{{Cite web|title=Meet our campaigners|url=https://www.greenpeace.org.au/meet-our-campaigners/|access-date=2021-11-18|website=Greenpeace Australia Pacific|language=en-AU}} Her father, Rod May, was a mayor of [[Shire of Hepburn|Hepburn Shire]].{{Cite news|date=2019-07-02|title=Daughters break down as they remember former mayor killed by dangerous driver|language=en-AU|work=ABC News|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2019-07-02/man-pleads-guilty-dangerous-driving-causing-former-mayors-death/11271594|access-date=2021-11-18}} Her mother was a media studies and drama teacher in Ballarat.{{Cite web|date=2009-09-30|title=Ballarat school mourns teacher taken by tsunami|url=https://www.smh.com.au/national/ballarat-school-mourns-teacher-taken-by-tsunami-20091001-gdan.html|access-date=2021-11-18|website=The Sydney Morning Herald|language=en}} Hodgins-May is the great-great-granddaughter of [[William Hill (Australian politician)|William Hill]], who was a founding member of the [[National Party of Australia|Country Party]] and a minister during the [[First Bruce Ministry|Bruce-Page]] government.{{Cite web|date=2026-10-03|title=Her great-great-grandfather helped create the National Party. Now she wants to 'bury it'|url=https://www.smh.com.au/politics/federal/her-great-great-grandfather-helped-create-the-national-party-now-she-wants-to-bury-it-20261003-p612c3.html |website=The Sydney Morning Herald|language=en}} She has a Bachelor of Law, Bachelor of Arts, and Master in International Relations from [[Deakin University]]. == Career == ===Early career=== Hodgins-May worked in [[property law]] before working in the Australian mission to the United Nations.{{Cite web|last=Willingham|first=Richard|date=2015-09-25|title=Labor confident of holding Melbourne Ports, despite Liberal and Greens challenge|url=https://www.theage.com.au/national/victoria/labor-confident-on-holding-melbourne-ports-despite-liberal--green-challenge-20150925-gjuyw7.html|access-date=2021-11-18|website=The Age|language=en}} She was also her father's business partner in their family's farm. Following the 2019 election, Hodgins-May took up a position as Greenpeace's Head of Pacific. In this position she pushed for Australia to do more to prevent [[climate change]] and to help the [[Pacific Islands]] with the challenges that climate change causes.{{Cite web|title=Biden Summit: Charities and churches call on PM to halve emissions by 2030 {{!}} Media Oxfam Australia|url=https://media.oxfam.org.au/2021/04/biden-summit-charities-and-churches-call-on-prime-minister-to-halve-emissions-by-2030/|access-date=2021-11-18|website=media.oxfam.org.au|language=en-US}}{{Cite web|last=McCulloch|first=Daniel|date=2020-07-24|title=States to handle environmental approvals|url=https://www.begadistrictnews.com.au/story/6848759/states-to-handle-environmental-approvals/|access-date=2021-11-18|website=Bega District News|language=en-AU}} === Political candidate === ==== 2013 election ==== Hodgins-May first ran for elected office at the [[2013 Australian federal election|2013 election]] for the [[division of Ballarat]], a safe Labor seat. She won 9.5% of the vote.{{Cite web|title=Ballarat - Federal Election 2013 |first=Antony |last=Green|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/federal-election-2013/guide/ball/|access-date=2021-11-18|website=ABC News|language=en}} ==== 2016 election ==== At the 2016 election, Hodgins-May contested the inner Melbourne seat of [[Division of Melbourne Ports|Melbourne Ports]], a seat held by Labor since 1906. In a three cornered contest between the Greens, Labor and Liberal, Hodgins-May secured 23.79% of the primary vote.{{Cite web|title=First preference count for the division of Melbourne Ports (VIC)|publisher=Australian Electoral Commission |url=https://results.aec.gov.au/20499/Website/HouseDivisionPage-20499-230.htm|access-date=2021-11-18|language=en-AU |date=28 July 2016}} The results of the election remained uncertain, with Hodgins-May closing in on the incumbent, Michael Danby with a strong preference flow.{{Cite news|last=Chang|first=Charis|date=2016-07-11|title=Do Greens still have a chance?|website=news.com.au|url=https://news.com.au/national/federal-election/do-the-greens-still-have-a-chance-to-pick-up-melbourne-ports/news-story/c5f88cd9d8a3a3f25d19c33e3585cb17|access-date=2021-11-18}}{{Cite web|date=2016-07-03|title=Greens face prospect that election result will not lead to gains|url=http://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2016/jul/03/greens-ponder-australian-election-vote-which-will-probably-not-lead-to-gains|access-date=2021-11-18|website=the Guardian|language=en}} However, Danby received strong support in the postal votes, and was ahead by fewer than 1000 votes on the seventh count of preferences. Hodgins-May was eliminated at that point, and her preferences allowed Danby to prevail in the final count over the Liberal candidate, Owen Guest. During the 2016 election campaign, Hodgins-May was invited with the other two major party candidates, [[Michael Danby]] and Owen Guest, to participate in a candidates' forum for the Jewish community, which makes up 9.9% of the [[division of Melbourne Ports]].{{cite web |title=Melbourne Ports 2016 Census All persons QuickStats |url=https://abs.gov.au/census/find-census-data/quickstats/2016/CED232 |website=Australian Bureau of Statistics }} The event was co-sponsored by [[Zionism Victoria|Zionism Victoria (ZV)]] and [[The Australian Jewish News]] (AJN).{{cn|date=September 2026}} After initially accepting the invitation, Hodgins-May declined due to event co-sponsor Zionism Victoria calling the United Nations a “nuisance and sham organisation”.{{Cite news|date=2016-06-09|title=Melbourne Ports Greens candidate pulls out of debate|url=https://www.crikey.com.au/2016/06/09/steph-hodgins-may-pulls-out-of-zionist-sponsored-debate/|url-access=registration|access-date=2021-11-18|work=Crikey|language=en-US |url-status=live}}{{Cite web|last=Levi|first=Joshua|title=Greens candidate 'hurts, insults' community|url=http://www.australianjewishnews.com/greens-candidate-hurts-insults-community/|access-date=2021-11-18|website=www.australianjewishnews.com|language=en-US}} Hodgins-May subsequently accepted a number of invitations to speak at a number of other Jewish organisations such as Mount Scopus, Habonim Dror, Jews for Refugees, and Limmud Oz.{{cite news |title=Selective Green to attend AUJS debate |url=https://www.crikey.com.au/2016/06/14/greens-zionist-debate/ |publisher=Crikey}} ==== 2019 election ==== Hodgins-May was the Greens candidate for the [[division of Macnamara]], the renamed former Division of Melbourne Ports, for the [[2019 Australian federal election|2019 federal election]]. While campaigning for the election, Hodgins-May secured the endorsement of [[Gillian Triggs]], who was the [[Australian Human Rights Commission|Australian human rights commissioner]] until 2017. The endorsement was a personal one and not an endorsement of the party as a whole.{{Cite web|title=Subscribe for award winning journalism |url=https://dsf.newscorpaustralia.com/theaustralian/subscription/|access-date=2021-11-18|language=en-AU}} Triggs came under fire from both the [[Liberal Party of Australia|Liberal]] and [[Australian Labor Party|Labor]] parties for giving the endorsement.{{Cite news|last=Brown|first=Greg|date=2019-02-22|title=Plibersek slams Triggs' backing for Green|work=The Australian|url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/nation/politics/plibersek-slams-triggs-backing-for-green/news-story/07eb01d2bec2c9fdfa9b3338f0663979|access-date=2021-11-18 |url-access=subscription}} While Hodgins-May increased her vote marginally, the new Labor candidate, [[Josh Burns (politician)|Josh Burns]] increased his primary vote significantly, while the Liberal Party vote fell, meaning Burns won the seat comfortably.{{Cite web|title=Macnamara (Key Seat) - Federal Election 2019|url=https://abc.net.au/news/elections/federal/2019/guide/macn|access-date=2021-11-18|website=abc.net.au|language=en-AU |first=Antony |last=Green}} ==== 2022 election ==== Hodgins-May was again preselected for the Greens in the Melbourne seat of [[Division of Macnamara|Macnamara]] for the 2022 election.{{Cite web|last=Douglas|first=Carly|title=Steph Hodgins-May back in the ring|url=https://www.australianjewishnews.com/steph-hodgins-may-back-in-the-ring/|access-date=2021-11-18|website=www.australianjewishnews.com|language=en-US}} It was one of the key seats that the Greens were targeting in their hopes of increasing their representation in parliament.{{Cite news|last=Smethurst|first=Annika|date=2021-10-21|title=Greens eyeing off five Melbourne seats in hopes of hung parliament|url=https://www.theage.com.au/politics/victoria/greens-eyeing-off-four-melbourne-seats-in-hopes-of-hung-parliament-20211020-p591ps.html|access-date=2021-11-18|website=The Age|language=en}} Hodgins-May increased her primary vote and finished second in primary votes behind Labor.{{cite web |url=https://greens.org.au/news/media-release/greens-winnable-macnamara-federal-electorate-candidate-announced-sonya-semmens |publisher=Victorian Greens Party |title=Greens winnable Macnamara federal electorate candidate announced: Sonya Semmens | Australian Greens |date=March 2024 }}{{Cite web |title=Macnamara (Key Seat) - Federal Election 2022 |first=Antony |last=Green |author-link=Antony Green |url=https://abc.net.au/news/elections/federal/2022/guide/macn |access-date=2022-06-09 |website=abc.net.au |language=en-AU }} ===Senator=== In 2023, Hodgins-May was pre-selected by The Greens to replace [[Janet Rice]] upon Rice's retirement in the first half of 2024.{{cite news |url=https://www.smh.com.au/politics/victoria/enormous-shoes-to-fill-ex-greenpeace-boss-to-replace-retiring-greens-senator-20231130-p5eo4u.html |url-access=registration |title='Enormous shoes to fill': Ex-Greenpeace boss to replace retiring Greens senator |access-date=1 December 2023 |date=30 November 2023 |first=Broede |last=Carmody|work=[[Sydney Morning Herald]]}} She was appointed to the Senate in a joint sitting of the [[Parliament of Victoria]] on 1 May 2024.{{cite web|url=https://www.parliament.vic.gov.au/4a5a17/globalassets/hansard-daily-pdfs/hansard-974425065-26304/hansard-974425065-26304.pdf|title=Joint Sitting of Parliament Legislative Council Wednesday 1 May 2024|page=93|website=Parliament of Victoria|date=1 May 2024|access-date=3 May 2024}} In May 2026, Hodgins-May chaired a Senate Select Committee on the Taxation of Gas Resources{{Cite web |last=corporateName=Commonwealth Parliament; address=Parliament House |first=Canberra |title=Committee Membership |url=https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Committees/Senate/Taxation_of_Gas_Resources/Committee_Membership |access-date=2026-07-22 |website=www.aph.gov.au |language=en-AU}} having spearheaded much of the public campaign for a 25 per cent tax on gas exports alongside other prominent crossbenchers such as [[David Pocock|Senator David Pocock]].{{Cite news |last=Jervis-Bardy |first=Dan |last2=Butler |first2=Josh |last3=Dhanji |first3=Krishani |last4=Cox |first4=Lisa |date=2026-04-29 |title=Anthony Albanese rules out gas export tax on existing contracts and criticises ‘populist’ campaign |url=https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/apr/29/anthony-albanese-rules-out-gas-export-tax-australia |access-date=2026-07-22 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}{{Cite web |date=2026-04-24 |title=Government says 'no change' in position amid growing calls for 25 per cent gas export tax |url=https://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/labor-say-no-change-on-gas-taxation/u41vnlg92 |access-date=2026-07-22 |website=SBS News |language=en}} On 30 September 2026, in the [[2026 Australian Greens leadership election|Greens leadership election]], following the resignation of leader Larissa Waters and deputy leader [[Mehreen Faruqi]], Hodgins-May ran for deputy leader of the Australian Greens. She was elected 6–5 in a two-candidate vote against Tasmanian Senator [[Vanessa Bleyer]]. [[David Shoebridge]] was elected leader.{{Cite news |date=2026-09-30 |title=Breaking: David Shoebridge named new Greens leader after three-way contest |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-09-30/federal-politics-greens-announce-new-leader-david-shoebridge/107211108 |access-date=2026-09-30 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}{{cite web | last1=Dhanji | first1=Krishani | last2=McIlroy | first2=Tom | last3=Butler | first3=Josh | title=David Shoebridge says 'we're here to replace Labor' in first remarks after being elected new Greens leader | publisher=The Guardian | date=30 September 2026 | url=https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/sep/30/david-shoebridge-greens-leadership-steph-hodgins-may-retreat-larissa-waters | access-date=30 September 2026}} == Political positions == Hodgins-May has taken a strong stance on climate policy, and has called on successive governments to do more. She has argued that government inaction has caused Australia to become a global pariah when it came to issues around the environment.{{Cite news|last=Hodgins-May|first=Steph|date=2021-03-28|title=Yes, achievements are important. So what has Morrison achieved on climate?|url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/7182272/yes-achievements-are-important-so-what-has-morrison-achieved-on-climate/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=2021-11-18|website=The Canberra Times|language=en-AU}} She is also an advocate for Australia increasing its foreign aid budget and to focus more on international development. == Personal life == As of 2021 Hodgins-May was living in the [[Melbourne]] suburb of [[Elwood, Victoria|Elwood]] with her partner Ogy Simic. She has a son.{{Cite web|title=Steph Hodgins-May, Greens Candidate for Macnamara|url=https://stephhodginsmay.org.au/|access-date=2021-11-18|website=Steph Hodgins-May, Greens Candidate for Macnamara|language=en-AU}} Simic, a lawyer, was elected to [[City of Port Phillip|Port Phillip City Council]] in 2016 and stood for the Greens at the [[2018 Victorian state election]].{{cite news|url=https://junctionjournalism.com/2018/10/15/greens-ogy-simic/|title=Albert Park – Greens: Ogy Simic|publisher=The Junction|date=15 October 2018|access-date=21 April 2025}} Hodgins-May's mother died in the [[2009 Samoa earthquake and tsunami|2009 Samoan tsunami]] while holidaying at a local resort.{{Cite news|first2=Darby|first1=Andra |last1=Jackson |last2=Andrew|date=2009-09-30|title=Surprise beachside holiday turns into tragedy|url=https://www.smh.com.au/national/surprise-beachside-holiday-turns-into-tragedy-20090930-gcrr.html|access-date=2021-11-18|website=The Sydney Morning Herald|language=en |url-access=registration}} In 2017 her father, Rod May, was killed in a traffic collision. '''Cleo Constantine Abram''' (born January 25, 1993) is an American [[video journalist]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleo Abram |url=https://www.journalismfestival.com/speaker/cleo-abram |website=JournalismFestival.com}}</ref><ref name="Creator">{{cite news |last1=Graber-Lipperman |first1=Nathan |date=30 June 2022 |title=From Vox to TikTok: Cleo Abram Explains The Future |url=https://powderblue.media/stories/cleo |access-date=13 May 2025 |work=Creator |publisher=Powder Blue Media}}</ref><ref name="Axios YouTube">{{cite news |last1=Flynn |first1=Kerry |title=YouTube's pitch to TV buyers: It's not just MrBeast |url=https://www.axios.com/2025/12/01/youtube-creator-premieres-tv-ads |access-date=3 December 2025 |work=[[Axios (website)|Axios]] |date=1 December 2025 |language=en}}</ref> She produced videos for ''[[Vox (website)|Vox]]'' until 2022, when she launched her own [[YouTube]] channel, ''Huge if True'',<ref name="YouTube blog">{{cite news |date=March 18, 2025 |title=5 huge if true moments for Cleo Abram |url=https://blog.youtube/creator-and-artist-stories/5-huge-if-true-moments-for-cleo-abram/ |access-date=13 May 2025 |work=YouTube Official Blog |publisher=[[YouTube]] |language=en-us}}</ref><ref name="Banner">{{cite news |last1=Gutierrez |first1=Sam |date=17 September 2024 |title=Cleo Abram – Huge* if True (YouTube) |url=https://www.thebanner.org/mixed-media/2024/06/cleo-abram-huge-if-true-youtube |access-date=13 May 2025 |work=[[The Banner (magazine)|The Banner]] |language=en}}</ref> which covers emerging technologies.<ref name="Semafor podcast">{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Ben |last2=Tani |first2=Max |author1-link=Ben Smith (journalist)|title=Mixed Signals: Professional optimist Cleo Abram on tech’s bright future |url=https://www.semafor.com/article/06/13/2025/cleo-abram-on-techs-bright-future |access-date=3 December 2025 |work=[[Semafor (website)|Semafor]] |date=June 13, 2025}}</ref> By June 2026, her channel had more than 8.1 million subscribers.

==Early life and education==
Abram was born and raised in [[Washington, D.C.]] After graduating from [[Sidwell Friends School]] in 2011,<ref>{{cite news |date=26 October 2021 |title=Video Producer Cleo Abram |url=https://intothegloss.com/2021/10/cleo-abram-beauty-routine/ |access-date=8 February 2024 |work=[[Into the Gloss]] |quote=I grew up in DC right after 9/11, and when I went to college, I really wanted to study the Middle East.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=22 March 2023 |title=Cleo Abram Biography, Age, Career, Boyfriend |url=https://thrillng.com/cleo-abram-biography-career-boyfriend-net-worth-tiktok/ |access-date=8 February 2024 |work=Thrill}}</ref> she attended [[Columbia University]], where she founded the school's [[TEDx|TEDx conference]] and was a University Senator for the [[Columbia College Student Council]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wang |first=Tracey |date=February 11, 2013 |title=CCSC elects new University Senator |url=https://www.columbiaspectator.com/2013/02/11/ccsc-elects-new-university-senator/ |access-date=12 January 2022 |work=[[Columbia Daily Spectator]]}}</ref>  She graduated in 2015 with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in [[political science]]. Abram is also a former model.<ref name="Ghost Vintage">{{cite news |last1=Tran |first1=Jess |date=July 6, 2018 |title=Cleo Abram |url=https://www.ghostvintage.com/profiles/2018/7/6/cleo-abram |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220112205024/https://www.ghostvintage.com/profiles/2018/7/6/cleo-abram |archive-date=2022-01-12 |access-date=12 January 2022 |work=Ghost Vintage}}</ref>

==Career==
Abram founded the newsletter "The Short Version", which examines arguments on opposing sides of current issues.<ref name="Ghost Vintage" /> She produced videos for ''[[Vox (website)|Vox]]'' about technology topics.<ref>{{Cite web |author1=Elizabeth Howell |date=October 7, 2019 |title='Glad You Asked': New Web Series Tackles Mars Terraforming (Exclusive Clip) |url=https://www.space.com/terraform-mars-vox-youtube-series.html |website=Space.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kugler |first1=Matthew B |last2=Pace |first2=Carly |year=2021 |title=Deepfake Privacy: Attitudes And Regulation |journal=[[Northwestern University Law Review]] |volume=116 |issue=3 |page=611-612 |issn=0029-3571 |id={{EBSCOhost|153720297}}}}</ref> She hosted the [[Vox Media Studios]] and [[YouTube Originals]] series ''Glad You Asked'',<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 8, 2019 |title=Extra: Vox, YouTube prep "Glad You Asked"; DRG inks deals Down Under |url=https://realscreen.com/2019/10/08/extra-vox-youtube-prep-glad-you-asked-drg-inks-deals-down-under/ |access-date=12 January 2022 |work=[[RealScreen]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=LaMagdeleine |first=Izz Scott |date=May 12, 2023 |title=Did Wright Brothers Fly Same Year NYT Said Flying Machines Could Take 10M Years To Develop? |url=https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/wright-brothers-first-flight/ |website=Snopes}}</ref> which was nominated for an [[Emmy Award]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite press release |title=Vox and Vox Media Studios' Emmy-Nominated Series "Glad You Asked" Returns to YouTube with Five New Episodes |date=28 July 2021 |publisher=[[Vox Media]] |url=https://www.voxmedia.com/2021/7/28/22597893/vox-and-vox-media-studios-emmy-nominated-series-glad-you-asked-returns-to-youtube-with-new-episodes |language=en |access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref> In January 2022, she left ''Vox'' to start a YouTube channel with a series titled "Huge if True" about emerging technologies.<ref name="mandhani">{{cite news |last1=Mandhani |first1=Nikita |date=15 October 2022 |title=Episode 8: Cleo Abram |url=https://videoconsortium.org/blog/episode-8-cleo-abram |access-date=8 February 2024 |work=The Video Consortium |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Can You Start a YouTube channel in 2023? With Cleo Abram |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fmIvzU115y0 |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Made on YouTube Recap |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FfJb0OpAD94 |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref>  In 2025, she was sponsored by [[Formula E]] racing to produce ''Evo Sessions'' documentaries on the science behind the competition.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleo Abram to join the NEOM McLaren Formula E Team for Formula E 'Evo Sessions' |url=https://www.mclaren.com/racing/formula-e/2025/cleo-abram-to-join-formula-e-evo-sessions/ |access-date=2025-09-04 |website=www.mclaren.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> In 2025, she signed with the [[United Talent Agency]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vlessing |first=Etan |date=2025-12-04 |title=YouTuber Cleo Abram Signs With UTA (Exclusive) |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/youtuber-cleo-abram-uta-1236442718/ |access-date=2025-12-11 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Awards and nominations==
In October 2023, MakeUseOf.com included Abram's channel in their collection of eight best explainers on Youtube.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gbenjo |first=Olasubomi |date=October 7, 2023 |title=The 8 Best YouTube Channels for Explainer Videos |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/best-youtube-channels-for-explainer-videos/ |website=MUO}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=Gularte |first=Alejandra |date=July 24, 2023 |title=Will DWTS Winner Charli D'Amelio Add a Streamy Award to Her Trophy Shelf? |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/streamy-awards-2023-nominations.html |website=Vulture}}</ref>

Abram was nominated at the [[13th Streamy Awards|13th]] [[Streamy Awards]] for "Best Collaboration", with [[MKBHD]].<ref name="auto" />

==Personal life==
Abram married Zachariah Reitano, the CEO and co-founder of the healthcare company [[Ro (company)|Ro]], in June 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cleo Abram Husband Zachariah Reitano And Their Age Gap |url=https://thefamilynation.com/cleo-abram-husband |access-date=8 February 2024 |work=thefamilynation.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Mark Rios''' (born 28 November 1987<ref>{{cite news |title=MR. Dripping, el artista de la Supercopa: "Benzema y Tom Cruise pensaban... ¡qué hace este loco!" |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/supercopa-espana/2022/01/16/61e2f80b22601d4e798b45c6.html |work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |date=16 January 2022 |language=es}}</ref> in Barcelona; professionally known as ''Mr. Dripping''<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.es/entry/mark-rios-mr-dripping_es_611d1d2ae4b0c6968103e017.html |title=Mark Ríos es Mr. Dripping |work=[[HuffPost]] |date=18 August 2021 |language=es}}</ref>) is a Spanish artist and fashion designer.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jorge Lorenzo a Dubai per relax ed eventi pubblicitari |url=https://www.corsedimoto.com/barsport/jorge-lorenzo-a-dubai-per-relax-ed-eventi-pubblicitari/ |work=Corsedimoto |date=15 January 2021 |language=it-IT}}</ref> His works have been exhibited in [[Barcelona]], [[Madrid]], [[Florence]], [[New York City|New York]], [[Miami]], and Los Angeles.<ref name="theamerican">{{cite news |title=Mr Dripping and Will Smith: A Performance Art Experience |url=https://www.theamerican.co.uk/pr/ne-Mr-Dripping-and-Will-Smith |work=www.theamerican.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Supercopa de España |url=https://trome.pe/deportes/supercopa-de-espana-el-artista-mark-rios-dibujara-el-rostro-del-hombre-del-partido-de-real-madrid-vs-athletic-club-nczd-noticia/ |work=Trome.pe |date=16 January 2022 |language=es}}</ref>

==Education==
Mark grew up in [[Barcelona, Spain]] where he studied art at the [[Frederic Mistral]] school and later enrolled in the [[ESDi School of Design]] where he directed his career towards fashion designing.<ref>{{cite web |title=Meet One Of My Favorite Artists: Mark Rios AKA Mr Dripping |url=https://www.villa88live.com/see/heres-a-look-at-one-of-my-favourite-artists-mark-rios-aka-mr-dripping/ |publisher=villa88live.com |access-date=2022-02-04 |archive-date=2022-01-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220129180956/https://www.villa88live.com/see/heres-a-look-at-one-of-my-favourite-artists-mark-rios-aka-mr-dripping/ |url-status=usurped }}</ref>

==Career==
He started his career with his own brand of clothing and bags that he was selling in multi-brand stores around the country.<ref>{{cite news |title=Artista pinta retrato ao vivo de Will Smith e filma tudo |url=https://lifestyle.sapo.pt/fama/noticias-fama/artigos/artista-pinta-retrato-ao-vivo-de-will-smith-e-filma-tudo |work=[[sapo.pt]] |language=pt}}</ref> In 2015, he took the art using dripping method as a career.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Noble |first1=Audrey |title=Go Inside Hairstylist Jennifer Yepez' Beauty Stash |url=https://www.harpersbazaar.com/beauty/hair/a25643316/jennifer-yepez-beauty-stash/ |work=[[Harper's Bazaar]] magazine |date=21 December 2018}}</ref> Dripping is a technique originally developed by [[Max Ernst]] in Germany<ref>{{cite news |title=Mr Dripping, el artista del goteo, de promoción en España |url=https://www.murcia.com/cultura/noticias/2021/08/17-mr-dripping--el-artista-del-goteo--de-promocion-en-espana.asp |work=www.murcia.com}}</ref> and later used by American artist, [[Jackson Pollock]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,808194-2,00.html |title=The Wild Ones |access-date=September 15, 2008 |magazine=Time (magazine) |date=February 20, 1956 |archive-date=May 6, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120506053634/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,808194-2,00.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> In the following year he moved to New York City and did his first show at [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] Dream Hotel featuring [[Kygo]] and a brand collaboration with [[Black Pyramid]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Los bolsos artísticos y personales de Anna Cortina |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/magazine/moda/20210103/6132325/anna-cortina-enamorada-moda-quiere-cambiar-mundo-bolsos-arte.html |work=[[La Vanguardia]] |date=3 January 2021 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Mr. Dripping; de soñar con pintura que volaba a retratar a Tom Cruise |url=https://www.diariodenavarra.es/noticias/cultura-ocio/cultura/2021/08/28/mr-dripping-sonar-pintura-volaba-retratar-tom-cruise-498766-1034.html |work=[[Diario de Navarra]] |date=28 August 2021 |language=es}}</ref>

His works have been recognized by [[Will Smith]],<ref name="theamerican"/> [[Sergio Agüero|Kun Aguero]], [[Tom Cruise]], [[Sebastián Yatra]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Mark Ríos (Mr. Dripping), el artista del momento del que todos hablan |url=https://www.hoymagazine.es/mark-rios-mr-dripping-el-artista-del-momento-del-que-todos-hablan/ |work=hoymagazine.es}}</ref> [[Antonio Banderas]], [[Sara Sampaio]], [[Marc-André ter Stegen]], [[Paul Pogba]], [[Luka Modrić]], [[Chris Brown]], [[Neymar|Neymar Jr]], [[Major Lazer]], [[Nyjah Huston]], [[Sara Sampaio]], Cindy Kimberly, [[Nieves Álvarez]], [[Sergio Agüero]], [[Karim Benzema]], [[Antonio Banderas]], [[Thomas Pieters]], [[Dean and Dan Caten|Dsquared]], [[Tom Cruise]], [[Sebastián Yatra]], [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi Hernandez]] etc.<ref>{{cite news |title=ME artist in residence Mr Dripping dedicates work to Angelina Jolie with help from OPA! restaurant |url=https://www.commercialinteriordesign.com/people/50127-me-artist-in-residence-mr-dripping-dedicates-masterpiece-to-angelina-jolie-with-help-from-opa-restaurant?amp |work=CommercialInteriorDesign.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=ME Dubai welcomes its first Artist in Residence, cultural superstar, Mr Dripping |url=https://www.lofficielarabia.com/art/me-dubai-welcomes-its-first-artist-in-residence-cultural-superstar-mr-dripping |work=[[L'Officiel]] (magazine) |language=en |archive-date=2022-01-29 |access-date=2022-02-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220129153506/https://www.lofficielarabia.com/art/me-dubai-welcomes-its-first-artist-in-residence-cultural-superstar-mr-dripping |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In December 2017, he exhibited his works in Miami and did a live performance with [[Major Lazer]] in the week of [[Art Basel]].<ref>{{cite news |title=NY 2021: UAE says Happy New Year 2021 with 33 fireworks shows |url=https://www.khaleejtimes.com/new-year-2021/ny-2021-uae-says-happy-new-year-2021-with-33-fireworks-shows |work=Khaleej Times |language=en}}</ref>

In 2022, Mark Rios participated in the [[United Tournament|super cup]] by creating an art work for the MVP. [[Karim Benzema]] received an artwork after he was named ''[[Player of the match|Man of the Match]]'' in the 2022 [[Spanish Super Cup|Spanish super cup]] semi-finals. [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] beat [[FC Barcelona]] 3-2 in the 2022 Spanish Super Cup semi-finals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Benzema receives personalised MVP artwork |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/onefootball/video/2022/01/13/benzema-receives-personalised-mvp-artwork |work=si.com |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2019–2023: Career beginnings ===
She played Maurice alongside [[Mia Wasikowska]] and [[Eliza Scanlen]] in the [[Sydney Theatre Company]]'s 2019 production of ''Lord of the Flies'' at the [[Roslyn Packer Theatre]].<ref name=fly>{{Cite journal|author= Rosie Niven |url=
https://www.theatretravels.org/post/review-lord-of-the-flies-at-sydney-theatre-company |title= REVIEW: Lord of the Flies at Sydney Theatre Company |website= theatretravels.org |date=7 August 2019}}</ref> She made her television debut with a recurring role in the American-French series ''[[Reef Break]]''.<ref name=tv>{{Cite web|url= https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/yerin-ha/credits/3000867063/ |title= Yerin Ha Credits |work= tvguide.com |access-date= 25 January 2024}}</ref>

Also in 2019, it was announced that Ha had been cast in the [[Steven Spielberg]]-produced television adaptation of the video game ''[[Halo (TV series)|Halo]]'',<ref name=tv/> in which she would portray a new character, Kwan Ha.<ref name=ha>{{Cite web|url=https://if.com.au/yerin-ha-lands-a-breakthrough-role-in-spielberg-produced-series/|title=Yerin Ha lands a breakthrough role in Spielberg-produced series|website=If|first=Don|last=Groves|date=18 April 2019|accessdate=25 March 2022}}</ref> The series premiered on [[Paramount+]] in 2022.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/lifestyle/stellar/aussie-actors-huge-role-in-spielberg-series/news-story/f5cbccba1a2df31974cd172294d24b68|title=Aussie actor's huge role in Spielberg series|journal=Daily Telegraph|date=12 March 2022|accessdate=25 March 2022}}{{subscription required}}</ref>

Ha was named a rising star by the [[Casting Guild of Australia]] in November 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://tvtonight.com.au/2021/11/casting-guild-of-australia-rising-stars-of-2021.html|title=Casting Guild of Australia: Rising Stars of 2021|website=TV Tonight|first=David|last=Knox|date=10 November 2021|accessdate=25 March 2022}}</ref> She was billed in the main cast of the [[ABC TV (Australian TV channel)|ABC TV]] series ''[[Troppo (TV series)|Troppo]]'' as Ah Rah, and made her feature film debut in ''[[Sissy (film)|Sissy]]''.<ref name=tv/> The latter premiered at the 2022 [[South by Southwest]] (SXSW) festival.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://about.abc.net.au/media-room/action-called-on-new-crime-series-troppo/|title=Action called on new crime series Troppo|website=ABC|date=12 August 2021|accessdate=15 March 2022}}</ref>

[[File:Yerin Ha - Logies 2023.jpg|thumb|Ha at the [[Logie Awards of 2023|63rd Logie Awards]] in 2023]]

[[Joey Mercury]] |debut = 2017 |retired = |education = [[Luther College (Iowa)|Luther College]] }} '''Jasper Kange''' is an American [[professional wrestler]], better known by the [[ring name]] '''Bishop Kaun''' or '''Kaun'''. He is signed to [[All Elite Wrestling]] (AEW) and its sister promotion [[Ring of Honor]] (ROH), where he is a member of The Demand stable and one-half of the tag team [[Gates of Agony]] (GOA). He is a former [[AEW World Trios Championship|AEW World Trios Champion]] (with stablemates [[Ricochet (wrestler)|Ricochet]] and [[Toa Liona]]). == Early life == Kange attended the [[University of Minnesota]] before transferring to [[Luther College (Iowa)|Luther College]], where he majored in art and played [[American football|football]] for the [[Luther Norse football|Luther Norse]]. After graduating, he worked in art and design before deciding to become a professional wrestler after moving to [[Baltimore]]. == Professional wrestling career == === Early career (2017–2018) === Kaun was trained at the [[Maryland Championship Wrestling]] [[professional wrestling school]], debuting in 2017. He spent the early years of his career primarily wrestling for Maryland Championship Wrestling, where he won the MCW Tag Team Championship with Malcolm Moses. === Ring of Honor / All Elite Wrestling (2018–present) === ==== Shane Taylor Promotions (2018–2021) ==== {{see also|Shane Taylor Promotions|}} Kaun debuted in [[Ring of Honor]] (ROH) in 2018, teaming with Moses as the Soldiers of Savagery. In 2021, he and Moses formed the [[stable (professional wrestling)|stable]] [[Shane Taylor Promotions]] with [[Shane Taylor (wrestler)|Shane Taylor]].{{Cite web |last=LAMBERT |first=JEREMY |title=New ROH Six-Man Tag Team Champions Crowned |url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/new-roh-six-man-tag-team-champions-crowned%3famp |access-date=February 22, 2021 |website=Fightful.com}} In February 2021, the trio defeated MexiSquad to win the [[ROH World Six-Man Tag Team Championship]]. They held the title until [[Final Battle (2021)|Final Battle]] in December 2021 when they lost to the Righteous. ==== Gates of Agony / GOA (2022–present) ==== {{Main|Gates of Agony}} Following Final Battle, ROH was put on hiatus until April 2022 by new owner [[Tony Khan]]. In December 2021, Kaun began also wrestling for ROH's sister promotion [[All Elite Wrestling]]. On April 1, 2022, on [[Supercard of Honor XV]], [[Tully Blanchard]] announced that Kaun would be part of his [[Tully Blanchard Enterprises]] stable, alongside [[Toa Liona]] and [[Brian Cage]]. The duo of Kaun and Liona were named the "[[Gates of Agony]]". In July 2022 at [[Death Before Dishonor (2022)|Death Before Dishonor]], [[Prince Nana]] announced he had purchased Tully Blanchard Enterprises and reformed [[The Embassy (professional wrestling)|The Embassy]], with Cage, Kaun and Liona. At [[Battle of the Belts IV]] in October 2022, Kaun and Liona unsuccessfully challenged [[FTR (professional wrestling)|FTR]] for the [[ROH World Tag Team Championship]]. At [[Final Battle (2022)|Final Battle]] in December 2022, the Gates of Agony defeated [[Dalton Castle (wrestler)|Dalton Castle]] and [[Tate Twins|The Boys]] to win the [[ROH World Six-Man Tag Team Championship]]. At ''[[Rampage: Grand Slam]]'' in September 2023, the Gates of Agony lost the ROH World Six-Man Tag Team Championship to [[The Elite (professional wrestling)|The Elite]]. On November 1, 2023 on ''[[AEW Dynamite]]'', the Gates of Agony regained the titles from The Elite. '''Zachary Miskom Bako-Bewele''' (born '''Zachary Miskom Tom''', March 26, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Tackle (gridiron football)|offensive tackle]] for the [[Green Bay Packers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]] and was selected by the Packers in the fourth round of the [[2022 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Bako-Bewele was born in [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]] grew up in [[Prairieville, Louisiana]], and attended [[Catholic High School (Baton Rouge, Louisiana)|Catholic High School]] in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Duncan |first=Jeff |date=August 30, 2018 |title=Brothers Cameron, Zach Tom play simultaneously Thursday night in New Orleans |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/article_4d60b1c4-0a65-5df6-87ff-7fe2695ef2d8.html |access-date=March 26, 2023 |website=NOLA.com |language=en}}</ref> He is of Nigerian descent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/green-bay-packers-ad3e11b5cdf1697a6683cfe237ad43d0|title=Packers offensive tackle changing his name from Zach Tom to Zach Bako-Bewele|date=August 3, 2026|website=AP News}}</ref>

==College career==
Bako-Bewele was a member of the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]] for five seasons and [[redshirted]] his true freshman season. He became the team's starting center going into his redshirt sophomore season and was named honorable mention All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) after starting all 13 of Wake Forest's games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Neill |first=Conor |date=February 29, 2020 |title=Zach Tom becomes linchpin of Beef Boys because of experience and versatility |url=https://journalnow.com/sports/college/wfu/zach-tom-becomes-linchpin-of-beef-boys-because-of-experience-and-versatility/article_67041761-c6c9-5615-aae1-5b47cbbe3fd9.html |access-date=March 26, 2023 |website=[[Winston-Salem Journal]]}}</ref> Bako-Bewele moved to left tackle the following season and started nine games. He was named first-team All-ACC in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dell |first=John |date=March 30, 2022 |title=Zach Tom of Wake Forest doing all the right things in pursuit of his NFL dream |url=https://journalnow.com/sports/college/wfu/zach-tom-of-wake-forest-doing-all-the-right-things-in-pursuit-of-his-nfl/article_9afc2634-b06f-11ec-bd86-4b544a73cea0.html |access-date=March 26, 2023 |website=[[Winston-Salem Journal]]}}</ref>

Bako-Bewele was drafted by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the fourth round (140th overall) of the [[2022 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hodkiewicz |first=Wes  |date=April 30, 2022 |title=2022 NFL Draft: Packers select Wake Forest OL Zach Tom in fourth round, No. 140 overall |url=https://www.packers.com/news/2022-nfl-draft-packers-select-wake-forest-ol-zach-tom-in-fourth-round-no-140-ove |access-date=April 30, 2022 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> He signed his four-year rookie contract on May 26, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 26, 2022 |title=Packers sign WR Romeo Doubs, OL Zach Tom |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-wr-romeo-doubs-ol-zach-tom-2022 |access-date=May 26, 2022 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> Bako-Bewele saw his first NFL action on September 11, during a Week 1 loss to the [[2022 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]], filling in at left guard after starter [[Jon Runyan Jr.]] suffered a [[Concussions in American football|concussion]] in the third quarter.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kruse |first1=Zach |title=Packers LG Jon Runyan Jr. exits Week 1 for concussion evaluation |url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/2022/09/11/packers-lg-jon-runyan-jr-exits-week-1-for-concussion-evaluation/ |work=USA Today |access-date=September 20, 2022 |date=September 11, 2022}}</ref>

In the 2023 season, Bako-Bewele became the permanent starter at right tackle for the Packers, starting all 17 games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 13, 2023 |title=With Childhood Competitive Streak, Tom Throws Block Party |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/packers/news/with-childhood-competitive-streak-tom-throws-block-party |access-date=July 21, 2025 |website=Green Bay Packers On SI |language=en-US }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Reischel |first=Rob |title=The Most Important Packers: No. 7 — Zach Tom |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/robreischel/2025/07/16/the-most-important-packers-no-7---zach-tom/ |access-date=July 21, 2025 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>

In April 2024, Bako-Bewele suffered a torn [[pectoral muscles|pectoral muscle]], causing him to miss part of Green Bay's offseason training program.<ref name="x873">{{cite web | last=Kruse | first=Zach | title=Packers TE Tucker Kraft, OL Zach Tom out until training camp with pectoral injuries | website=Packers Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=May 21, 2024 | url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/2024/05/21/packers-te-tucker-kraft-ol-zach-tom-out-until-training-camp-with-pectoral-injuries/ | access-date=December 7, 2024}}</ref> In the 2024 season, he started all 17 games and scored the sixth-highest grade (85.8) among offensive tackles in the 2024 season per [[Pro Football Focus]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zach Tom 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TomxZa00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=June 16, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyman |first=Jim |date=February 25, 2025 |title=Highest-graded offensive tackles from the 2024 NFL season |url=https://www.pff.com/news/nfl-highest-graded-offensive-tackles-2024-nfl-season |access-date=July 21, 2025 |website=PFF |language=en}}</ref>

On July 22, 2025, Bako-Bewele signed a four-year, $88 million contract extension, including a $30.2 million signing bonus. At the time of signing, the bonus was the largest for an offensive lineman in league history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Packers, Zach Tom agree to four-year, $88 million extension; OT earns historic signing bonus |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/packers-zach-tom-agrees-to-four-year-88-million-extension-ot-earns-historic-signing-bonus |access-date=July 21, 2025 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on September 28, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Packers sign G Laken Tomlinson|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-g-laken-tomlinson-sept-28-2026|access-date=September 28, 2025 |website=packers.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bako-Bewele's older brother, [[Cameron Tom]], was also an offensive linemen in the NFL and went to college at [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles football|The University of Southern Mississippi]].

On August 2, 2026, he officially announced that he was changing his last name from "Tom" to "Bako-Bewele," a combination of his paternal grandparents' Nigerian last names. Tom is his father's [[surname]], but his paternal grandfather's [[given name]].<ref>{{Cite web|title= Zach Tom Changes Name to Zach Bako-Bewele|url= https://cheeseheadtv.com/blog/packers-zach-tom-changes-name-to-zach-bako-bewele-722|access-date=2026-08-02|website=CheeseheadTV}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/packers/2026/08/02/zach-tom-new-last-name-packers-bako-bewele/91142233007/|title=Packers offensive lineman is changing his last name. Here's why|work=USA Today|date=August 2, 2026}}</ref>
