'''María Peláez Sánchez'''<ref>{{Cite news |title=Alsondelpez gana el 25º Certamen Andaluz de Canción de Autor |url=https://elpais.com/ccaa/2012/07/28/andalucia/1343494418_378777.html |date=28 July 2012 |newspaper=El País|language=es|last=Donaire |first=Ginés}} </ref> (born 31 March 1990), known professionally as '''María Peláe''', is a Spanish singer and composer. She has released two albums, entitled ''Hipocondría'' and ''La folcrónica''. She participated as a contestant in the ninth edition of [[Antena 3 (Spanish TV channel)|Antena 3]]'s ''[[Tu cara me suena (Spanish TV series)|Tu cara me suena]]'' (2021–2022), finishing third.<ref name="Antena 3">{{Cite web |title=María Peláe, tercera clasificada en la Gran Final: "En ningún momento ha habido competición ni competencia alguna" |url=https://www.antena3.com/programas/tu-cara-me-suena/temporada-9/noticias/maria-pelae-tercera-clasificada-gran-final-ningun-momento-habido-competicion-competencia-alguna_202203056222b37af6355200014ad9a1.html|date=5 March 2022 |website=Antena3|language=es}}</ref> Her music is a mix of flamenco and pop rhythms, and the words to her songs are often humorous and critical of society. <ref name="El mundo">{{Cite web |title=Quién es María Peláe, la invitada en El Hormiguero que cambió su apellido |url=https://www.elmundo.es/television/2021/10/28/617af310fc6c83f7078b45e2.html |date=29 October 2021 |website=ElMundo|language=es}} </ref>

== Life and career ==
She was born in [[Málaga]] on 31 March 1990. At the age of 13, she was given a guitar, and at 16, she gave her first concert as a percussionist. At the age of 18, shortly before entering medical school, she gave her first concert as a soloist (guitar and voice). She felt so strongly about it that she decided to study something that would allow her to combine it with music, which led her to choose social work and, later, anthropology.

In 2016, she released her first studio album, ''Hipocondría'', thanks to a crowdfunding campaign and with it she toured a multitude of venues in various Spanish cities, such as Café Berlin in Madrid or Cochera Cabaret in Málaga.<ref>{{Cite web |title=¿Quién es María Peláe, concursante de 'Tu cara me suena 9'? |url=https://www.elconfidencial.com/television/programas-tv/2021-11-05/quien-es-maria-pelae-concursante-tu-cara-me-suena_3314596/ |date=5 November 2021 |website=ElConfidencial|language=es}}</ref>

She has composed two songs that were finalists to represent Spain at [[Eurovision Song Contest|Eurovision]]: "Arde", sung by Aitana (composed with Alba Reig from [[Sweet California]])<ref>{{Cite web |title=¿Quién es María Peláe, concursante de 'Tu cara me suena 9'? |url=https://www.elconfidencial.com/television/programas-tv/2021-11-05/quien-es-maria-pelae-concursante-tu-cara-me-suena_3314596/ |date=20 March 2022 |website=ElConfidencial|language=es}}</ref> and "Nadie se salva" (with Nil Moliner and [[Garabato (band)|Garabato]]), performed by [[Miki Núñez]] and Natalia Lancuza. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Quién es María Peláe: su música, su novia y su verdadero apellido |url=https://www.europafm.com/noticias/famosos/quien-maria-pelae-musica-novia-verdadero-apellido_20211028617af12834d4be00018ce53d.html |date=28 October 2021 |website=EuropaFM|language=es}}</ref> From 2019, after delaying the start of her new project due to last minute changes, she began to upload to her Youtube channel a series of songs that denoted a change towards a more modern production (a change recommended by Alba Reig of Sweet California).

The first single from this new stage, released in July 2019, was En casa de herrero (talking about the music industry and the artist's own change of sound),<ref>{{Cite web |title=María Peláe: '¿Mi objetivo? Destapar la doble moral y pasármelo bien' |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/cultura/musica/20210508/7437421/maria-pelae-entrevista-concierto-barts-doble-moral.html |date=8 May 2021 |website=LaVanguardia|language=es}}</ref> and in September of that same year she released ''La niña'' (dealing with female homosexuality using irony and with autobiographical overtones).

''La niña'' followed by ''Y quién no'', ''No me mires así'', sung with Alba Reig and whose video clip was recorded during the quarantine derived from the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], ''La confesión'', ''La quería''  with Riki Rivera on guitar, ''Te espero en jarra'' with the singer Sandra Carrasco, and ''Mi tío Juan'' (in which she talks about male homosexuality with a lot of irony).<ref>{{Cite web |title=María Peláe:En mi cabeza cumplí los 84 hace meses" |url=https://www.diariodesevilla.es/entrevistas/Maria-Pelae-Cantante_0_1590741976.html|date=1 August 2021 |website=Diario de Sevilla|language=es}}</ref> Later, she released ''Que vengan a por mí'', a more serious song she composed after "seeing a demonstration of very young people with a lot of hate in their eyes, attacking and saying very ugly things to people who were demonstrating for something nice," as she said in an interview on the [[Antena 3 (Spanish TV channel)|Antena 3]] program [[El Hormiguero]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=El tropezón, literal, de Pablo Motos con María Peláe en 'El hormiguero'" |url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/television/20211028/7824530/maria-pelae-el-hormiguero-cantante-concursante-tu-cara-me-suena.html |date=28 October 2021 |website=LaVanguardia |language=es}}</ref>

In 2023, she was a guest celebrity judge in the episode ''¡Un, dos, drags!'' of the Spanish language reality television series ''[[Drag Race España]]'' streamed on [[ATRESplayer Premium]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 2, 2023 |title=Las reinas de 'Drag Race España' participarán en la versión drag del mítico 'Un, dos, tres'|url=https://premium.atresplayer.com/drag-race/noticias/reinas-participaran-version-drag-mitico-dos-tres_202306026479f9b845377c00016eb025.html|access-date=2023-06-06 
|website=[[ATRESplayer Premium]] |language=Spanish |archive-date=2023-03-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331210154/https://premium.atresplayer.com/drag-race/noticias/reinas-participaran-version-drag-mitico-dos-tres_202306026479f9b845377c00016eb025.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

Peláez competed in [[Benidorm Fest 2024]], the Spanish selection for the [[Eurovision Song Contest 2024]], with the song "Remitente".<ref>{{cite web|last=Solano|first=Cristhian|url=https://www.escplus.es/benidorm-fest/2023/minuto-a-minuto-presentacion-de-participantes-del-benidorm-fest-2024/|title=Minuto a minuto: presentación de participantes del Benidorm Fest 2024|trans-title=Minute by minute: presentation of Benidorm Fest 2024 participants|language=es-ES|work=ESCplus España|date=2023-11-11|access-date=2023-11-11}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Mancheño|first=José Miguel|url=https://www.escplus.es/benidorm-fest/2023/conoce-los-titulos-de-las-16-canciones-del-benidorm-fest-2024/|title=Conoce los títulos de las 16 canciones del Benidorm Fest 2024|trans-title=Know the titles of the 16 songs of Benidorm Fest 2024|work=ESCplus España|language=es-ES|date=2023-12-07|access-date=2023-12-07}}</ref> She came second in her semi-final on 1 February 2024, qualifying for the final,<ref>{{cite web|last=Canto|first=Jesús|url=https://www.escplus.es/benidorm-fest/2024/elegidos-los-ultimos-cuatro-finalistas-del-benidorm-fest-2024/|title=Elegidos los últimos cuatro finalistas del Benidorm Fest 2024|trans-title=The last four finalists of Benidorm Fest 2024 have been selected|language=es-ES|work=ESCplus España|date=2024-02-02|access-date=2024-02-02}}</ref> where she finished sixth.<ref>{{cite web|last=Canto |first=Jesús |url=https://www.escplus.es/benidorm-fest/2024/nebulossa-con-zorra-gana-el-benidorm-fest-2024-y-representara-a-espana-en-el-festival-de-eurovision/ |title=Nebulossa con «Zorra» gana el Benidorm Fest 2024 y representará a España en el Festival de Eurovisión |trans-title=Nebulossa with "Zorra" wins Benidorm Fest 2024 and will represent Spain in the Eurovision Song Contest |language=es-es |website=ESCplus España |date=2024-02-03 |access-date=2024-02-04}}</ref>

=== ''Tu cara me suena'' ===
On 23 July 2021, her official participation as a contestant in the ninth edition of [[Antena 3 (Spanish TV channel)|Antena 3]]'s ''[[Tu cara me suena (Spanish TV series)|Tu cara me suena]]'' was confirmed,<ref>{{Cite web |last=antena3 |date=23 July 2021 |title=Agoney, concursante confirmado para la novena edición de 'Tu cara me suena' El cantante ya tiene experiencia en el concurso. |url=https://www.antena3.com/programas/tu-cara-me-suena/noticias/agoney-concursante-confirmado-novena-edicion_2021072360faa30939fa6f00018ed145.html/ |website=Antena3 |language=es}}</ref> alongside personalities such as Los Morancos, [[Lydia Bosch]], [[Loles León]], Eva Soriano, David Fernández, [[Rasel (singer)|Rasel Abad]], Nia Correia and [[Agoney]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 July 2021 |title=Tu Cara Me Suena 9: Estos son todos los concursantes confirmados del talent show de Antena 3 Nia, Rasel, Eva Soriano y María Peláe se unen a Los Morancos, Agoney, Loles León, David Fernández y Lydia Bosch |url=https://los40.com/los40/2021/07/30/cinetv/1627654230_977944.html/ |website=Los40 |language=es |access-date=10 June 2022 |archive-date=8 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211108235452/https://los40.com/los40/2021/07/30/cinetv/1627654230_977944.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

She became the second finalist after her imitation of [[Barbara Pravi]],  [[France in the Eurovision Song Contest 2021|the French representative in the Eurovision Song Contest 2021]]. She came in third place with her imitation of [[Lola Flores]], whom she has cited on multiple occasions as a reference, and was one of the favorites throughout the edition.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 March 2022 |title=María Peláe, finalista de Tu cara me suena: "El porno lésbico está hecho para hombres" |url=https://www.elmundo.es/loc/2022/03/08/6225ee2efc6c83ac6a8b4571.html/|website=ElMundo|language=es}}</ref>

Peláez is openly [[lesbian]] and has used her songs and appearances on TV and in the press to bring more attention to the [[LGBT rights in Spain|LGBT+ community]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 March 2022 |title=María Peláe es 'La folcrónica': "Si mi pareja es una mujer, ¿por qué no voy a decirlo?" |url=https://shangay.com/2022/03/16/maria-pelae-folcronica-lgtbi-cara-me-suena-entrevista/ |website=ShanGay|language=es}}</ref>

'''Ronald Merle McNutt''' ({{start date|1987|05|23}} – {{start date|2020|08|31}}) was an American [[United States Army Reserve|US Army Reserve]] veteran from [[New Albany, Mississippi]], who on August 31, 2020, [[Commit Suicide|committed suicide]] during a [[Facebook]] [[Live streaming|livestream]]. The clip of McNutt's suicide spread virally across [[social media]] sites, which led to discussions on [[suicide and the Internet]] and if social media platforms have a [[legal liability|legal obligation]] to remove graphic and disturbing footage.

== Life and career ==
Born on May 23, 1987, in the community of [[Alcorn, Mississippi]], McNutt was a resident of [[New Albany, Mississippi|New Albany]], Mississippi, and had served in the [[United States Army Reserve]], including in [[Iraq]]. He worked at a [[Toyota]] plant. He had a variety of mental health problems, such as [[Major depressive disorder|depression]] as well as [[post-traumatic stress disorder]] (PTSD), the latter of which was a direct consequence of his time served in the [[Iraq War]] in 2007 and 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kitching |first=Chris |date=2020-09-14 |title=Tragic story of Ronnie McNutt who killed himself on Facebook live stream |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/us-news/ronnie-mcnutt-tragic-story-man-22665676 |access-date=2023-01-02 |website=Mirror |language=en |archive-date=December 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20201201002234/https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/us-news/ronnie-mcnutt-tragic-story-man-22665676 |url-status=live }}</ref> Some reports also said that he lost his job during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], though ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' disputed this.<ref name="Dickson">{{cite web |last1=Dickson |first1=EJ |date=September 9, 2020 |title=Why Did Facebook Keep a Man's Livestreamed Suicide Up for Hours? |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-news/facebook-tiktok-livestream-suicide-1056959/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123163911/https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/culture-news/facebook-tiktok-livestream-suicide-1056959/ |archive-date=November 23, 2023 |access-date=March 24, 2022 |website=www.rollingstone.com |publisher=[[Rolling Stone]]}}</ref> McNutt was a [[Christianity|Christian]] who regularly attended church.<ref name=":3">{{cite web |last1=Steinbuch |first1=Yaron |title=Army veteran Ronnie McNutt commits suicide in Facebook livestream |url=https://nypost.com/2020/09/08/army-veteran-kills-himself-in-facebook-livestream/ |website=nypost.com |date=September 9, 2020 |publisher=New York Post |access-date=March 24, 2022 |archive-date=January 9, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240109191351/https://nypost.com/2020/09/08/army-veteran-kills-himself-in-facebook-livestream/ |url-status=live }}</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=September 2026}}<ref name=":1">{{cite news |last1=Wakefield |first1=Jane |title=Friend challenges Facebook over Ronnie McNutt suicide video |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-54176205 |website=www.bbc.com |date=September 19, 2020 |publisher=BBC News |access-date=March 24, 2022 |archive-date=February 13, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240213224145/https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-54176205 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Suicide ==
On August 31, 2020, McNutt began a [[Live streaming|livestream]] on [[List of Facebook features#Live streaming|Facebook Live]]. His best friend, Joshua Steen, noticed the stream. He told ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' that McNutt "often used a livestreaming platform as his form of therapy", regularly conversing with viewers on various topics; but he noticed almost immediately that this particular livestream was "different" from the others, as McNutt "appeared to be heavily inebriated and despondent", and appeared to [[Negligent discharge|misfire]] a [[rifle]] into the air at one point.<ref name = Dickson/> Steen claimed that he attempted to intervene numerous times – particularly when McNutt misfired the rifle – hoping that Facebook would cut off the stream and end the video feed, preventing people from seeing into McNutt's home while Steen sought police intervention. Facebook refused to cut the stream, claiming that the stream was not in any violation of its platform's guidelines, as McNutt had not yet killed himself.<ref name=":0" />

As the stream went on, McNutt's cell phone rang frequently. The last call he received was from his girlfriend, which he answered, leading to a brief argument between the two. After she ended the call, McNutt took hold of the gun and addressed the audience for the final time, saying his last words: "Hey guys, I guess that's it." He then aimed the rifle under his chin and [[Suicide methods#Shooting|fatally shot himself]].<ref name="Ronnie McNutt: A Heartbreaking Suicide Story That Echoes Veteran Struggles">{{cite news |title=Ronnie McNutt: A Heartbreaking Suicide Story That Echoes Veteran Struggles|publisher=Vibro Media |url=https://vibromedia.com/ronnie-mcnutt/ |access-date=February 23, 2026}}</ref> About a second before his suicide, the phone he had left on his desk began to ring again. The stream was captured by multiple viewers.<ref>{{cite web |last1=LeMaster |first1=C.J. |title=Criticism lobbed at social media companies after suicide video of Mississippi man goes viral |url=https://www.wdam.com/2020/09/09/criticism-lobbed-social-media-companies-after-suicide-video-mississippi-man-goes-viral/ |website=www.wdam.com |date=September 10, 2020 |publisher=WDAM7 News |access-date=March 24, 2022 |archive-date=October 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231003004651/https://www.wdam.com/2020/09/09/criticism-lobbed-social-media-companies-after-suicide-video-mississippi-man-goes-viral/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The New Albany Police Department had been called to the scene during the livestream, but did not enter McNutt's apartment until after they heard the fatal gunshot; his phone was still ringing as officers searched the scene. Police Chief Chris Robertson reported that his officers had secured the perimeter and evacuated nearby residents before attempting to communicate with McNutt via speakerphone, to no avail. Robertson concluded that McNutt was "in such a mental state nobody could've gotten through to him".<ref name=":2">{{cite web |last1=McEvoy |first1=Jemima |title=Friend Of Ronnie McNutt, Whose Livestreamed Suicide Went Viral, Says Facebook Could've Stopped It |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jemimamcevoy/2020/09/09/friend-of-ronnie-mcnutt-whose-livestreamed-suicide-went-viral-says-facebook-couldve-stopped-it/ |work=[[Forbes]] |access-date=March 24, 2022 |archive-date=March 25, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220325003540/https://www.forbes.com/sites/jemimamcevoy/2020/09/09/friend-of-ronnie-mcnutt-whose-livestreamed-suicide-went-viral-says-facebook-couldve-stopped-it/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

McNutt made a final post on Facebook shortly before starting the livestream. It read, "Someone in your life needs to hear that they matter. That they are loved. That they have a future. Be the one to tell them."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Steinbuch |first1=Yaron |title=Army veteran Ronnie McNutt shared final heartbreaking message before suicide |url=https://nypost.com/2020/09/09/ronnie-mcnutt-shared-heartbreaking-message-before-suicide/ |website=[[New York Post]] |date=September 9, 2020 |access-date=March 25, 2022 |archive-date=October 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231027172235/https://nypost.com/2020/09/09/ronnie-mcnutt-shared-heartbreaking-message-before-suicide/ |url-status=live}}</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=September 2026}} Two days after his suicide, McNutt was buried in Snowdown Church of Christ Cemetery in [[Prentiss County, Mississippi]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McMillen |first=Lynn |date=2020-09-02 |title=Ronald 'Ronnie' Merle McNutt |url=http://quadcitiesdaily.com/?p=611074 |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=Quad-Cities Daily |language=en-US |archive-date=April 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406155015/http://quadcitiesdaily.com/?p=611074 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Aftermath ==
=== Viral spread ===
[[Screencast]]s and downloads of the livestream were posted online, beginning its proliferation on the web. The video of McNutt's suicide was posted by users across social media platforms such as Facebook, [[YouTube]], [[TikTok]], and [[Instagram]], often in the form of [[bait-and-switch]] content which would unexpectedly display the video alongside innocuous content. Variants of the video appeared in TikTok's "For you" page, so that users would scroll upon it without warning as the suicide automatically played, [[Shock site|with the apparent intention of frightening or upsetting viewers]] as a form of [[Troll (slang)|trolling]]. The #ronniemcnutt [[hashtag]] had 15.6 million views on TikTok within the first few days after the suicide.<ref name="Refinery29">{{cite web |last1=Cortés |first1=Michelle Santiago |title=Let's Talk About The Graphic Video Going Viral On TikTok |url=https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/2020/09/10012185/tiktok-suicide-video-reactions |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209210122/https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/2020/09/10012185/tiktok-suicide-video-reactions |archive-date=December 9, 2023 |access-date=March 24, 2022 |publisher=Refinery29}}</ref>

According to ''[[Heavy (website)|Heavy]]'', Facebook also initially refused to prevent the spread of recorded video of McNutt's misfire and suicide, but later agreed to remove the videos from its platform.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Warnock |first=Caroline |date=2020-09-10 |title=Ronnie McNutt's Friend Says Facebook Didn't Do Enough to Stop Suicide Livestream |url=https://heavy.com/news/2020/09/ronnie-mcnutt-facebook-video/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231215142017/https://heavy.com/news/2020/09/ronnie-mcnutt-facebook-video/ |archive-date=December 15, 2023 |access-date=2023-01-02 |website=Heavy.com |language=en-US}}</ref> McNutt had not expressed any intent for the viral spread to occur; Steen said that he did not think McNutt started livestreaming with the intention of killing himself, adding: "When you go back and follow his digital trail there is this beautiful telling of his life on various social-media platforms. He had a history of getting on a streaming service and talking."<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> 

Though the platforms worked to remove the videos, new uploads of it would appear from separate accounts, while links to the video also began to appear in [[Reddit]]'s [[true crime]] communities. As TikTok's moderation became aware of the video with its [[algorithm]]s, uploaders evaded detection by placing the video after unrelated, innocuous imagery.<ref>{{cite web |last1=O'Hanlon |first1=Aengus |title=Parents warning as distressing suicide video being 'disguised' and circulated on TikTok |url=https://www.corkbeo.ie/news/parents-warning-distressing-suicide-video-18903050 |website=www.corkbeo.ie |date=September 9, 2020 |publisher=CorkBeo |access-date=March 24, 2022 |archive-date=October 26, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201026222422/https://www.corkbeo.ie/news/parents-warning-distressing-suicide-video-18903050 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Dawson |first1=Brit |title=Why can't TikTok take down that disturbing suicide video? |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/science-tech/article/50382/1/why-cant-tiktok-take-down-that-disturbing-suicide-video |website=www.dazeddigital.com |date=September 9, 2020 |publisher=Dazed |access-date=March 24, 2022 |archive-date=September 10, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200910225021/https://www.dazeddigital.com/science-tech/article/50382/1/why-cant-tiktok-take-down-that-disturbing-suicide-video |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Public response ===
The incident was compared to the filmed suicides of television news reporter [[Christine Chubbuck]] and treasurer of Pennsylvania [[R. Budd Dwyer|R.{{nbs}}Budd Dwyer]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ep. 3: The public suicide squad |url=https://www.listennotes.com/podcasts/jack-of-all-graves/ep-3-the-public-suicide-squad-o5dOSIwMu8x/ |website=www.listennotes.com |date=September 13, 2020 |publisher=Jack of All Graves |access-date=March 25, 2022}}</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=September 2026}} A large margin of the response online was one of sympathy towards McNutt, with users using the case as an opportunity to discuss [[mental health]] and [[suicide prevention]], as well as concern over the video's prevalence online. Some [[TikTok]] users announced [[boycott]]s of the platform until the suicide video was completely taken down, while other users began posting prayers and messages of respect and commemoration for McNutt in the comments sections of the video uploads.<ref name="Refinery29"/><ref>{{cite web |last1=MacDonald |first1=Cheyenne |title=Sharing a video of a person's suicide doesn't make you edgy. It makes you a POS. |url=https://www.inputmag.com/culture/sharing-a-video-of-a-persons-ronnie-mcnutt-suicide-on-facebook-live-doesnt-make-you-edgy-it-makes-you-a-pos |magazine=Input |date=September 7, 2020  |access-date=March 25, 2022 |archive-date=October 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201001124402/https://www.inputmag.com/culture/sharing-a-video-of-a-persons-ronnie-mcnutt-suicide-on-facebook-live-doesnt-make-you-edgy-it-makes-you-a-pos |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Lewis |first1=Rachel Charlene |title=Very OnlineYou Can't Escape Death on TikTok |url=https://www.bitchmedia.org/article/tiktok-death-and-suicide-videos-trending |website=Bitch Media |access-date=March 25, 2022 |archive-date=November 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101135939/https://www.bitchmedia.org/article/tiktok-death-and-suicide-videos-trending |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Many parents reported that their children were highly distressed after encountering the video, with one girl becoming physically ill and needing to sleep with the lights on.<ref name="BBC News">{{cite news |last1=Wakefield |first1=Jane |title=TikTok tries to remove widely shared suicide clip |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-54069650 |date=September 8, 2020 |website=BBC News |access-date=March 25, 2022 |archive-date=September 8, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200908141737/https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-54069650 |url-status=live }}</ref> Another parent argued that she fears that her children, who accidentally discovered the video on TikTok, may have post-traumatic stress disorder.<ref name="Bedo">{{cite web |last1=Bedo |first1=Stephanie |title=Ronnie McNutt suicide video leaves kids traumatised after platforms struggle to remove it |url=https://www.news.com.au/technology/online/social/ronnie-mcnutt-suicide-video-leaves-kids-traumatised-after-platforms-struggle-to-remove-it/news-story/1dea8b68b23fcbdc5134e4725a607bd5 |website=www.news.com.au |access-date=March 25, 2022 |archive-date=September 8, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200908075724/https://www.news.com.au/technology/online/social/ronnie-mcnutt-suicide-video-leaves-kids-traumatised-after-platforms-struggle-to-remove-it/news-story/1dea8b68b23fcbdc5134e4725a607bd5 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Perrin |first1=Isabella |title=Bracknell parents warned over viral distressing TikTok video |url=https://www.bracknellnews.co.uk/news/18708768.bracknell-parents-warned-viral-distressing-tiktok-video/ |date=September 10, 2020 |website=Bracknell News |access-date=March 25, 2022 |archive-date=September 10, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200910125624/https://www.bracknellnews.co.uk/news/18708768.bracknell-parents-warned-viral-distressing-tiktok-video/ |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Institute of Mums'' circulated further warnings for parents about seemingly benign video content hiding the McNutt video, stating, "Alarmingly, there are also reports of the video being sandwiched in the middle of cute and funny [[Cats and the Internet|cat videos]], which begin with viewer-friendly footage before quickly changing to the disturbing suicide."<ref>{{cite web |title=Parents urged to restrict TikTok as video of man shooting himself trends |url=https://instituteofmums.com/2020/09/07/parents-urged-to-restrict-tiktok-as-video-of-man-shooting-himself-trends/ |date=September 7, 2020 |website=Institute of Mums |access-date=March 25, 2022 |archive-date=October 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201001125313/https://instituteofmums.com/2020/09/07/parents-urged-to-restrict-tiktok-as-video-of-man-shooting-himself-trends/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> The then-[[Prime Minister of Australia]] [[Scott Morrison]] referred to the video as something that "no child should be exposed to", while [[Computer security|cybersecurity]] expert Susan McLean publicly recommended that parents prevent minor children from accessing the TikTok app until the video was fully removed.<ref name="Bedo"/>

===Liability===
The case sparked a debate over what [[legal liability]] is owed by Internet platforms that fail to promptly remove graphic and disturbing footage from public view, with the blame generally being placed on Facebook for failing to cut off the livestream during the initial suicide attempt. Joshua Steen, and many of McNutt's other friends, say they had reported the livestream to Facebook "hundreds" of times prior to McNutt's death;<ref name=":2" /> Steen had also called Facebook multiple times, and had called the police, neither of which stopped the stream before McNutt killed himself.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Feis |first1=Aaron |title=Facebook, other sites scrambling to remove video of Ronnie McNutt suicide |url=https://nypost.com/2020/09/08/facebook-scramble-to-remove-video-of-ronnie-mcnutt-suicide/ |website=nypost.com |date=September 8, 2020 |publisher=New York Post |access-date=March 25, 2022 |archive-date=September 10, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200910142414/https://nypost.com/2020/09/08/facebook-scramble-to-remove-video-of-ronnie-mcnutt-suicide/ |url-status=live }}</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=September 2026}} Steen declared, "if some woman posts a [[Nude photography|topless photo]], their software will detect ''that'', remove it, and ban their account. That's apparently more offensive than my friend killing himself."<ref name="Dickson" /> Theo Bertram, TikTok's European director of public policy, stated that "a coordinated raid from the [[dark web]]" was responsible for ongoing circulation of the video.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hern |first1=Alex |title='Dark web' responsible for TikTok suicide video, says company |url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2020/sep/22/dark-web-responsible-for-tiktok-suicide-video-says-company |website=[[The Guardian]] |date=September 22, 2020 |access-date=March 25, 2022 |archive-date=September 22, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200922150802/https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2020/sep/22/dark-web-responsible-for-tiktok-suicide-video-says-company |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Lewis |first1=Sophie |title=TikTok struggles to stop the spread of viral suicide video |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/tiktok-video-suicide-man-shooting-self-struggles-remove/ |website=www.cbsnews.com |date=September 9, 2020 |publisher=CBS News |access-date=March 25, 2022 |archive-date=September 9, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200909145801/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/tiktok-video-suicide-man-shooting-self-struggles-remove/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

TikTok released a public statement saying, "Our systems have been automatically detecting and flagging these clips for violating our policies against content that displays, praises, glorifies, or promotes suicide. We appreciate our community members who've reported content and warned others against watching, engaging or sharing such videos on any platform, out of respect for the person and their family". Facebook, likewise, publicly stated, "We removed the original video from Facebook last month, on the day it was streamed, and have used automation technology to remove copies and uploads since that time. Our thoughts remain with Ronnie's family and friends during this difficult time".<ref name="BBC News"/>

'''Pável Uriel Pérez Hernández''' (born 26 June 1998) is a Mexican professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Liga MX]] club [[Toluca FC|Toluca]].

==Career==
Pérez began his career as a youth player with [[C.D. Guadalajara|Guadalajara]]. Between 2020 and 2022, he played for [[CD Toledo|Toledo]] in Spain’s [[Tercera División]], for [[Tepatitlán F.C.|Tepatitlán]] in the [[Liga de Expansión MX|Liga de Expansión]], where he helped the club win the Clausura 2021 tournament, and for [[C.D. Tapatío|Tapatío]], Guadalajara’s reserve team that also competes in the Liga de Expansión.

In December 2024, Pérez secured a permanent move to [[Club Necaxa|Necaxa]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-05 |title=Pável Pérez llega al equipo de Aguascalientes |url=http://clubnecaxa.mx/noticias/3452/Pvel-Prez-llega-al-equipo-de-Aguascalientes |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=clubnecaxa.mx |language=en}}</ref> During his time with the ''Rayos'', he achieved greater consistency, appearing in 37 official matches and scoring 6 goals.

In January 2026, he joined [[Toluca FC|Toluca]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=El bicampeón se sigue reforzando |url=https://www.tolucafc.com/noticias/el-bicampeon-se-sigue-reforzando |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=www.tolucafc.com |language=es}}</ref>

'''Nikolas Brouillard'''{{efn|{{IPA|fr|nikola bʁujaʁ}}}} (born February 7, 1995) is a Canadian professional [[ice hockey]] player who is a [[defenceman]] for the [[Djurgårdens IF (men's ice hockey)|Djurgårdens IF]] of the [[Swedish Hockey League]] (SHL).

A native of [[Quebec]], Brouillard played hockey locally in the [[Quebec Junior Hockey League]] until 2011, when he was selected by the [[Drummondville Voltigeurs]] in the 2011 [[Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League|Quebec Major Junior Hockey League]] (QMJHL) entry draft. After three years with the team, he was traded to the [[Quebec Remparts]], and midway through the [[2015–16 QMJHL season|2015–16 season]], he was traded to the [[Rouyn-Noranda Huskies]]. That season, Brouillard and the Huskies won the [[Gilles-Courteau Trophy|President's Cup]] as QMJHL champions. Throughout his entire QMJHL career, Brouillard attended many [[National Hockey League]] (NHL) development camps, but was never selected in the [[NHL entry draft]]. Brouillard signed his first professional contract in 2016, with the AHL's [[Toronto Marlies]]. During the [[2016–17 ECHL season|2016–17 season]], he spent most of his time with the Marlies' [[ECHL]] affiliate, the [[Orlando Solar Bears]], playing only one game with the Marlies.

For the 2017–18 season, Brouillard took the collegiate route, joining the [[McGill Redbirds ice hockey|McGill Redmen]] of [[U Sports]]. In his third and final year with the team, he was named the U Sports defenceman of the year. He then signed with the San Diego Gulls in 2021, and he remained with the team for three seasons, before signing with the NHL's [[New York Rangers]]. During the [[2023–24 AHL season|2023–24 season]], Brouillard only played with the Rangers' AHL affiliate, the [[Hartford Wolf Pack]]. For the [[2024–25 AHL season|2024–25 season]], he signed with the [[Seattle Kraken]], but once again, he only played in he NHL, this time with the [[Coachella Valley Firebirds]]. In 2025, he rejoined the Gulls for the [[2025–26 AHL season|2025–26 season]].

He finished the regular season with 12 goals and nine assists through 26 games. During the OUA playoffs, he recorded one goal and three assists in five games.<ref name=":6" /> On November 15, 2019, during the 2019–20 season, Brouillard collected two goals and two points in a 4–3 overtime win over the Ontario Tech Ridgebacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Figueroa |first=Rafael |date=2019-11-15 |title=McGill pulls goalie, scores twice then ruffles Ridgebacks in overtime thriller |url=https://mcgillathletics.ca/news/2019/11/15/mens-ice-hockey-mcgill-pulls-goalie-scores-twice-then-ruffles-ridgebacks-in-overtime-thriller.aspx |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=McGill University Athletics |language=en}}</ref> On November 29, he notched two goals and an assist in a 4–3 overtime defeat of the [[Carleton Ravens men's ice hockey|Carleton Ravens]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Figueroa |first=Rafael |date=2019-11-29 |title=Lucky Lalonde lifts lads with OT winner as McGill topples No. 3 Ravens |url=https://mcgillathletics.ca/news/2019/11/29/mens-ice-hockey-lucky-lalonde-lands-whopper-in-huge-ot-win-over-no-3-ravens.aspx |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=McGill University Athletics |title=OUA Hockey Awards: McGill trio of Brouillard, Guindon and Talbot-Tassi honoured |date=2020-03-11 |title=Brouillard becomes fourth McGillian to be named top defenceman in U Sports Athletics |language=en}}</ref> During the OUA playoffs, he totaled two assists in three games.<ref name=":6" />

===Professional===
====San Diego Gulls====
On January 11, 2021, Brouillard signed a one-year contract with the AHL's [[San Diego Gulls]].<ref name=":8" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-01-11 |title=Gulls sign four to AHL deals |url=https://theahl.com/news/gulls-sign-four-to-ahl-deals |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=American Hockey League |language=en-US}}</ref> On March 3, during the [[2020–21 AHL season|2020–21 season]], he recorded his first AHL point, an assist, on the game-winning overtime goal by [[Chase De Leo]] in a 5–4 win over the [[Ontario Reign]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-03-03 |title=Chase De Leo's Overtime Goal Sinks Ontario Reign |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/san-diego-gulls-ontario-reign-recap-march-3-2021 |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> On March 26, he scored his first two AHL goals in a 4–1 win over the [[Bakersfield Condors]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-03-26 |title=Gulls Open Homestand With Win Over Condors |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/san-diego-gulls-take-down-bakersfield-condors-march-26-2021 |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> Brouillard finished his first AHL season with three goals and 11 assists through 29 games. During the 2021 Pacific Division playoffs, Brouillard recorded one assist in three games.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |title=Nikolas Brouillard Stats and Player Profile |url=https://theahl.com/stats/player/6442 |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=American Hockey League |language=en-US}}</ref>

On July 15, 2021, the Gulls signed Brouillard to a one-year contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-07-15 |title=Gulls Sign Nikolas Brouillard To One-Year Contract Extension |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/san-diego-gulls-sign-nikolas-brouillard-to-one-year-contract-extension |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> In September, Brouillard attended the training camp of the Gulls' NHL affiliate, the [[Anaheim Ducks]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-09-23 |title=Ducks Training Camp Notebook: Brouillard, Benoit Chase Higher Expectations |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/nikolas-brouillard-simon-benoit-reach-for-new-heights |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> and on October 4, he was reassigned by the Ducks to San Diego.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-10-04 |title=Anaheim Ducks Assign 15 Players To San Diego Gulls |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/anaheim-ducks-assign-15-players-to-san-diego-gulls-october-4-2021 |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> On October 15, he was named to San Diego's opening roster for the [[2021–22 AHL season|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-10-15 |title=San Diego Gulls Announce 2021–22 Season-Opening Roster |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/san-diego-gulls-announce-2021-2022-season-opening-roster |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> On November 13, he recorded his fifth point in his previous five games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-11-13 |title=Perreault's Highlight-Reel Tally Not Enough In Loss To Bakersfield |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/san-diego-gulls-bakersfield-condors-recap-november-13-2021 |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> On January 15, 2022, in a 4–3 win over the [[Abbotsford Canucks]], Brouillard fought with [[Danila Klimovich]] with under a minute remaining in the third period.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-17 |title=2021–22 Top Moments: Best Hits And Fights |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/2021-2022-san-diego-gulls-top-moments-best-hits-fights |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> On March 16, Brouillard tallied two goals and an assist in a 6–1 victory against the [[Henderson Silver Knights]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-16 |title=Live: Gulls Win Third Straight, Defeat Henderson 6–1 |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/san-diego-gulls-henderson-silver-knights-live-game-blog-march-16-2022 |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> Two days later, Brouillard scored a [[Short-handed|shorthanded]] goal in a 3–1 defeat of the Silver Knights.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-18 |title=Live: Gulls Push Win Streak To Four |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/san-diego-gulls-henderson-silver-knights-live-game-blog-march-18-2022 |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> In 66 games that season, Brouillard scored 13 goals, tied for first place in the AHL among defencemen, and collected 26 assists for 39 points.<ref name=":10" /><ref name=":11">{{Cite web |date=2022-10-13 |title=San Diego Gulls Sign Gates Jr., Osipov, Brouillard And Healey To Contracts |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/san-diego-gulls-sign-gates-jr-osipov-brouillard-and-healey-to-contracts |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> During the 2022 Calder Cup playoffs, he totaled two assists in two games.<ref name=":10" /> Brouillard re-signed with the Gulls on October 13, 2022, for the [[2022–23 AHL season|2022–23 season]].<ref name=":11" /> The next day, in the Gulls' season opener against the [[Grand Rapids Griffins]], he notched a goal and two assists in a 6–2 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-10-14 |title=Preview: Gulls Seek To Continue Their Good Start Against Griffins Brouillard recorded a career-high four assists in a 5–4 loss to the Abbotsford Canucks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-12-14 |title=Brouillard Sets Career High, Gulls Lose 5–4 To Canucks |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/san-diego-gulls-abbotsford-canucks-recap-december-14-2022 |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> Through all 72 games that season, Brouillard notched six goals and 33 assists.<ref name=":10" />

====New York Rangers and Seattle Kraken organizations====
On July 1, 2023, Brouillard signed a one-year contract with the [[New York Rangers]], his first NHL contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-01 |title=Rangers Agree to Terms with Connor Mackey and Nikolas Brouillard |url=https://www.nhl.com/rangers/news/rangers-agree-to-terms-with-connor-mackey-and-nikolas-brouillard-345158542 |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=National Hockey League |language=en}}</ref> After being named to the Rangers' training camp on September 19,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-19 |title=Rangers Announce 2023–24 Training Camp Roster and Schedule |url=https://www.nhl.com/rangers/news/rangers-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster-and-schedule |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=National Hockey League |language=en}}</ref> he was assigned to their AHL affiliate, the [[Hartford Wolf Pack]], on September 24 to start the [[2023–24 AHL season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-24 |title=Rangers Trim Roster to 48 Players |url=https://www.nhl.com/rangers/news/rangers-trim-roster-to-48-players-0924 |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=National Hockey League |language=en}}</ref> On October 21, he recorded his first assist and first goal with the Wolf Pack, an assist in a 5–1 win over the [[Lehigh Valley Phantoms]], the Wolf Pack's 1000th win as a franchise.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-21 |title=Wolf Pack Win 1,000th Game in Franchise History 5–1 Over Phantoms |url=https://www.hartfordwolfpack.com/news/detail/wolf-pack-win-1000th-game-in-franchise-history-5-1-over-phantoms |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=Hartford Wolf Pack |language=en}}</ref> Brouillard finished the season with five goals and 31 assists in 70 games. During the [[2024 Calder Cup playoffs]], he put up two assists in 10 games.<ref name=":10" />

[[File:Calgary Flames at Seattle Kraken - 2024-09-22 - Nikolas Brouillard and Clark Bishop (54016294397).jpg|thumb|alt=Ice hockey players skating|Brouillard (right) with the Kraken during a preseason game in September 2024]]

On July 1, 2024, Brouillard signed a one-year contract with the [[Seattle Kraken]].<ref name=":9" /> After participating in the Kraken's training camp, he was assigned to the [[Coachella Valley Firebirds]], their AHL affiliate, on September 27, 2024, to start the [[2024–25 AHL season|2024–25 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-07 |title=Camp Blog Kraken Roster Taking Shape Ahead of Tuesday's Opener |url=https://www.nhl.com/kraken/news/blog-2024-kraken-camp-pres-by-starbucks-ft |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=National Hockey League |language=en}}</ref> He earned his first point with the Firebirds on October 18, assisting on a goal in a 6–5 victory over his former team, the San Diego Gulls.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rotolo |first=Gina |date=2024-10-19 |title=Coachella Valley's Offense Explodes for Six Goals in Victory Over San Diego |url=https://cvfirebirds.com/2024/10/18/fleurys-hat-trick-leads-firebirds-to-first-win-of-season/ |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=Coachella Valley Firebirds |language=en-US}}</ref> On November 26, Brouillard scored his first goal with the Firebirds and then recorded three assists in an 8–2 win over the [[Tucson Roadrunners]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rotolo |first=Gina |date=2024-11-27 |title=Brouillard's Four-Point Performance Extends Coachella Valley's Points Streak to Eight |url=https://cvfirebirds.com/2024/11/26/brouillard-records-four-points-in-firebirds-win-over-roadrunners/ |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=Coachella Valley Firebirds |language=en-US}}</ref> On April 5, Brouillard scored two goals in the first period of a 3–1 victory against the Henderson Silver Knights.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rotolo |first=Gina |date=2025-04-05 |title=Coachella Valley Defeats Henderson to Begin Weekend Series, 3-1 |url=https://cvfirebirds.com/2025/04/05/brouillard-strikes-twice-as-firebirds-down-silver-knights/ |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=Coachella Valley Firebirds |language=en-US}}</ref> Through 69 games that season, Brouillard totaled seven goals and 31 assists. During the [[2025 Calder Cup playoffs]], he tallied one assist in six games.<ref name=":10" />

====Return to San Diego====
On July 2, 2025, Brouillard signed a one-year contract with his former team, the San Diego Gulls.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Diego Gulls Sign Matthew Phillips And Nikolas Brouillard |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/san-diego-gulls-sign-phillips-and-brouillard-july-2-2025 |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> On December 12, he became the first Gulls player to record 100 career points with the team, doing so in a 4–1 win over the Henderson Silver Knights.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-12 |title=Gulls Defeat Silver Knights for Third Straight Victory |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/san-diego-gulls-henderson-silver-knights-recap-dec-12-2025 |archive-date= |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> Brouillard surpassed [[Brandon Montour]] for most goals as a defenceman in Gulls history on March 7, 2026, in a 6–4 victory over the [[Rockford IceHogs]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-07 |title=Carpenter Shines in Gulls Victory Over IceHogs |url=https://www.sandiegogulls.com/news/detail/san-diego-gulls-rockford-icehogs-recap-mar-7-2026 |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Gulls |language=en}}</ref> He played his record 229th game with the Gulls on April 9 in a 5–2 win against the San Jose Barracuda.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carter |first=Ivan |date=2026-04-09 |title=Pro Sports Report: Gulls closing in on AHL playoff berth; Sockers learn playoff foe |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2026/04/09/pro-sports-report-gulls-closing-in-on-ahl-playoff-berth-sockers-learn-playoff-foe/ |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=San Diego Union-Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished the [[2025–26 AHL season|2025–26 season]] with four goals and 20 assists in 67 games. During the [[2026 Calder Cup playoffs]], he tallied one assist in two games.<ref name=":10" />

====Djurgårdens IF====
On July 8, 2026, Brouillard signed a one-year contract with [[Swedish Hockey League]] (SHL) club [[Djurgårdens IF (men's ice hockey)|Djurgårdens IF]], ending a run of six consecutive seasons in the AHL.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Djurgårdens drag - värvar kanadensare |url=https://hockeysverige.se/nyheter/djurgarden-varvar-nikolas-brouillard-ab5cu2O4LJJm/ |last=Jansson |first=Martin |date=2026-07-08 |access-date=2026-07-25 |website=Hockeysverige.se |language=Swedish}}</ref>

|language=fr |url=https://the-melting-pop.blogspot.com/2022/08/naika-qui-est-la-chanteuse-qui.html |access-date=2026-03-03 |website=The Melting Pop |date=2022-08-07}}{{cite web |url=https://www.myp-magazine.com/interview/naika-a-uniting-sound/ |title=We've created so many boundaries, I want to tear these walls down. |website=MYP Magazine |date=2018-02-20 |access-date=2022-05-14}}{{Cite web |date=2015-09-25 |title=John Lennon Scholarship Winners Announced |url=https://www.bmi.com/news/entry/john_lennon_scholarship_winners_announced |access-date=2025-08-20 |website=BMI.com |language=en}} known professionally as '''Naïka''', is an American and [[French Haitians|French-Haitian]] singer-songwriter. == Early life and education == Naïka was born in [[Miami]] to a [[Haitians|Haitian]] mother of [[Palestinians|Palestinian]], [[Syrian]] and [[Lebanese people|Lebanese]] origin{{Cite web |last=Lodi |first=Hafsa |date=2026-01-12 |title=Naïka Embraces her Layered Identity and Looks to New Horizons |url=https://www.voguearabia.com/article/naika-looks-to-new-horizons |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=Vogue Arabia |language=en-AE}} and a French father who was raised in [[Madagascar]].{{cite web |url=https://sdvoyager.com/interview/meet-naika/ |title=Meet Naïka |work=SDVoyager |language=en-US |date=2018-08-20 |access-date=2025-11-29}}{{cite web |last=Jean-Marie|first=Ruth |url=https://haitiantimes.com/2025/11/23/naika-multicultural-identity-music/ |title=Beyond the layers with French-Haitian singer-songwriter Naïka |work=[[Haitian Times]] |language=en-US |date=2025-11-23 |access-date=2025-11-29}} She and her mother traveled with him as he moved for work. As a child, Naïka lived in various countries and regions, namely [[Guadeloupe]], [[Vanuatu]], [[Nairobi]], [[Paris]], and [[South Africa]], before moving back to Miami when she was 16.{{cite web |url=https://www.naikaofficial.com/about |title=About Naïka |work=naikaofficial.com |language=en-US |access-date=2025-01-07}}{{cite web |url=https://voyagela.com/interview/meet-naika/ |title=Meet Naïka |work=Voyage LA |language=en-US |date=2020-02-17 |access-date=2025-01-07}}{{cite web |url=https://reggieslive.com/show/naika/ |title=Naïka |publisher=[[Reggies]] |language=en-US |date=2022 |access-date=2025-02-19}}{{cite web |url=https://www.cntraveler.com/story/women-who-travel-podcast-singer-naika-on-life-as-a-third-culture-kid |title=Women Who Travel Podcast: Singer Naïka on Life As a Third Culture Kid |work=[[Condé Nast Traveler]] |language=en-US |date=2025-03-14 |access-date=2025-09-27}} She developed her musical interests at an early age,{{cite web|last=Randolph|first=Choya|url=https://musicrunnermag.com/posts/naika/|title=Naïka Creates Her Own Brand of 'World Pop'|language=en-US|work=Musicrunner|date=December 23, 2019|access-date=January 8, 2025}}{{cite web |url=https://www.positionmusic.com/artist/MjczNDg0LTIzMDA4Mw |title=Naïka |work=Position Music |access-date=2021-12-05}} attending [[tamure]] classes during her time in Vanuatu and receiving two years of classical piano training in South Africa. In 2015, Naïka placed second in the BMI John Lennon Foundation Scholarship competition.{{cite web |url=https://www.universal-music.de/naika/biografie |title=Naïka {{!}} Biografie |language=de |publisher=[[Universal Music Germany]] |access-date=2021-12-05}}{{cite web |url=https://www.anrfactory.com/naika/ |title=A&R Factory Present: Naïka |work=A&R Factory |date=2017-05-26 |access-date=2025-01-07}} She studied Performance as her major at [[Berklee College of Music]] in [[Boston]],{{cite web |url=https://www.montreuxjazzfestival.com/en/artist/naika/ |title=Naïka |publisher=[[Montreux Jazz Festival]] |access-date=2025-02-19}} and was selected during her first year for a tour with [[Michael Bolton]]. She participated in the [[NBC]] casting show ''[[The Voice (American TV series)|The Voice]]'' and, during her 7th semester, she was selected to take part in a [[training camp|bootcamp]] class by songwriter [[Kara DioGuardi]]. She created the song "Ride", which she would release after her debut single "Call Me Marilyn". Following graduation, she moved to [[Los Angeles]] to pursue a musical career.{{cite web |url=https://www.fewordscollective.com/stories/naika-singer-songwriter |title=Naika — Singer/Songwriter |work=Fewords Collective |date=2024-06-22 |access-date=2025-02-19 |url-status=dead}} == Career == [[File:2018-07-15 ZDF Fernsehgarten Naika-0979.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Naïka on the German TV show ''[[ZDF-Fernsehgarten]]'']] Her 2016 rendition of the Haitian traditional song "Papa Gèdè (Bel Gason)" received 200,000 clicks within two days and a total of over 1 million views. After the success of her 2017 debut single "Ride", which obtained 5 million [[Spotify]] streams{{snd}}resulting in a second place on the platform's Global Viral chart{{snd}}and charted in twelve countries, she signed a two-year contract with [[Capitol Records]] (a division of [[Universal Music Group|Universal Music]]). After releasing several singles between 2017 and 2019, she rose to prominence in early 2020, when a [[TikTok]] video of her version of "[[Don't Rush (Young T & Bugsey song)|Don't Rush]]" garnered over 20 million views in three months, drawing the attention of the original artists [[Young T & Bugsey]]. In 2020 and 2021, respectively, she released the EPs ''Lost in Paradïse, Pt. 1'' and ''Lost in Paradïse, Pt. 2'', under the label [[AWAL]].{{cite web |last=Tindel |first=Arielle |url=https://www.wearetheguard.com/music/best-new-artists-naika |title=Featured find: Naïka has the 'sauce' and the recipe to an emerging genre |work=We Are: The Guard |language=en-US |date=2021-03-18 |access-date=2025-01-07}} In 2021, her song "Sauce" debuted in an [[IPhone|Apple iPhone]] commercial during the [[Grammy Awards|Grammys]] telecast.{{Cite web |last=Andrews |first=Lucas |date=2021-03-22 |title=Naika unleashes 'Sauce', premiered in Apple's iPhone campaign during The Grammy's {{!}} New Music |url=https://www.musiccrowns.org/new-music/naika-unleashes-sauce-premiered-in-apples-iphone-campaign-during-the-grammys/ |access-date=2025-10-18 |website=Music Crowns |language=en-US}} In April 2024, Naïka made an appearance during [[Saint Levant]]'s performance at [[Coachella 2024]], duetting to an unreleased song.{{cite web |last=Sharawneh |first=Dana |url=https://www.cosmopolitanme.com/celebs/saint-levant-and-naika |title=A timeline of Saint Levant and Naika's relationship (IYKYK) |work=[[Cosmopolitan (magazine)|Cosmopolitan]] Middle East |date=2024-08-28 |access-date=2025-01-10}} Her debut album, ''Eclesia'', was released on February 20, 2026. [[File:Naïka at 2026 Montreux Jazz Festival 21.jpg|thumb|upright|Naïka performing at the 60th [[Montreux Jazz Festival]] in 2026.]] === Artistry === Naïka is a multilingual artist, singing in [[French language|French]], [[Haitian Creole]], and English. Her musical style, which she defines "world pop", is based on a mix of [[world music]]{{snd}}blending [[European music|European]] (particularly [[Music of France|French]]), [[African music|African]], [[Caribbean music|Caribbean]] and [[Afro-Caribbean music|Afro-Caribbean]] music{{snd}}with [[Pop music|pop]], [[soul music|soul]] and [[R&B]]. She cites childhood influences from [[Britney Spears]], [[Destiny's Child]], [[Usher (musician)|Usher]], the [[Black Eyed Peas]], [[Bob Marley]], [[Miriam Makeba]], [[Brenda Fassie]] and [[Nameless (musician)|Nameless]],{{cn|date=October 2025}} as well as classical composers like [[Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart]]. == Personal life == Naïka lives and works in Los Angeles. She identifies as a "[[third culture kid]]". In December 2023, she started a relationship with Palestinian rapper [[Saint Levant]];{{cite web|last=Laïreche|first=Rachid|url=https://www.liberation.fr/portraits/saint-levant-libre-reveur-20240603_JM4246LR4ZDFFINZW6DGLOHJ3Y/|title=Saint Levant, Libre rêveur|language=fr|work=[[Libération]]|date=2024-06-03|access-date=2025-01-09|url-access=subscription}}{{cite web|last=Catabui|first=Quinn|url=https://graziamagazine.com/me/articles/timeline-of-saint-levant-naika-relationship/|title=A Complete Timeline Of Saint Levant & Naika's Relationship|work=[[Grazia Middle East]]|date=2025-01-07|access-date=2025-01-07}}{{cite web|url=https://al-ain.com/article/saint-levant-naika-breakup|title=انفصال سانت ليفانت ونايكا.. رسائل الوداع مؤثرة|language=ar|work=al-ain.com|date=2025-09-25|access-date=2025-09-25}} the couple announced their breakup via [[Instagram]] on September 25, 2025.{{cite web|last=Raut|first=Mamta|url=https://me.mashable.com/culture/61562/power-couple-saint-levant-and-naika-call-it-quits-but-its-all-love-and-respect|title=Power couple Saint Levant and Naïka call it quits but it’s all love and respect|work=[[Mashable]] Middle East|date=2025-09-26|access-date=2025-09-27}} == Discography == [[File:Naïka Logo.png|thumb|Naïka's logo in use since 2020]] === Albums === * ''Eclesia'' (2026) === EPs === * ''Lost in Paradïse, Pt. 1'' (2020) * ''Lost in Paradïse, Pt. 2'' (2021) * ''Transitions EP'' (2022) === Singles === * "Call Me Marilyn" (2017) * "Ride" (2017) * "Limbo" (2017) * "Serpentine" (2018) * "Oh Mama" (2018) * "Blame" (2018) * "Snowing in L.A." '''Will Hochman''' is an American stage, television and film actor.

==Early life==
From [[Brooklyn]], Hochman graduated from [[Colby College]] with a degree in economics. He started acting at the age of 20, and took an acting course at Colby's Department of Performance, Theater, and Dance and performed as a student at the Powder and Wig, Colby's student-run theatre club. His performances included playing John Proctor in a production of ''[[The Crucible (play)|The Crucible]]''.<ref name="lewis"/><ref name="baker">{{cite web|url= https://www.wmagazine.com/culture/will-hochman-the-sound-inside-broadway-interview|website=wmmagazine|accessdate=27 March 2025|title= New Faces: Will Hochman, The Sound Inside's Tortured Soul|first=Brooke|last=Marine|date=15 November 2019}}</ref><ref name="bailey"/>

==Career==
Hochman's first professional stage play was a stage adaptation of ''[[Dead Poets Society]]'' for [[Classic Stage Company]] in New York.<ref name="lewis">{{cite web|url= https://www.broadway.com/buzz/197212/will-hochman-on-how-a-basketball-injury-helped-him-win-his-the-sound-inside-role-going-toe-to-toe-with-mary-louise-parker/|website=Broadway.com|accessdate=27 March 2025|title= Will Hochman on How a Basketball Injury Helped Him Win His The Sound Inside Role & 'Going Toe-to-Toe' with Mary-Louise Parker|date=11 October 2019|first=Lyndsey|last=Sullivan}}</ref> He had an early television appearance in [[CBS]] series ''[[The Code (American TV series)|The Code]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.countryliving.com/life/entertainment/a34933764/who-plays-joe-hill-on-blue-bloods-will-hochman-actor/|website=Country Living|accessdate=27 March 2025|title= Who Plays Joe Hill on 'Blue Bloods'? Here's Where You've Seen Will Hochman Before|date=11 Dec 2020|first=Rebecca|last=Norris}}</ref> His early film roles include [[John Leguizamo]]'s directorial debut ''[[Critical Thinking (film)|Critical Thinking]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2018/11/john-leguizamo-jorge-lendeborg-jr-michael-k-williams-critical-thinking-1202502901/|title=John Leguizamo, 'Bumblebee's Jorge Lendeborg Jr., Michael K. Williams To Star In 'Critical Thinking'; Leguizamo Directing|website=Deadline Hollywood|first=Amanda|last=N'Duka|date=November 16, 2018|access-date=27 March 2025}}</ref> and the [[Kevin Costner]] film ''[[Let Him Go (film)|Let Him Go]]''. He appeared on [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]] at [[Studio 54]] between October 2019 and January 2020, in  [[David Cromer]]'s production of the play ''[[The Sound Inside (play)|The Sound Inside]]'' by [[Adam Rapp]]''.'' He played Christopher, a Yale student, alongside [[Mary-Louise Parker]]'s professor Bella, for a total of 100 performances.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2019-10-18 |title=Review: Mary-Louise Parker in the Subliminal, Sublime ‘Sound Inside’ (Published 2019) |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/10/17/theater/the-sound-inside-review.html |access-date=2025-08-01 |language=en}}</ref> The play received six [[Tony Award]] nominations, including for [[Tony Award for Best Play|Best Play]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Evans|first=Greg|date=15 October 2020|title=Tony Awards Nominations 2020 – The Complete List|url=https://deadline.com/2020/10/tony-award-nominations-2020-broadway-theater-2-1234598010/|access-date=27 March 2025|website=Deadline Hollywood}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=30 July 2024|first=Julianne|last=MacNeill|website=Womans World|url= https://www.womansworld.com/entertainment/celebrities/blue-bloods-will-hochman-where-the-actor-got-his-start#|title= 'Blue Bloods' Star Will Hochman: Where He Really Got His Start|accessdate=27 March 2025}}</ref>

He appeared in five seasons of CBS series ''[[Blue Bloods]]'', in the role of Joe Hill, joining the series in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://deadline.com/2020/12/blue-bloods-spoilers-recap-coronavirus-whoopi-goldberg-season-debut-kevin-wade-interview-police-cbs-1234649887/|website=Deadline Hollywood|accessdate=27 March 2025|title= 'Blue Bloods' EP Kevin Wade On Tonight's Season 11 Debut, Whoopi Goldberg, Police Brutality, & Pandemic Production|date=4 Dec 2020|first=Dominic|last=Patten}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.closerweekly.com/posts/blue-bloods-cast-members-support-will-hochman-amid-big-career-news/#|website=Closer Weekly|accessdate=27 March 2025|title= 'Blue Bloods' Cast Members Show Support for Costar Will Hochman Amid His Big Career News|date=24 March 2025|first=Samantha|last=Agate}}</ref> He appeared in the 2022 film ''[[The Greatest Beer Run Ever]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grobar |first=Matt |date=November 8, 2021 |title='The Greatest Beer Run Ever' Adds Ruby Ashbourne Serkis, Matt Cook, Omari K. Chancellor & Will Hochman |url=https://deadline.com/2021/11/the-greatest-beer-run-ever-adds-ruby-ashbourne-serkis-matt-cook-more-peter-farrelly-apple-1234869919/ |website=Deadline Hollywood |access-date=27 March 2025}}</ref>

He had a recurring role in [[Billy Crystal]] and [[Judith Light]]'s [[Apple TV+]] series ''[[Before (TV series)|Before]]''. He will star alongside [[Deborah Ann Woll]] and [[Jeffrey Donovan]] in ''The Cycle''.<ref>{{cite web|website=Collider|url= https://collider.com/vought-rising-cast-will-hochman-elizabeth-posey/|accessdate=27 March 2025|title= 'The Boys' Prequel 'Vought Rising' Expands Its Cast With 'Blue Bloods' and 'Euphoria' Stars|first=Britta|last=DeVore|date=Mar 19, 2025}}</ref> In March 2025, he joined the cast of ''[[Vought Rising]]'', a spin-off prequel series from superhero television comedy series ''[[The Boys (TV series)|The Boys]]'' as Torpedo.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/the-boys-prequel-vought-rising-cast-will-hochman-1236342518/ |website=Variety|accessdate=27 March 2025|title= 'The Boys' Prequel 'Vought Rising' Casts 'Blue Bloods' Alum Will Hochman (EXCLUSIVE) |first=Joe|last=Otterson|date=March 19, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://deadline.com/gallery/vought-rising-super-suits-photos-the-boys-prime-video/|website=Deadline Hollywood|accessdate=14 August 2025|title= 'The Boys' Prequel Series 'Vought Rising' Super Suits Photos: Jensen Ackles As Soldier Boy, Mason Dye As Bombsight & More|first= Armando |last=Tinoco|date=August 14, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.thewrap.com/vought-rising-first-look-jensen-ackles-mason-dye-cast-supersuits/|website=The Wrap|accessdate=14 August 2025|title= 'The Boys' Debuts 'Vought Rising' Prequel Series First Look at Jensen Ackles, Mason Dye and More|first=Raquel |last=Harris}}</ref>

'''Najoua Laamri''' (born 30 June 1994), known professionally as '''Nej'''', is a French singer-songwriter. She rose to prominence in 2021 with her viral single [[Paro (song)|Paro]].

== Early life ==
Born in [[Toulouse]], France, Nej' is of [[Moroccans in France|Moroccan]] heritage.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aficia.info/actualite-musique/nej-paro/244372|title=Nej’ explose avec "Paro" : le phénomène TikTok confirmé|website=Aficia|date=6 November 2021|access-date=19 April 2025}}</ref>

== Career ==
Nej' began her musical career in 2016, releasing her early works independently.{{Cn|date=May 2025}} She gradually built an online following, gaining wider public attention with the success of ''[[Paro (song)|Paro]]'' in 2021.{{Cn|date=May 2025}} She continued to release a series of successful EPs and full-length albums, with her 2023 album ''Athéna'' solidifying her presence in the French urban music landscape and expanding her reach to broader audiences both in France and internationally.{{Cn|date=May 2025}}

In 2023, Nej' launched the Athéna Tour, her first nationwide headlining concert series across major French cities.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/scenes/concerts/articles/283846-nej-en-concert-a-la-seine-musicale-en-novembre-2023|title=Nej' en concert à la Seine Musicale en novembre 2023|website=Sortir à Paris|access-date=19 April 2025}}</ref>

== Musical style and influences ==
Nej's music is known for emotional storytelling, melodic hooks, and [[Music of North Africa|North African influences]]. She writes much of her own material, drawing on themes such as heartbreak, healing, and self-empowerment. Nej often blends [[French language|French]] with [[Arabic]] phrases in her lyrics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://vl-media.fr/interview-nej-nous-parle-de-son-univers-et-de-son-nouveau-projet-athena/|title=Interview : Nej’ nous parle de son univers et de son projet " Athéna "|website=VL Media|date=17 March 2023|access-date=19 April 2025}}</ref>

Her musical inspirations include [[Rhythm and blues|R&B]] icons like [[Beyoncé]] and [[Alicia Keys]], as well as French-speaking artists such as [[Zaho]] and [[Amel Bent]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nrj.fr/artistes/nej/biographie|title=Biographie de Nej’|website=NRJ|access-date=19 April 2025}}</ref> Her North African roots frequently influence her vocal stylings and lyrical themes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raprnb.com/2022/06/24/nej-je-nai-jamais-renie-mes-origines-interview/|title=Nej’ : "Je n’ai jamais renié mes origines"|website=RAPRNB|date=24 June 2022|access-date=19 April 2025}}</ref>

'''Christian Roger Beharie''' (born 22 April 1994), known professionally as '''Beharie''', is a Norwegian [[Soul music|soul]]/[[Rhythm and blues|RnB]] singer/songwriter from [[Sandnes]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-10-21 |title=Beharie (27) skal snart dele scene med idolet sitt i Sandnes: – Først tenkte jeg: Hæ, hva får han ut av det? |url=https://www.aftenbladet.no/kultur/i/9Ko3Vr/jeg-fikk-selvtillit-til-aa-foele-at-jeg-har-en-plass-i-musikkbransje |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=Stavanger Aftenblad}}</ref>

He released his third EP, ''Bhearie, the Third'', in 2022, and was nominated for the Spellemannprisen 2022 in the RnB/soul category for this.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2023-03-03 |title=Karpe nominert til syv Spellemenn – med nykommerne Undergrunn hakk i hæl |url=https://www.dagsavisen.no/kultur/karpe-nominert-til-syv-spellemenn-med-nykommerne-undergrunn-hakk-i-hael/4330821 |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Dagsavisen |language=nb-NO}}</ref>

In October 2023, he released his debut album ''Are You There, Boy?''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mukuria |first=Andrew |date=2023-10-19 |title=Beharie: En av Norges beste artister |url=https://www.aftenposten.no/kultur/i/eJgVxy/en-av-norges-beste-artister |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Aftenposten |language=nb}}</ref> That year he was nominated for the [[Bendiksen Award]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-27 |title=Fem nominerte til Arne Bendiksens talentpris 2023 |url=https://www.ballade.no/bransjen/fem-nominerte-til-arne-bendiksens-talentpris-2023/ |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Ballade |language=nb-NO}}</ref> and the Spellemannprisen 2023 in the RnB/Soul category.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Djukastein |first=Bjørne Østrem |date=2024-02-29 |title=Dette er dei nominerte til Spellemannprisen |url=https://www.nrk.no/kultur/dette-er-dei-nominerte-til-spellemannprisen-1.16784055 |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=NRK |language=nn-NO}}</ref>

He contributed to the song "River" by [[Thomas Dybdahl]] from the album ''Fever'' in 2020. In 2018 and 2019 he played in the [[Det Norske Teatret|Norwegian Theatre]] production of ''[[The Book of Mormon (musical)|The Book of Mormon]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Christian Beharie {{!}} Skodespelarar |url=https://www.detnorsketeatret.no/skodespelarar/christian-beharie |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Det Norske Teatret |language=nn}}</ref>

'''Frida Orupabo''' (born 1986)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Frida Orupabo born 1986 |url=https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artists/frida-orupabo-32007 |access-date=2025-11-08 |website=Tate |language=en-GB}}</ref> is a Norwegian artist who makes work about identity, sexuality, race and belonging, using collage and video installation made from visual material found online.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Llorens |first=Natasha Marie |date=2022-05-11 |title=Frida Orupabo Preaches to the Choir |url=https://www.frieze.com/article/frida-orupabo-how-fast-shall-we-sing-review-2022 |access-date=2025-11-08 |work=Frieze |language=en |issue=228 |issn=0962-0672}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Sumba |first=Eric Otieno |date=2021-09-21 |title=Frida Orupabo Flips the Script on the Trope of the Horse in Art History |url=https://www.frieze.com/article/frida-orupabo-girl-on-horse |access-date=2025-11-08 |work=Frieze |language=en |issue=222 |issn=0962-0672}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |website=Victoria and Albert Museum|title=Replacement |date=2024 |url=https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O1784103/replacement-photograph-orupabo-frida/ |access-date=2025-11-08}}</ref> She is also a trained [[Sociology|sociologist]]. Orupabo's mother is Norwegian and her father is Nigerian.<ref name="artreview">{{Cite web |title=Frida Orupabo Reconfigures Black Female Sexuality |url=https://artreview.com/frida-orupabo-reconfigures-black-female-sexuality/ |access-date=2025-11-08 |website=artreview.com |language=en}}</ref> She has had solo exhibitions at [[Fotomuseum Winterthur]] in Switzerland and at [[Astrup Fearnley Museum of Modern Art]] in Oslo, and her work was shown in the [[58th Venice Biennale]]. She has an Honorary Fellowship from the [[Royal Photographic Society]] in the UK.

==Early life and education==
Orupabo was born and grew up in [[Sarpsborg]], Norway.<ref name="hyperallergic">{{Cite web |last=Cielatkowska |first=Zofia |date=2019-05-20 |title=Using Collage to Illuminate How People Are Shaped by Identity Strategies |url=https://hyperallergic.com/499564/using-collage-to-illuminate-how-people-are-shaped-by-identity-strategies/ |access-date=2025-11-08 |website=Hyperallergic |language=en-US}}</ref> She has a White Norwegian mother and a Black Nigerian father.<ref name="artreview"/><ref name="rps">{{Cite web |title=Frida Orupabo |url=https://rps.org/about/awards/the-rps-awards-2023/rps-awards-2023-recipients/frida-orupabo/ |access-date=2025-11-09 |website=rps.org |language=en-GB}}</ref> She obtained a bachelor's degree in [[development studies]] then a master's degree in [[sociology]] from the [[University of Oslo]].<ref name="hyperallergic"/><ref name="studiomuseum">{{Cite web |title=Frida Orupabo |url=https://www.studiomuseum.org/artists/frida-orupabo |access-date=2025-11-08 |website=Studio Museum in Harlem |language=en}}</ref>

==Work==
She was shortlisted for the ''[[Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation Prize]]'' in 2023. The work—about identity, sexuality, race and belonging—was described by [[Sean O'Hagan (journalist)|Sean O'Hagan]] in ''The Guardian'' as "sculptural photographic collages [. . . ] strange, hybrid creations [. . . ] Her raw material is sourced from the digital sphere – images found on social media, eBay and old colonial archives. Printed, cut out and then layered in segments, her collages have a distinctly old-fashioned, hands-on feel, but her mainly female figures are loaded with meaning, both personal and cultural."<ref>{{Cite news |last=O'Hagan |first=Sean |date=2023-03-03 |title=Deutsche Börse photography prize review – stern heroes, uncanny hybrids and a missing person |url=https://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2023/mar/03/deutsche-borse-prize-review-the-photographers-gallery-london |access-date=2025-11-08 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>
