'''Ko Eun-sung''' ({{Korean|고은성}}; born on September 11, 1990) is a South Korean [[musical theatre]] actor and singer. He debuted in 2011 in the South Korean production of ''[[Spring Awakening (musical)|Spring Awakening]]'' and rose to fame by appearing on the [[JTBC]] audition program ''[[Phantom Singer]]'' in 2016, where he reached the finals and was part of the 3rd place quartet Hpresso. He has since played leading roles in various musicals in South Korea, and released his debut extended play ''Start Over'' in 2021.

== Early life and education ==
Ko was born in [[Daejeon]], South Korea,<ref name="daejeon" /> on September 11, 1990.<ref name="themusical" /> He has a younger brother.<ref name="daejeon" />

In his second year of high school, Ko dropped out of school because he felt that he would not find his life path through studying alone, and started attending a practical music academy since he liked singing. He wanted to become a singer first and almost debuted in a band, but switched to musical acting after watching a performance of ''[[Notre-Dame de Paris (musical)|Notre-Dame de Paris]]'' he had been forcibly taken to.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Park |first=Ga-young |date=2017-07-03 |title=[예능리뷰] ‘비정상회담’ 고은성, “10년동안 뮤지컬에 미쳐있다” |trans-title=[Entertainment Review] "Abnormal Summit"'s Ko Eun-sung: "I've Been Obsessed with Musicals for 10 Years" |url=https://www.topstarnews.net/news/articleView.html?idxno=280806 |website=TopStarNews |language=ko}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |date=2016-03-03 |title=[FACE] 37.5℃의 열정 [No.149] |trans-title=[FACE] 37.5℃ Passion [No. 149] |url=https://www.themusical.co.kr/Magazine/Detail?num=2702 |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=The Musical |language=ko}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=Park |first=Eun-hee |date=2016-12-27 |title=[AT인터뷰①] 고은성 “가능한 성대모사만 238가지…기회 되면 라이브로 보여줄 것” |trans-title=[AT Interview ①] Ko Eun-sung: "I have 238 possible voice impersonations... I'll show them live if I get the chance." |url=https://www.asiatoday.co.kr/kn/view.php?key=20161227001242099 |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=Asia Today |language=ko}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-07-19 |title='복면가왕' 노천탕 정체는 뮤지컬 배우 고은성…검투사 3R 진출 |trans-title=The identity of Outdoor Bather on "King of Mask Singer" is musical actor Ko Eun-sung... Gladiator advances to the third round |url=https://www.chosun.com/site/data/html_dir/2018/06/03/2018060301738.html |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=[[Chosun Ilbo]] |language=ko}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-12 |title=고은성 "저는 뮤지컬에 미친 사람…군대 휴가 나와 오디션 봤죠" |trans-title=Ko Eun-sung: "I'm crazy about musicals... I auditioned during my military leave" |url=https://www.sportschosun.com/entertainment/2024-01-12/202401120000000000010013 |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=Sports Chosun |language=ko}}</ref> He therefore entered the Musical Theater department of [[Daekyeung University]], which he quit after one semester because he had become intrigued by the world of musicals in [[Seoul]] after attending a lesson by Professor Cho Seung-yong, a musical actor; this decision almost had him kicked out of the family house. Unable to afford the move to the capital alone right away and not knowing anyone there, Ko temporarily stayed with a friend living in [[Incheon]] and attended an acting school while preparing for the entrance exam for [[Dankook University]]'s Department of Performing Arts and Film.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":8" />

== Career ==

=== 2011–2016: Beginnings ===
Ko debuted in 2011 in ''[[Spring Awakening (musical)|Spring Awakening]]'' while attending college, and later performed in ''[[Fame (musical)|Fame]]'', ''[[Grease (musical)|Grease]]'' and ''[[Spamalot]]'', among others.<ref name="agency">{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Ho-young |date=2017-02-13 |title=고은성, “좋아하는 이성 만나면 웃음 주려 노력한다”…이성관 화제 |trans-title=Ko Eun-sung, "I try to make people I like laugh when I meet them"… Lee Seong-gwan becomes a hot topic. |url=https://www.topstarnews.net/news/articleView.html?idxno=241517 |website=TopStarNews |language=ko}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Moon |first=Su-gyeong |date=2024-01-14 |title=[EN:터뷰]고은성 "뮤지컬로 바뀐 내 인생, 무대 허투루 설 수 없죠" |trans-title=[EN:Interview] Ko Eun-sung: "My life has changed through musicals. I can't just stand on stage and do nothing." |url=https://www.nocutnews.co.kr/news/6078521 |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=No Cut News |language=ko}}</ref> Finding himself unemployed after ''Fame'' ended, he returned to his hometown in Daejeon and worked part-time as a courier for a while.<ref name=":11">{{Cite news |last=Jang |first=Min-su |date=2021-05-04 |title=[인터뷰②] '그레이트 코멧' 고은성 "데뷔 10년, 포기 안하길 잘했죠" |trans-title=[Interview ②] 'Great Comet' Ko Eun-sung: "10 Years Since My Debut, I'm Glad I Never Gave Up" |url=https://www.slist.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=248458 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210518231835/https://www.slist.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=248458 |archive-date=May 18, 2021 |access-date=2026-01-29 |work=Single List |language=ko |url-status=live }}</ref> His financial struggles prompted him to decide to temporarily quit musicals and move to the United States with the help of one of his middle school classmates who already lived there to find a different job, earn money, and try again with musical acting in the future.<ref name=":15">{{Cite web |last=Choi |first=Yeong-hyeon |date=2023-07-26 |title=[COVER STORY] 너의 음악이 나를 외칠 때 - "Memphis" 고은성 [No.226] |trans-title=[COVER STORY] When Your Music Calls Me Out - "Memphis" Ko Eun-sung [No. 226] |url=https://www.themusical.co.kr/Magazine/Detail?num=5171 |access-date=2026-02-02 |website=The Musical |language=ko}}</ref> At the same time, Yang Joo-in, who directed him the previous year in ''Goddess Is Watching'', recommended he auditioned for the South Korean production of ''[[Wicked (musical)|Wicked]]'' because she thought his voice tone would fit it: originally, Ko had no intention of trying for the musical, lacking the desire to play a "cool character" and having a preference for non-mainstream roles, but Yang's words convinced him to change his mind.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Heo |first=Seol-hee |date=2016-07-26 |title=[MD인터뷰] '위키드' 고은성 "뽀얀 프린스? 구릿빛 섹시男 의도했죠" |trans-title=[MD Interview] Ko Eun-sung from 'Wicked': "A White Prince? I Intended to Be a Tanned, Sexy Man" |url=https://v.daum.net/v/ibkMuDpTMe |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=Daum}}</ref> He took the audition without aiming for a specific character, since he liked the ''Wicked'' numbers but had only heard of [[Elphaba]]'s and [[Glinda]]'s before, and was ultimately cast as [[Fiyero]]. Even though he struggled to resonate with the character's reasons at first, the role brought him further recognition as a musical actor thanks to his stable acting and singing skills, and he abandoned the plan to emigrate.<ref name=":15" /><ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Jang |first=Jang-young |date=2017-08-16 |title='라디오스타' 아이비 남친 고은성, 무대 씹어먹는 마성의 매력 |trans-title='Radio Star' Ivy's boyfriend Ko Eun-sung shows off his captivating stage presence. |url=http://www.mhns.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=72497 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201031221231/http://www.mhns.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=72497 |archive-date=October 31, 2020 |access-date=2026-01-15 |work=Munhwa News |language=ko |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== 2016–2020: ''Phantom Singer'' and military enlistment ===

'''Yuka Sadaka''' (born 2 November 1994) is a Japanese [[rugby union]] player. She competed for {{nwrut|Japan}} at the [[2021 Rugby World Cup]].
==Rugby career==
Sadaka started playing [[Rugby union|rugby]] in her first year of junior high school.

She earned her first [[Cap (sport)|cap]] for {{nwrut|Japan}} in May 2014 in the [[2014 Asia Women's Four Nations|Asian Championship]] match against {{nwrut|Hong Kong}}.

In 2022, she scored one of two tries in the [[Japan women's national rugby union team|Sakura's]] historic match against the [[New Zealand women's national rugby union team|Black Ferns]] before the World Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burnes |first=Campbell |date=2022-09-24 |title=Woodman bags seven tries in Japan rout |url=https://www.allblacks.com/news/woodman-bags-seven-tries-in-japan-rout |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-25 |website=www.allblacks.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-24 |title=Rugby: Sakura Fifteen thrashed 95-12 by World Cup hosts New Zealand |url=https://english.kyodonews.net/articles/-/35922 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=Japan Wire by KYODO NEWS |language=en}}</ref> She was selected in Japan's squad for the delayed [[2021 Rugby World Cup]] in [[New Zealand]].

She featured for Japan at the inaugural [[2023 WXV#WXV 2|WXV 2]] tournament in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-20 |title=Sakura Fifteen Team Announced for Samoa WXV Match |url=https://en.rugby-japan.jp/2023/10/20/sakura-fifteen-team-announced-for-samoa-wxv-match/ |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=Japan Rugby Football Union |language=en}}</ref>

'''Jeong Hanee''' ({{korean|hangul=정하늬}}; born August 26, 1987), known professionally as '''Honey J''' ({{lang|ko|허니제이}}), is a South Korean choreographer, dancer, and singer. She is known for her work with the crews HolyBang and BumsUp and earlier affiliations with Soul Sisterz and Purplow. She has served as a backing dancer for artists including [[Jay Park]]. Jeong competed on the dance competition series ''[[Street Woman Fighter]]'' and ''[[World of Street Woman Fighter]]'', leading HolyBang to victory on ''Street Woman Fighter'' in 2021. In May 2022, she signed as the first artist to Jay Park's label [[More Vision]] and released the single "Look".

== Early life and education ==
Jeong Hanee was born on August 26, 1987, in [[Cheongju]], South Korea. Her parents divorced when she was eight, after which she spent a year living with her father. Her mother, Jang Hyun‑sook, lived separately about ten minutes away and struggled with depression due to being a housewife with no income.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newsen.com/news_view.php?uid=202503160833221110|title=허니제이 母, 딸 8살에 이혼 "양육권 뺏겨 극단적 생각+몸무게 37㎏" (엄마를 부탁해)|language=ko|date=March 16, 2025|last=Im |first=Yesol|website=Newsen}}</ref> Following an day in which Jeong's father and aunt returned home late, Jeong left a note for her father and traveled with her younger sibling to live with their mother when she was in second grade of elementary school.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imbc.com/broad/enews/view.html?idx=453185|title='엄마를 부탁해' 허니제이 母 "딸 8살 때 이혼…양육권 빼앗겨 극단적 생각"|language=ko|date=March 16, 2025|website=[[IMBC]]|last=Baek |first=Ah-young}}</ref>

Jeong began studying dance as a child at a neighborhood jazz academy while in middle school, developing her skills and winning a competition award. She continued dancing through middle and high school, forming the group Rahe with friends and remaining active with them until college.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news1.kr/entertain/broadcast-tv/4613124|title=허니제이, 러블리 모친 공개…스티커 사진→꽃꽂이 '완벽' 청주 데이트(종합)|language=ko|date=March 12, 2022|website=[[News1 (South Korean newspaper)|News1]]|last=Ah |first=Nun-jae}}</ref> While in high school, she saw a performance by Soul Sisterz, which inspired her to pursue dance full time and to join the group.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wkorea.com/2018/04/02/몸으로-말하는-사람들-댄서-6팀-vol-1/|title=몸으로 말하는 사람들, 댄서 6팀 Vol.1|language=ko|date=April 2, 2018|last=Lee |first=Chae-min|website=[[W Korea]]}}</ref> She attended and graduated from the {{ill|Paekche Institute of the Arts|ko|백제예술대학교}} with an [[associate degree]] in practical dance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbntv.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=996309|title=허니제이 예비신랑 정담 "이렇게 잘생긴 남편인데" 직업·나이 주목받을 수밖에|language=ko|date=October 22, 2022|first=Byeonghun |last=Jin|website=[[NBN TV]]}}</ref>

== Dance career ==
[[File:HolyBang, 2021.jpg|thumb|upright=1|right|Honey J (fourth from left) with other members of HolyBang in 2021.]]
She made her first appearance with Soul Sisterz at the 2009 Gyeongpo Dance Festival as the group's youngest member, performing [[waacking]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.xportsnews.com/article/1522144|title=[엑:스피디아] 허니제이 맞아? '춤짱'이 된 백금발 막내 (옛날 신인)|language=ko|date=January 10, 2022|website=[[XSport News]]}}</ref> In 2011, Jeong formed the dance crew Purplow and was put in charge of artist choreography at [[AOMG]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=115710|title="내 이상형은 키 큰 미남이고, 박재범 이상형은 아이유" 허니제이가 박재범과 찐친일 수밖에 없는 이유를 밝혔다|language=ko|date=December 30, 2021|last=Kang |first=Na-yeon|website=[[HuffPost]]}}</ref> During her time with Purplow, she became friends with rapper [[Jay Park]], with Jeong participating in a choreography video for Park's "Me Like Yuh".<ref name = hp/> Purplow collaborated with artists including [[Mad Clown]], [[Hyolyn]], and [[Hyoyeon]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edaily.co.kr/News/Read?newsId=02076246615924984&mediaCodeNo=257|title= 패션 소셜미디어 캠스콘, 'WE ARE PURPLOW' 화보 공개 |language=ko|date=May 2, 2017|last=Choi |first=Sung-keun|website=[[Edaily]]}}</ref> She later departed Purplow and formed the hip‑hop-focused dance crew HolyBang in September 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mk.co.kr/news/society/11348893|title= "저게 춤이야? XX이지"...허니제이, 욕설 논란에 입 열었다 |language=ko|date=June 22, 2025|last=Ji |first=Seung-hoon|website=[[Maeil Business Newspaper]]}}</ref> She continued to perform alongside Park, appearing at the 2018 Grand Mint Festival and the 2019 [[Waterbomb festival]].<ref name = hp>{{cite web|url=https://www.harpersbazaar.co.kr/article/59301|title=허니제이와 박재범의 꿀 케미 |language=ko|date=October 14, 2021|website=[[Harper's Bazaar]]|last=Ga |first=Nam-hee}}</ref>

Jeong and the other members of HolyBang competed on the dance competition series ''[[Street Woman Fighter]]'' in August 2021, joining seven other crews.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hankyung.com/article/202108244516H|title= K팝 안무 만든 댄서들 매력 공개…'스트릿우먼파이터' 온다 [종합] |language=ko|date=August 24, 2021|last=Kim |first=So-yeon|website=[[The Korea Economic Daily]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newsis.com/view/NISX20210825_0001559114|title=센언니들 통쾌한 댄스 배틀…'스트릿 우먼 파이터' 들썩|language=ko|date=August 26, 2021|website=[[Newsis]]}}</ref> HolyBang won the competition in October 2021, defeating runner‑up Hook and fellow finalists Lachica and Coca N'Butter; the crew received ₩50 million, a trophy, and an opportunity to sign an advertising contract with a global beer brand, in which they signed with [[Budweiser]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20211027053700005|title=K-댄스 신드롬 일으킨 '스우파' 최종 우승은 '홀리뱅'|date=October 27, 2021|website=[[Yonhap News Agency]]|last=Kang |first=Ae-ran}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.khan.co.kr/article/202110311728001|title=진한 여운 남긴 '스트릿 우먼 파이터'…기획의도, 왜 이렇게까지 통했나|language=ko|date=October 31, 2021|last=Yoo |first=Kyung-sun|website=[[Kyunghyang Shinmun]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.hankooki.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=6745621|title='스우파' 상금 5000만원 주인공은 홀리뱅…허니제이 "대한민국 댄서 너무 멋있어"[종합]|language=ko|last=Cho |first=Eun-ae|website=[[Hankook Ilbo]]|date=October 27, 2021}}</ref> After her win, Park asked that she not join his backing dance crew, expressing a desire for her to pursue an independent career; they did not perform together onstage until 2024, when they both appeared at the Waterbomb festival.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mt.co.kr/entertainment/2024/08/20/2024082019162812154|title= 허니제이, 박재범 해고에 눈물…"최선 다했는데, 직장 잃은 느낌" |date=August 20, 2024|last=Jeon |first=Hyeong-ju|website=[[Maeil Business Newspaper]]}}</ref>

In May 2022, Jeong signed with [[More Vision]], a label founded by Jay Park.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inews24.com/view/1478343|title=[영상]허니제이, 박재범 레이블 '모어비전' 합류…시선강탈 비주얼 필름 공개|language=ko|date=May 9, 2022|last=Moon |first=Su-ji|website=[[INews24]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.khan.co.kr/article/202205090716003|title=허니제이, 박재범과 손 잡았다…모어비전 行|date=May 9, 2022|website=[[Kyunghyang Shinmun]]|last=Lee |first=Dawon}}</ref> Jeong was the first artist signed to More Vision and released the songs "Look" and "Honey Drop", collaborating with producers Blase and Bronze and featuring artist Lil Cherry.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fromtheintercom.com/interview-honey-j-choreographer-artist-and-dance-pioneer/|title=Interview: Honey J, choreographer, artist, and dance pioneer|last=Jiang |first=Nancy|website=From The Intercom|date=September 30, 2022}}</ref> Jeong formed a new dance crew, Bumsup, to compete in the third season of the ''Street Woman Fighter'' series, [[World of Street Woman Fighter]] in 2025, alongside fellow alumni Aiki and [[Leejung Lee]]. Their performance amassed nearly 16 million views, described by ''[[The Korea Times]]'' as the most ever across the ''Street Woman Fighter'' franchise.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/entertainment/shows-dramas/20250724/did-world-of-street-woman-fighter-succeed-in-winning-global-fans|title=Did 'World of Street Woman Fighter' succeed in winning global fans?|website=[[The Korea Times]]|last=Park |first=Jin-hai|date=July 24, 2025}}</ref> During filming, Jeong and Aiki drew criticism for making inappropriate remarks towards another team, with both issuing apologies for the remarks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://biz.chosun.com/entertainment/enter_general/2025/06/22/WMSIXSDUMJURZFOXBRAZYV54R4/|title="국가유산급 무대"→하루 만에 욕설 논란…허니제이, 팬들 충격 속 사과 (Oh!쎈 이슈)|language=ko|date=June 22, 2025|website=[[The Chosun Ilbo]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://biz.chosun.com/entertainment/enter_general/2025/07/07/QYBLKBESP5N5ZR3NT6MOXULNSE/|title='무례 논란' 허니제이·아이키, AG스쿼드에 직접 사과.."정말 미안해" [Oh!쎈 예고]|language=ko|date=July 7, 2025|website=[[The Chosun Ilbo]]}}</ref> The team was eliminated in the eighth episode, finishing behind Motiv, AG Squad, and Osaka Ojo Gang.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://biz.chosun.com/entertainment/enter_general/2025/07/16/45RJFE3ONSJVPLI7L3HGEUBGOU/|title=허니제이 "마지막까지 함께하고 싶었다"...범접, '스우파3' 파이널 좌절 [종합]|language=ko|date=July 16, 2025|website=[[The Chosun Ilbo]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://biz.chosun.com/entertainment/enter_general/2025/07/16/UWW36ADPTGYJTVBP5ONZEUM4UE/|title=범접, 파이널 문턱 못 넘었다..눈물의 탈락 "두 번은 못할 것 같아"(월드 오브 스우파)[종합]|date=July 16, 2025|language=ko|website=[[The Chosun Ilbo]]}}</ref>

== Other ventures ==
[[File:Members of BumsUp at JTBC Studio Ilsan, 2021.jpg|thumb|upright=1|Honey J (second from right) with dancers Ri.Hey, No:ze, and Monika in 2021.]]

=== Public image and endorsements ===
Jeong has been described by the ''[[South China Morning Post]]'' as "one of the most respected and experienced dancers in South Korea", with writer Ben Chin noting her preference for "midriff-baring outfits with hip-hop flair". She serves as an ambassador for fashion retailer Han Style, which stocks brands such as [[Off-White (company)|Off‑White]] and [[JW Anderson]], and appeared in a pictorial for ''[[Playboy|Playboy Korea]]'' in 2017.<ref name = bhi>{{cite web|url=https://www.scmp.com/magazines/style/celebrity/article/3155868/meet-k-pops-hottest-dancers-lee-jung-choreographed|title=Meet K-pop’s hottest dancers: Lee Jung choreographed for Blackpink’s Lisa and Noze’s Hey Mama challenge went viral on TikTok – but is veteran Honey J even better?|website=[[South China Morning Post]]|last=Chin |first=Ben|date=November 13, 2021}}</ref>

She is a professor of practical dance at the Korea Art Conservatory and at [[Kyung Hee University]].<ref name = bhi/> Previously she taught at [[Hanlim Arts School]], where she instructed Noh Jihye, later known as No:ze, who went on to join Jeong's dance group BumsUp.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.segye.com/newsView/20211121503293|title=허니제이도 아이돌 데뷔 권했다는데...노제 고교 시절 사진 보니|language=ko|date=November 21, 2021|last=Kang |first=Min-seon|website=[[Segye Ilbo]]}}</ref> In a 2021 episode of ''[[I Live Alone (TV program)|I Live Alone]]'', she revealed plans to launch her own brand to secure a more stable income during the [[COVID‑19 pandemic in South Korea|COVID‑19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scmp.com/magazines/style/k-pop/article/3158295/5-k-pop-backup-dancers-stealing-show-blackpinks-jennie|title=5 K-pop backup dancers stealing the show, from Blackpink’s Jennie lookalike Kim Ji-hyang and Chungha’s choreographer Wood, to Noze who shared the spotlight with Exo’s Kai|date=December 3, 2021|last=Jeong |first=Lucy|website=[[South China Morning Post]]}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In September 2022, Jeong announced that she was pregnant and engaged to be married; the identity of her fiancé was not disclosed at the time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/2022/09/16/entertainment/kpop/korea-honey-j-engagement/20220916120124977.html|title=Korean dancer Honey J makes marriage, pregnancy announcement|date=September 16, 2022|last=Shin |first=Min-hee|website=[[Korea JoongAng Daily]]}}</ref> Following media reports alleging that her fiancé was ten years her junior, her agency More Vision issued a statement denying the claim and the article was subsequently removed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/2022/09/22/entertainment/kpop/Honey-J-fiance-rumor/20220922164134762.html|title=Honey J's agency sets record straight regarding reports about her fiancé|date=September 22, 2022|website=[[Korea JoongAng Daily]]|last=Lee |first=Jae-lim}}</ref> She later identified her fiancé as Jeong Dam, a model who had worked abroad; the couple married on November 18, 2022. Jeong gave birth to a daughter, Love, in April 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news1.kr/entertain/broadcast-tv/4980500|title='정담♥' 허니제이 "남편 직업은 원래 모델…해외에서 주로 활동해"|language=ko|date=March 13, 2022|website=[[News1 (South Korean newspaper)|News1]]|last=Lee |first=Ji-hyun}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elle.co.kr/article/83602|title=허니제이 딸 정러브, 생후 8개월 만에 TV 데뷔?|language=ko|date=January 10, 2024|last=Ra |first=Hyo-jin|website=[[Elle (magazine)|Elle]]}}</ref>

'''Louise Ekman''' (born 10 April 1997) is a Swedish [[high jump]]er. She won the [[Swedish Indoor Athletics Championships|Swedish Indoor Championships]] in 2023. In 2026, she moved to third on the Swedish all-time indoor list with a jump of 1.96 metres, later placing sixth overall at the [[2026 World Athletics Indoor Championships|2026 World Indoor Championships]].<ref>{{cite web|title= Louise Ekman|website=World Athletics|accessdate=27 Feb 2026|url=https://worldathletics.org/athletes/sweden/louise-ekman-14487342}}</ref>

==Biography== 
From [[Gävle]],<ref>{{cite web|date=29 November 2018|title= Louise Ekman honored to inaugurate the goat|url= https://www.sverigesradio.se/artikel/7101407|website=Sverigesradio.se|accessdate=27 Feb 2026}}</ref> Ekman is coached by Bengt Jönsson, and is a member of Gefle IF.<ref name="baker">{{cite web|url= https://swedenherald.com/article/swedish-hidden-star-louise-ekman-ready-for-world-indoor-championships-after-196-meters-personal-best|title= Louise Ekman ready for World Indoor Championships after huge leap, third all-time among Swedish women|date=24 Feb 2026|accessdate=27 Feb 2026|website=Sweden Herald}}</ref><ref name="lewis"/> She was a finalist in the [[high jump]] at the [[2019 European Athletics U23 Championships – Women's high jump|2019 European Athletics U23 Championships]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.svt.se/nyheter/lokalt/gavleborg/louise-ekman-vidare-till-em-final-i-hojdhopp |website=svt.se|title=Louise Ekman advances to European Championship final in high jump
|date= July 12, 2019|accessdate=27 Feb 2026}}</ref> Ekman placed third at the 2021 [[Swedish Indoor Athletics Championships]] in [[Malmö]] with 1.83 metres, and was runner-up the following year behind [[Maja Nilsson]] with a jump of 1.84 metres.<ref>{{Cite web|title= Swedish Indoor Championships|url= https://worldathletics.org/competition/calendar-results/results/7179876?eventId=10229526
|date=25 February 2022|access-date=27 Feb 2026| website=World Athletics}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title= Swedish Indoor Championships|url= https://worldathletics.org/competition/calendar-results/results/7161955?eventId=10229526
|date=17 February 2021|access-date=27 Feb 2026| website=World Athletics}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=21 Feb 2021|title= Louise Ekman from Gävle third at the Swedish Indoor Championships in high jump |url= https://www.sverigesradio.se/artikel/louise-ekman-fran-gavle-trea-pa-inomhus-sm-i-hojdhopp |website=Sverigesradio.se|accessdate=27 Feb 2026}}</ref>

Ekman won the Swedish Indoor Athletics Championships in 2023 February in Malmö, winning ahead of [[Bianca Salming]] with 1.81 metres.<ref>{{Cite web|title= Swedish Indoor Championships|url= https://worldathletics.org/competition/calendar-results/results/7193423?eventId=10229526
|date=17 February 2023|access-date=27 Feb 2026| website=World Athletics}}</ref> Later that year, she was also runner-up competing outdoors at the [[2023 Nordic Athletics Championships]] in [[Copenhagen]] and the [[Swedish Athletics Championships]] in [[Söderhamn]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://worldathletics.org/competition/calendar-results/results/7176907?eventId=10229526
|title=Nordic Senior Championships|date=27 May 2023
|access-date=27 Feb 2026| website=World Athletics}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title= Swedish Championships|url=https://worldathletics.org/competition/calendar-results/results/7193429?eventId=10229526
|date=28 July 2023|access-date=27 Feb 2026| website=World Athletics}}</ref>

In June 2024, she jumped 1.85 to place third at the Swedish Athletics Championships in [[Uddevalla]].<ref>{{Cite web|title= Swedish Championships|url= https://worldathletics.org/competition/calendar-results/results/7207644?eventId=10229526
|date=28 June 2024|access-date=27 Feb 2026| website=World Athletics}}</ref> In February 2025, she cleared 1.87 metres to place second behind [[Engla Nilsson]] at the Swedish Indoor Championships in [[Växjö]].<ref>{{Cite web|title= Swedish Indoor Championships|url= https://worldathletics.org/competition/calendar-results/results/7217885?eventId=10229526
|date=21 Feb 2025|access-date=27 Feb 2026| website=World Athletics}}</ref> In August, she was runner-up to [[Ella Junnila]] at the [[Finnkampen]] in Stockholm.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://worldathletics.org/competition/calendar-results/results/7218010?eventId=10229526
|title= Finnkampen|date=22 August 2025|access-date=27 Feb 2026| website=World Athletics}}</ref>

At the start of 2026, Ekman added nine centimetres to her personal best, first jumping 1.91 meters in [[Lyon]], France, before having a third place finish in February at the [[Banskobystricka latka]] in [[Banská Bystrica]], Slovakia, a [[World Athletics Indoor Tour]] Silver meeting, with 1.96 metres.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.european-athletics.com/home/news/2-00m-topic-clears-landmark-barrier-to-win-at-tipos-banskobystricka-latka|website=European Athletics|accessdate=27 Feb 2026|title= 2.00m! Topić clears landmark barrier to win at Tipos Banskobystricka latka|first=
Jasmine |last=Trapnell|date=
24 Feb 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.friidrott.se/tavling-landslag/nyhetsarkiv-tavling-landslag/galen-succe-for-louise-ekman-valdigt-lycklig/|website= friidrott.se|accessdate=27 Feb 2026|title= Crazy success for Louise Ekman – "Very happy!"|date=Feb 24, 2026}}</ref> The jump moved her third on the Swedish all-time indoor list and was the best jump by a Swedish indoors for 12 years. |title= Mahuchikh regains world indoor high jump title in Kujawy Pomorze|date=20 March 2026 
|access-date=20 March 2026| website=World Athletics}}</ref>

On 15 August, she placed sixth with a clearance of 1.88 metres at the [[2026 European Athletics Championships – Women's high jump |2026 European Championships]] in [[Birmingham]], England.<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=15 August 2026 |publisher=Athletics Weekly |title=Mahuchikh completes hat-trick of European titles |url=https://athleticsweekly.com/news/mahuchikh-completes-hat-trick-of-european-titles-1040012631/}}</ref>

'''Javiera Petersen Muga''' (born 7 April 1990) is a Chilean [[economist]]. She serves as the [[Undersecretary]] of Economy and Small Businesses, a role she has held since March 2022. She is a prominent member of the [[Communist Party of Chile]] (PCCh).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2022-02-01 |title=Paridad de género y mayoría de profesionales de la U. de Chile: Quiénes son los subsecretarios nombrados por Gabriel Boric |url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/Nacional/2022/02/01/1045628/boric-subsecretarios-listado-perfil-datos.html |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Emol |language=Spanish}}</ref>

== Early life & career ==
Petersen was born in [[Valparaíso]], Chile.<ref name=":0" /> She holds a master's degree in economic analysis from the [[University of Chile]] and a master's degree in economic governance and policy from the [[University of London]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |title=Ministry of Economy, Development and Tourism |url=https://www.gob.cl/en/ministries/ministry-of-economy-development-and-tourism/ |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Government of Chile |language=en}}</ref> In 2022, prior to her government appointment, she was a PhD student at [[University College London]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Ortiz |first=Florencia |date=2022-02-02 |title=Quién es Javiera Petersen: la próxima subsecretaria de Economía del gobierno de Gabriel Boric |url=https://www.biobiochile.cl/noticias/nacional/chile/2022/02/02/quien-es-javiera-petersen-la-proxima-subsecretaria-de-economia-del-gobierno-de-gabriel-boric.shtml |access-date=2026-03-03 |website=BioBioChile |language=es}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Bobadilla |first=Matias |last2= |first2= |date=2022-02-01 |title=Quién es Javiera Petersen, nueva subsecretaria de Economía |url=https://www.pauta.cl/actualidad/2022/02/01/javiera-petersen-nueva-subsecretaria-de-economia.html |access-date=2026-03-04 |website=Radio Pauta 100.5 |language=es}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Alonso |first=Carlos |date=2022-03-27 |title=Javiera Petersen: “Las medidas que se anunciarán es la mejor política pública, dado el actual momento de la crisis” |url=https://www.latercera.com/pulso/noticia/javiera-petersen-las-medidas-que-se-anunciaran-es-la-mejor-politica-publica-dado-el-actual-momento-de-la-crisis/AZCEPOLETNH4LOE64XRETOHQU4/ |access-date=2026-03-04 |website=[[La Tercera]] |language=es}}</ref>

Petersen is a co-founder and executive director of the Observatorio de Políticas Económicas (OPES), an economic [[think tank]] and applied research centre.<ref name=":1" /> She has also worked as an external consultant for the World Bank and as a researcher at the Microdata Centre at the University of Chile.<ref name=":2" />

== Political career ==
In 2011, Petersen participated in the [[2011–2013 Chilean student protests|Chilean Winter]], a series of student-led protests, which led to her involvement with the [[Communist Youth of Chile]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=González |first=Felipe |date=2021-08-06 |title=Javiera Petersen y Fernando Carmona: ¿Quiénes son los dos primeros comunistas en cruzar el muro para sumarse al comando de Boric? |url=https://www.theclinic.cl/2021/08/06/javiera-petersen-y-fernando-carmona-quienes-son-los-dos-primeros-comunistas-en-cruzar-el-muro-para-sumarse-al-comando-de-boric/ |access-date=2026-03-04 |website=The Clinic |language=es}}</ref> During the [[2017 Chilean general election|2017 presidential election]], she was a member of the economic team for independent candidate [[Alejandro Guillier]].<ref name=":4" />

In 2021, Petersen worked on the [[2021 Chilean presidential primaries|presidential primary]] campaign of [[Daniel Jadue]], mayor of [[Recoleta, Chile|Recoleta]], contributing to the development of his economic policy platform. Following Jadue's defeat in the [[Communist Party of Chile|Communist Party]] primary, she joined the campaign of [[Gabriel Boric]].<ref name=":3" />

In February 2022, Petersen was appointed Undersecretary of Economy and Small Businesses by president-elect Boric.<ref name=":0" /> She took office on 11 March 2022; at age 31, she was the youngest undersecretary in Boric's cabinet.<ref name=":3" />

=== International ===
A May 2025 note by ''[[Clarín (Argentine newspaper)|Clarín]]'' described Falcón as a favourite of [[Claudio Tapia]], the president of the [[Argentine Football Association]]. His career quickly rose in prominence, with the coordinator of the referees' body, former referee Federico Beligoy, assigning several matches in the Primera B and the [[AFA Liga Profesional de Fútbol]] to Falcón.<ref name="chiquitapia"/> He was subsequently promoted to international [[FIFA]] status in 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=Argentinian Football Association {{!}} International match officials |url=https://inside.fifa.com/associations/ARG/referees |access-date=13 April 2026 |work=Inside FIFA |date=1 January 2026}}</ref><ref name="fifa2026">{{cite news |last1=Trasmonte |first1=Jorge Mario |title=El uno por uno de los árbitros que van al Mundial |url=https://www.ole.com.ar/mundial/mundial-2026/arbitraje-fifa-mundial2026-designacion_0_oSDcMwLrrO.html |access-date=13 April 2026 |work=[[Olé (sports newspaper)|Olé]] |date=9 April 2026 |language=es}}</ref>

International competitions within [[CONMEBOL]] for Falcón include [[Copa Sudamericana]] and [[Copa Libertadores]] editions and [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|qualification matches]] for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], making his debut on 20 March 2025 in a match between [[Peru national football team|Peru]] and [[Bolivia national football team|Bolivia]].<ref name="chiquitapia"/> In 2024, Falcón was chosen for the [[2024 Copa América]] in the United States, where he oversaw a single [[2024 Copa América Group D#Costa Rica vs Paraguay|group stage match for Group D]] between [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]] and [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]] at the [[Q2 Stadium]] in [[Austin, Texas]].<ref name="asdiario">{{cite news |last1=Martín J |first1=Víctor |title=Así es Yael Falcón Pérez, el árbitro del Costa Rica - Paraguay de Copa América 2024 |url=https://as.com/us/futbol/copa-america/asi-es-yael-falcon-perez-el-arbitro-del-costa-rica-paraguay-de-copa-america-2024-n/ |access-date=13 April 2026 |work=[[Diario AS]] |date=2 July 2024 |language=es}}</ref> Falcón had another controversial performance, this time at a game between [[Alianza Lima]] of Peru and [[Deportes Iquique]] during the [[2025 Copa Libertadores]]{{'s}} third round.<ref name="infobae2">{{cite news |last1=Solis Ruiz |first1=Miguel |title=Perfil de Yael Falcón Pérez, el árbitro del Perú vs Bolivia que debutará en Eliminatorias 2026: ‘pragmático’, “deja jugar” y generó polémica en Alianza vs Iquique |url=https://www.infobae.com/peru/deportes/2025/03/20/perfil-de-yael-falcon-perez-el-arbitro-del-peru-vs-bolivia-que-debutara-en-eliminatorias-2026-pragmatico-deja-jugar-y-genero-polemica-en-alianza-vs-iquique/ |access-date=13 April 2026 |work=[[Infobae]] |date=20 March 2025 |language=es}}</ref>

Between 2023 and 2024, Falcón also refereed in [[Football in Saudi Arabia|Saudi football]] after the Saudis submitted a request for professional referees.<ref name="casar"/> Also outside CONMEBOL, Falcón was appointed as a referee for the [[2023 FIFA U-20 World Cup]] in his native Argentina.<ref>{{cite news |title=Yael Falcón Pérez: de protagonizar el polémico clásico de Avellaneda, a dirigir el Mundial Sub 20 |url=https://www.ole.com.ar/futbol-internacional/mundialsub20-arbitros-yaelfalconperez-polemica_0_k2F9ndH7ec.html |access-date=13 April 2026 |work=[[Olé (sports newspaper)|Olé]] |date=20 April 2023 |language=es}}</ref> Falcón was appointed as a referee for the [[Football at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|men's tournament]] of the [[2024 Summer Olympics]].<ref name="olympics"/> In April 2026 FIFA named Falcón as a central referee for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026 edition]] of the [[FIFA World Cup]] along with fellow Argentine assistant referees Facundo Rodríguez and Maximiliano Del Yesso.<ref name="yesindeed">{{cite news |last1=Sisto |first1=Hernán |title=Récord: los tres árbitros argentinos que dirigirán el Mundial 2026 |url=https://www.tycsports.com/mundial/herrera-tello-falcon-perez-arbitros-argentina-mundial-id723317.html |access-date=13 April 2026 |work=[[TyC Sports]] |date=9 April 2026 |language=es}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Falcón is a [[physical education|physical education teacher]] by profession and, in addition to his refereeing activities, was a municipal employee in the city of [[Lanús]] from 2020 to 2023.<ref name="casar"/> In 2017, he was honored by the [[Argentine Olympic Committee]] for his courageous reaction during the Primera C match where he is credited with saving Olariaga's life following a head collision.<ref name="casar"/> He also worked for the local government of Mayor [[Néstor Grindetti]] in Lanús (2015–2023).<ref>{{cite news |last1=Butarazzi |first1=Leandro |title=La particular historia del árbitro que debutará el domingo en el 15 de Abril |url=https://www.unosantafe.com.ar/ovacion/la-particular-historia-del-arbitro-que-debutara-el-domingo-el-15-abril-n2163230.html |access-date=13 April 2026 |work=Uno Santa Fe |date=30 January 2019 |language=es}}</ref>

Falcón resides in Lanús.<ref>{{cite news |title=El árbitro del Independiente - Racing trabajó hasta este miércoles en la intendencia de Grindetti |url=https://www.tycsports.com/racing-club/arbitro-yael-falcon-perez-trabajo-hasta-este-miercoles-en-la-intendencia-de-grindetti-id505181.html |access-date=13 April 2026 |work=[[TyC Sports]] |date=13 April 2023 |language=es}}</ref>

'''Knut André Skjærstein''' (born 6 July 1995) is a Norwegian footballer who plays as a goalkeeper for [[Strømmen IF]].

==Career==
He hails from [[Kolbotn]]<ref name=kolb/> and played for [[Kolbotn Fotball|Kolbotn]] until the age of 19. He then joined the umbrella team in the region, [[Follo FK]], where he made his senior debut in September 2014. In 2018 he moved on to promotion chasers in the [[2. divisjon]], [[KFUM-Kameratene Oslo|KFUM]]. The team won promotion and established themselves in the [[1. divisjon]].<ref name=nff>{{NFF|2980002}}</ref>

In January 2020 he was on trial with [[Eliteserien]] team [[Aalesunds FK|Aalesund]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nettavisen.no/sport/kilder-til-nettavisen-aafk-har-lagt-inn-bud-pa-keeper/s/12-95-3423909876|title=Kilder til Nettavisen: - Aafk har lagt inn bud på keeper|date=14 January 2020|work=Nettavisen|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> He was eventually signed to the first tier by [[Lillestrøm SK]] in August 2021.<ref name=kolb>{{cite news|url=https://www.oblad.no/knut-andr-26-fra-kolbotn-blir-eliteseriekeeper/s/5-68-1038852|title=Knut André (26) fra Kolbotn blir eliteseriekeeper|date=9 August 2021|work=Østlandets Blad|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rb.no/fjerdemann-ut-i-keeperkampen-pa-et-ar-jeg-har-planer-om-a-bli-her/s/5-43-1620891|title=Fjerdemann ut i keeperkampen på et år: – Jeg har planer om å bli her|date=11 August 2021|work=Romerikes Blad|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref>

He made his Eliteserien debut in September 2021 against Brann.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nettavisen.no/sport/eksperten-sjokkert-over-det-han-fikk-se-av-brann-noe-av-det-verre/s/12-95-3424177685|title=Eksperten sjokkert over det han fikk se av Brann: - Noe av det verre|date=11 September 2021|work=Nettavisen|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> However he did not break through and was loaned out to [[Egersunds IK|Egersund]] in 2023.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.vg.no/sport/i/9zQx0l/lsk-laaner-ut-keeper-henter-tilbake-en-annen|title=LSK låner ut keeper – henter tilbake en annen|date=21 August 2023|work=VG|agency=NTB|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> After they secured promotion to the [[2024 1. divisjon]], the move was made permanent.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rb.no/forlater-lsk-jeg-er-ferdig/s/5-43-2182590|title=Forlater LSK: – Jeg er ferdig|date=11 January 2024|work=Romerikes Blad|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> He was their first-choice goalkeeper until a blood clot hospitalized him and halted his career.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tv2.no/sport/fikk-skrekkbeskjed-tragisk/17086996/|title=Fikk skrekkbeskjed: – Tragisk|date=16 October 2024|publisher=TV 2|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.oblad.no/i-oktober-fikk-knut-andr-skrekkbeskjeden-i-dag-var-han-med-a-knuse-rosenborg/s/5-68-1696444|title=I oktober fikk Knut-André skrekkbeskjeden – i dag var han med å knuse Rosenborg|date=22 June 2025|work=Østlandets Blad|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref>

He was released and spent the first half of 2025 without a club. In June 2025, he was picked up by Eliteserien club [[Kristiansund BK]] who faced a crisis with their existing goalkeepers being injured.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sportsbibelen.no/forlot-lsk-i-2023-klar-for-eliteserieklubb/|title=Forlot LSK i 2023. Klar for Eliteserieklubb|date=17 June 2025|work=Sportsbibelen|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> He made his KBK debut against Rosenborg.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tk.no/skjarstein-blir-kbk-keeper/s/5-51-1702172|title=Skjærstein blir KBK-keeper|date=16 June 2025|work=Tidens Krav|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> Then, in the [[2025 Norwegian Football Cup|2025 cup]] tie against Stabæk, Skjærstein became the "hero" by saving two efforts in the [[penalty shootout]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nrk.no/mr/fotball-nm_-knut-andre-skjaerstein-ble-cuphelt-for-kristiansund-mot-alle-odds-1.17477788|title=Knut-André ble cuphelt mot alle odds|date=9 July 2025|publisher=NRK|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref> After Kristiansund's other goalkeepers returnd from injury, Skjærstein moved on and signed for [[Strømmen IF|Strømmen]] in 2026.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.strommen-if.no/nyheter/velkommen-til-klubbens-nye-keeper|title=Velkommen til klubbens nye keeper|date=28 January 2026|publisher=Strømmen IF|language=no|access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref>

'''Leonel Gomes Silva Fernandes''' (born 12 March 1998) is a Portuguese [[handball]] player.

== Career ==
He started playing handball at ADA Maia, and in 2013 he joined the youth department of [[FC Porto (handball)|Porto]]. From 2016 to 2018 he was loaned back to ADA Maia.<ref>[https://www.handball-base.com/leonel-fernandes Handball Base profile]</ref>

From 2018 he played for Porto's first team, where he won the [[Andebol 1|Portuguese Championship]] in 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2023. He also won the Cup in 2019 and 2021.

== National team ==
He represented Portugal at the [[2018 Mediterranean Games]], at the [[2021 World Men's Handball Championship]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://portal.fpa.pt/2020/10/qualifiers-ehf-euro-2022-os-herois-do-mar-estao-de-volta/|title=Qualifiers EHF Euro 2022: Os Heróis do Mar estão de volta|publisher=portal.fpa.pt|date=30 October 2020|access-date=30 October 2020|language=pt}}</ref> and at the [[2022 European Men's Handball Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://portal.fpa.pt/2022/01/ehf-euro-2022-conheca-os-18-convocados-finais/|title=EHF Euro 2022: Conheça os 18 convocados finais|publisher=portal.fpa.pt|access-date=11 January 2022|language=pt}}</ref>

At the [[2023 World Men's Handball Championship]] he represented Portugal again, where they finished 13th. In 2025 he was part of the Portugal team that reached the semifinals of the [[2025 World Men's Handball Championship|World Championship]] for the first time in history. They lost the semifinals to Denmark and the third place playoff to France.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sport.tv2.dk/haandbold/2025-02-02-sindssyg-afslutning-paa-dramatisk-bronzekamp|title=Sindssyg afslutning på dramatisk bronzekamp|publisher=[[TV2 Danmark]]|first=Oliver|last=Orup Kristensen|date=2 February 2025|accessdate=2 February 2025|language=da|trans-title=Insane finish to bronze match}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ihf.info/sites/default/files/competitions/7c2253d6-1efd-4495-b237-6171c39fac97/pdf/PORTOTAL.PDF |title=29th IHF Men’s World Championship 2025: Cumulative Statistics Portugal |website=ihf.info|publisher=[[International Handball Federation]] |language=en |access-date=2025-02-12}}</ref> At the [[2026 European Men's Handball Championship]] he was part of the Portugal team that got 5th place, their best ever finish at a European Championship.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sport.tv2.dk/live/haandbold/2026-01-30-em-semifinalerne/historiske-portugal?entry=42743564-6e5e-40f5-8bf5-9ebb67009ecd|publisher=TV2 Danmark|title=Historiske Portugal|date=30 January 2026|access-date=30 January 2026|language=da}}</ref>

'''Marie Colomb''' (born 1995) is a French actress. She rose to prominence for starring in [[Rodrigo Sorogoyen]]'s 2022 thriller film ''[[The Beasts]]'', for which she received a nomination for the [[Goya Award for Best Supporting Actress]]. In 2025, she received the [[Trophée Chopard]] at the [[2025 Cannes Film Festival|Cannes Film Festival]] and Madame Figaro Rising Star Award at [[2025 Canneseries|Canneseries]].

==Career==
In 2017, Colomb made her feature acting debut starring in ''Un, deux, trois...'', a comedy drama film directed by Mathieu Gari.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.allocine.fr/film/fichefilm_gen_cfilm=254423.html|title=Un, deux, trois...|work=[[AlloCiné]]|lang=fr|accessdate=22 April 2026}}</ref> In 2019, she starred in the [[titular role]] of [[France 2]] limited series ''Laëtitia'', based on the murder of Laëtitia Perrais.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.franceinter.fr/culture/laetitia-un-fait-divers-devenu-serie-par-jean-xavier-de-lestrade|title=L'affaire Laetitia au cœur d'une série télévisée|work=[[Radio France]]|date=21 September 2020|accessdate=22 April 2026|first=Fanny|last=Leroy|lang=fr}}</ref> It was broadcast in the United States by [[HBO]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2021/08/hbo-french-drama-laetitia-the-staircase-director-jean-xavier-de-lestrade-1234811279/|title=HBO Picks Up French Drama 'Laetitia' From 'The Staircase' Director Jean-Xavier de Lestrade, Sets Premiere Date & Trailer|work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=9 August 2021|accessdate=22 April 2026|first=Peter|last=White}}</ref> She starred in thriller film ''Rascal'', which had its world premiere at the [[2020 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.screendaily.com/news/cannes-reveals-2020-official-selection-titles/5150302.article|title=Cannes reveals 2020 Official Selection titles|work=[[Screen International]]|date=4 June 2020|accessdate=22 April 2026|first=Orlando|last=Parfitt}}</ref> In 2021, she starred as Marianne in Vincent Maël Cardona's ''Magnetic Beats'', which premiered at the [[Directors' Fortnight]] of the [[2021 Cannes Film Festival|Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2021/film/news/cannes-directors-fortnight-the-souvenir-part-ii-2021-lineup-1234991044/|title=Cannes Directors' Fortnight Unveils 2021 Lineup - 'The Souvenir Part II,' 'Ali & Ava,' 'A Chiara,' 'Neptune Frost,' 'Futura' Among Selections|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=8 June 2021|accessdate=22 April 2026|first=Elsa|last=Keslassy}}</ref> She starred in [[Rodrigo Sorogoyen]]'s thriller film ''[[The Beasts]]'' in 2022. For her performance in the film, she received a nomination for the [[Goya Award for Best Supporting Actress]] at the [[37th Goya Awards|37th ceremony]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.screendaily.com/news/the-beasts-prison-77-lead-goya-nominations/5177059.article|title='The Beasts', 'Prison 77' lead Goya nominations|work=Screen International|first=Ellie|last=Calnan|date=1 December 2022|accessdate=22 April 2026}}</ref>

In 2023, she starred in Frédéric Mermoud's drama film ''[[The Path of Excellence]]'', which had its world premiere at the [[76th Locarno Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.screendaily.com/features/locarno-2023-line-up-guide-piazza-grande-and-international-competition-titles/5184550.article|title=Locarno 2023 line-up guide: Piazza Grande and International Competition titles|work=Screen International|date=31 July 2023|accessdate=22 April 2026|first=Nikki|last=Baughan}}</ref> In 2024, she portrayed reality television star [[Loana Petrucciani]] in anthology series ''Cult'', which explores the creation of ''[[Loft Story (French TV series)|Loft Story]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.grazia.fr/people/culte-marie-colomb-interprete-de-loana-dans-une-serie-sur-les-coulisses-de-loft-story-1115151.html|title=Culte : qui est Marie Colomb, interprète de Loana dans cette série sur les coulisses de Loft Story ?|lang=fr|work=[[Grazia|Grazia France]]|date=31 March 2026|accessdate=22 April 2026|first=Jordane|last=Guignon}}</ref> In April 2025, it was reported that Colomb would portray [[Éponine]] in [[Fred Cavayé]]'s film adaptation of ''[[Les Misérables]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.allocine.fr/article/fichearticle_gen_carticle=1000141894.html|title=Ni Pierre Niney, ni François Civil : après Monte-Cristo, on connaît le casting impressionnant de la prochaine adaptation littéraire française d'envergure|work=AlloCiné|lang=fr|date=30 April 2025|accessdate=22 April 2026|first=Brigitte|last=Baronnet}}</ref>

She served on the jury for the International Panorama section at the [[2025 Series Mania]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.prensario.net/SERIES-MANIA-2025-unveils-its-selection-juries-and-guests-48185.note.aspx|title=SERIES MANIA 2025 unveils its selection, juries and guests|work=Prensario|date=13 February 2025|accessdate=22 April 2026}}</ref> In April 2025, she received the ''Madame Figaro'' Rising Star Award at [[Canneseries]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://madame.lefigaro.fr/celebrites/culture/marie-colomb-a-l-ecole-on-jouait-au-loft-et-deja-j-etais-toujours-loana-20250425|title=Marie Colomb : «À l'école, on jouait au Loft et déjà, j’étais toujours Loana»|lang=fr|date=25 April 2025|accessdate=22 April 2026|first=Christelle|last=Laffin|work=[[Madame Figaro]]}}</ref> She also was honored with the [[Trophée Chopard]] at the [[2025 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2025/film/markets-festivals/angelina-jolie-trophee-chopard-award-cannes-film-festival-1236394142/|title=Angelina Jolie to Present Trophée Chopard Award in Cannes|work=Variety|date=12 May 2025|accessdate=22 April 2026|first=Angelique|last=Jackson}}</ref>

''El Pollito'' | birth_place = [[San Fernando del Valle de Catamarca]], [[Argentina]] | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1999|7|24}} | height = {{altura|m=1.79}} | weight = | country = [[Argentina]] | sport = [[Padel]] | position = ''Revés'' (left-side) | turned_pro = 2018 | rank = '''1st''' ([[Premier Padel]]) | partner = [[Arturo Coello]] | highest_ranking = 1st ([[2023 World Padel Tour|2023]], [[Premier Padel 2024|2024]], [[Premier Padel 2025|2025]]) | worlds = [[Padel World Championship|2022, 2024]] | updated = 27 September 2026 }} '''Darío Agustín Tapia Nievas''' (born 24 July 1999), known as '''Agustín Tapia''', is an Argentine professional padel player.{{Cite web|url=https://www.padelfip.com/es/player/agustin-tapia/|title=Agustin Tapia Official Profile 2023|website=Padel FIP|language=es-ES}} He currently holds the number 1 position in the [[International Padel Federation|FIP ranking]], is right-handed, and plays on the backhand side alongside [[Arturo Coello]]. Together, they form the current number one ranked padel pair in [[Premier Padel]]. Despite his young age, he has played with some of the best players in history, such as [[Juan Martín Díaz Martínez|Juan Martín Díaz]], [[Fernando Belasteguín]], and [[Pablo José Lima|Pablo Lima]], eventually becoming world number 1 by winning the [[2023 Vigo Open]] with Coello. They repeated the feat in the [[Premier Padel 2024|2024]] and [[Premier Padel 2025|2025 Premier Padel]] editions, padel main circuit. He is known in the world of padel as "El Mozart de Catamarca" (''The Mozart of Catamarca''),{{cite web|language=es |title="Gato", "Ratón", "Lobo", "Mozart", "Sanyo", "Rengo", qué hay detrás de los apodos de los mejores jugadores de pádel del mundo {{!}} Poli|url=https://www.lavoz.com.ar/deportes/y-mas/gato-raton-lobo-mozart-sanyo-rengo-que-hay-detras-de-los-apodos-de-los-mejores-jugadores-de-padel-del-mundo/ |website=La Voz del Interior}} and he is currently the active player with the most tournament wins. == Padel Career == Agustín Tapia began his career on the [[World Padel Tour]] in [[2018 World Padel Tour|2018]], starting with [[Marcello Jardim]] as his partner.{{Cite web|title=Multiusos Jardim – Agustín Tapia, nueva pareja World Padel Tour 2018|url=https://padelgood.com/multiusos-jardim-agustin-tapia-nueva-pareja-wpt-2018/|work=padelgood.com}} At the [[2018 Catalunya Master|Catalunya Master]], held in March of that year, he already began to stand out, reaching the quarterfinals.{{Cite web|title=Ha nacido una estrella: Agustín Tapia|url=https://as.com/opinion/2018/03/26/blogs/1522083982_162751.html|publisher=Diario AS}} ===Partnership with Juan Martín Díaz=== ====2019==== {{see|2019 World Padel Tour}}In 2019, Tapia became the new partner of 14-time world number one [[Juan Martín Díaz Martínez|Juan Martín Díaz]]. In their first tournament together, they were eliminated in the Round of 16 by three-time world number ones and future partners of Tapia, [[Fernando Belasteguín]] & [[Pablo José Lima|Pablo Lima]]. However, they would play only three more tournaments together due to an injury Díaz sustained at the [[2019 WPT Buenos Aires Master|Buenos Aires Master]], with Tapia playing the subsequent three tournaments alongside different temporary partners.[[File:PPT-Comunidad-de-Madrid08-1355.jpg|right|278x278px|thumb|[[Juan Martín Díaz Martínez|Juan Martín Díaz]], who partnered Tapia in the first half of 2019.]] ===Partnership with Fernando Belasteguín=== Midway through the season, after months of speculation, [[Fernando Belasteguín]] became his new sporting partner.{{Citeweb|title=Fernando Belasteguín y Agustín Tapia, nueva y prometedora pareja|url=https://www.mundipadel.com/fernando-belasteguin-agustin-tapia-nueva-pareja}}{{cite web|title=Belasteguín regresa en Mijas con nueva pareja tras dos meses lesionado|url=https://www.latimes.com/espanol/noticas-mas/articulo/2019-08-06/efe-4038339-15665296-20190806|publisher=Los Angeles Times}} The partnership had one of the largest age differences in the circuit, with a 20 years difference between the two players. They debuted in the [[2019 WPT Mijas Open|Mijas Open]], exiting in the round of 16, however in their second tournament together, the [[2019 Madrid Master|Madrid Master]], they defeated all the top teams on their road to the title, beating the No. 2 ranked team [[Juan Lebrón Chincoa|Juan Lebrón]] & [[Paquito Navarro]] in the round of 16, and the No. 1 rankeds [[Maxi Sánchez]] & [[Sanyo Gutiérrez]] in the final, with Tapia claiming its first professional title, at only 20 years of age.{{citeweb|title=Belasteguín y tres campeones nuevos ganan en Madrid|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2019/09/08/polideportivo/1567952512_591923.html|publisher=AS}} They would also reach the next four tournaments semifinals, but were unable to progress in any of them. At the [[2019 WPT Mexico Open|Mexico Open]], the last tournament before the year-ending [[2019 Master Final|Master Final]], they were unexpectedly eliminated in the round of 16. At the Master Finals, they defeated the newly crowned No. 1 ranked team, Lebrón & Paquito, in the semifinals, but lost in the final against [[Alejandro Galán Romo|Alejandro Galán]] & [[Pablo José Lima|Lima]],{{citeweb|title=El equipo Adeslas hace pleno en el Master Final|url=https://www.marca.com/padel/2019/12/22/5dff7ed546163fa2188b4578.html|work=Marca}} ending the season ranked fourth as a pair. ===2020=== [[File:Bela_Campeón_del_Mundo.jpg|right|278x278px|thumb|[[Fernando Belasteguín]], who partnered Tapia for two seasons.]] {{see|2020 World Padel Tour}} Belasteguín and Tapia continued together in 2020, starting as the No. 5 ranked pair due to other players changing partner, and forming new teams. The season was heavily affected by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and only had 11 tournaments. They began the new season, losing in the quarter-finals of the [[2020 WPT Marbella Master|Marbella Master]], shortly before the circuit was suspended. After a three-month hiatus, they returned to competition in the [[2020 WPT Estrella Damm Open|Estrella Damm Open]], again losing in the quarterfinals. In the [[2020 WPT Vuelve a Madrid Open|third tournament]] of the season, also in Madrid, the Argentine duo reached the final, but lost to the No. 1 ranked team, [[Alejandro Galán Romo|Galán]] & [[Juan Lebrón Chincoa|Lebrón]].{{citeweb|title=Lebrón y Galán se doctoran en una hermosa final en Madrid|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2020/07/19/polideportivo/1595162175_832655.html|publisher=AS}} After two quarter-final exits in the following two Open's, in the sixth tournament of the season, and the only international tournament of the year, the [[2020 WPT Sardinia Open|Sardinia Open]] , Belasteguín and Tapia won their second title together, defeating Javier Ruiz & Uri Botello in the final.{{citeweb|title=Belasteguín-Tapia y Triay-Sainz se estrenan en este año|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2020/09/13/polideportivo/1600022894_965709.html|publisher=AS}} In next four tournaments, they reached one more the final, in the [[2020 WPT Menorca Open|Menorca Open]], but were once again defeated by [[Franco Stupaczuk]] & [[Sanyo Gutiérrez]].{{citeweb|title=Tercer título de Ale y Ariana y primero de Sanyo y Stupaczuk|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2020/09/27/polideportivo/1601207235_213607.html|publisher=AS}} They entered the [[2020 WPT Master Final|Master Final]] as the No. 3 ranked team. Before their quarter-final match, Belasteguín and Tapia announced in an emotional video that the tournament would be their last together.{{citeweb|publisher=Sport|title=Belasteguin y Tapia anuncian su ruptura antes de debutar en el Master Final|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/padel/belasteguin-tapia-anuncian-ruptura-antes-debutar-master-final-8236344}} They went on to defeat Gutiérrez & Stupaczuk in the semifinals and then overcame the No. 1 rankeds Galán & Lebrón, 6–3, 7–6 in the final, which concluded with a 24-point tie-break. With the win, Belasteguín became the oldest Master Final champion, with 41 years, while Tapia became the youngest, at 21 years.{{cite web|title=Bela y Tapia, maestros para la historia|url=https://www.marca.com/padel/2020/12/13/5fd6088c46163fba1a8b4595.html|publisher=Marca}} They finished the season ranked second as a pair, with both ranked third individually. ===Partnership with Pablo Lima=== ====2021==== {{see|2021 World Padel Tour}} [[File:Lima WPT tenerife.jpg|right|278x278px|thumb|[[Pablo José Lima|Pablo Lima]], who partnered Tapia for most of the 2021 season.]] In 2021, Tapia teamed up with three-time world number one [[Pablo José Lima|Pablo Lima]].{{citeweb|title=Pablo Lima confirma que jugará con Agustín Tapia en 2021|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/padel/pablo-lima-confirma-que-jugara-con-agustin-tapia-2021-8238987|publisher=Sport}} They reached the semifinals in their [[2021 WPT Madrid Open|first tournament]] together but failed to repeat the feat in the [[2021 WPT Alicante Open|following event]], suffering a surprise quarterfinal exit at the hands of [[Arturo Coello]] & Miguel Lamperti.{{citeweb|title=Las semifinales del Estrella Damm Alicante, servidas|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/padel/worldpadeltour/20210423/493430472233/las-semifinales-del-estrella-damm-alicante-servidas.html|publisher=Mundo Deportivo}} After a semifinal appearance and an early exit in the round of 16 in the next two tournaments, Lima and Tapia reached their first final in the fifth tournament of the year, the [[2021 WPT Marbella Master|Marbella Master]], where they were defeated by the world number ones, [[Alejandro Galán Romo|Galán]] & [[Juan Lebrón Chincoa|Lebrón]].{{citeweb|title=Ale Galán y Juan Lebrón marcan las diferencia como pareja|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2021/06/13/polideportivo/1623584428_226341.html|publisher=AS}} After two early exits in subsequent tournaments, the Argentine-Brazilian duo reached their second final at the [[2021 WPT Las Rozas Open|Las Rozas Open]], having defeated Galán & Lebrón in the semifinals, where they beat the second-ranked pair, [[Fernando Belasteguín]] & [[Sanyo Gutiérrez]], to claim their first trophy of 2021.{{citeweb|title=Paula Josemaría y Ari Sánchez se destacan como las mejores|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2021/07/25/polideportivo/1627212893_870130.html|publisher=AS}} They went on to win another title at the following tournament, the [[2021 WPT Málaga Open|Malaga Open]], by defeating [[Martín Di Nenno]] & [[Paquito Navarro]].{{citeweb|title=Pablo Lima y Agus Tapia mantienen su ascenso imparable|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2021/08/08/polideportivo/1628425504_318163.html|publisher=AS}} However, the results following the summer break were not as positive, reaching only one semifinal across four tournaments, leading Tapia to decide to end his partnership with Lima.{{Citeweb|title=Triste punto final y despedida para Sanyo-Bela y Lima-Tapia|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2021/09/24/polideportivo/1632516850_788441.html|publisher=AS}} ===Partnership with Sanyo Gutiérrez=== A few days later it was confirmed that [[Sanyo Gutiérrez]] would be his new partner for the remainder of the season.{{Citeweb|title=Sanyo Gutiérrez, otro número 1 que jugará al lado de Agustín Tapia|url=https://www.marca.com/padel/2021/09/22/614b6c3fca4741ff4a8b45f2.html|publisher=Marca}} Together they won a tournament before the end of the year, the [[2021 WPT Swedish Open|Swedish Open]], after defeating the number 2 seeds, [[Martín Di Nenno]] & [[Paquito Navarro]], in the final by 7–5 and 6–0.{{Citeweb|title=Sanyo y Tapia dejan helados a Navarro y Di Nenno y logran su primer título como pareja en Malmoe|url=https://www.marca.com/padel/2021/11/14/619129a4268e3eb4658b4573.html|publisher=Marca}} ====2022==== {{see|2022 World Padel Tour}} {{see|Premier Padel 2022}} [[File:Santo Gutiérrez and Pato Paradiso, World Padel Championship Dubai 2022.jpg|right|278x278px|thumb|[[Sanyo Gutiérrez]], who Tapia played with in the late part of 2021 and fought for the world number 1 spot in 2022.]] In 2022, Tapia continued playing alongside [[Sanyo Gutiérrez|Sanyo]] throughout the year. The pair began the season being eliminated in the [[2022 WPT Miami Open|Miami Open]] semifinals but bounced back to win the [[2022 WPT Reus Open|Reus Open]], defeating Galán & Lebrón in the finals.{{citeweb|title=Tapia y Gutiérrez, campeones del Estrella Damm Reus Costa Daurada Open|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/padel/worldpadeltour/20220313/1001766380/tapia-gutierrez-campeones-estrella-damm-reus-costa-daurada-open.html|publisher=Mundo Deportivo}} However, the world number ones avenged the loss by eliminating them in the semifinals of the [[2022 WPT Vigo Open|Vigo]], [[2022 WPT Alicante Open|Alicante]], and [[2022 WPT Brussels Open|Brussels]] Open's. Next came a victory at the [[2022 WPT Danish Open|Danish Open]],{{citeweb|title=Marta Ortega y Bea González se estrenan esta temporada|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2022/05/22/polideportivo/1653226951_510171.html|publisher=AS}} followed by a semifinal loss to the top-ranked pair in [[2022 WPT Marbella Master|Marbella]], a defeat they avenged in the [[2022 WPT Vienna Open|Vienna Open]] final.{{citeweb|title=Rebelión contra los números uno del pádel en Viena|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/polideportivo/rebelion-contra-los-numeros-uno-del-padel-en-viena-n/|publisher=AS}} At the [[2022 WPT French Open|French Open]], they lost again in the semifinals to Galán & Lebrón, as well as in the [[2022 WPT Valladolid Master|Valladolid Master]] semifinals to [[Arturo Coello]] & [[Fernando Belasteguín|Belasteguin]]. However, they headed into the summer break with wins in [[2022 WPT Valencia Open|Valencia]] (against the world number ones) and [[2022 WPT Málaga Open|Málaga]],{{citeweb|title=Sanyo Gutiérrez y Tapia le dan la vuelta a la final ante Lebrón y Galán|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/polideportivo/sanyo-gutierrez-y-tapia-le-dan-la-vuelta-a-la-final-ante-lebron-y-galan-n/|publisher=AS}} and a 3–5 record against their main rivals, allowing them to rise to the number two spot and significantly close the gap on the top-ranked pair in the rankings.{{citeweb|title=Sanyo Gutiérrez y Agustìn Tapia, quinto título en cinco finales|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/polideportivo/sanyo-gutierrez-y-agustin-tapia-quinto-titulo-en-cinco-finales-n/|publisher=AS}} Nevertheless, they were unable to maintain their level of play during the final months of the competition, advancing past the quarterfinals in only two of the last nine World Padel Tour tournaments of the year. Even so, they finished as the number two ranked pair, with over 10,000 points each, and officially announced their split following the [[2022 WPT Master Final|Master Final]]. In [[Premier Padel 2022|2022]], Tapia also made his debut on the new [[Premier Padel]] circuit. His best performance came at the [[2022 Mexico Major|Mexico Major]], where he reached the final alongside Sanyo but lost in three sets to Belasteguín & Coello.{{cite web|title=El insaciable Belasteguín logra su título 230 junto a Coello en Monterrey|url=https://www.marca.com/padel/2022/12/05/638daef246163fb7108b456f.html|publisher=Marca}} ===Partnership with Arturo Coello=== ====2023==== {{see|2023 World Padel Tour}} {{see|Premier Padel 2023}} [[File:Arturo Coello (cropped).jpg|right|278x278px|thumb|[[Arturo Coello]], who has partnered Tapia for the last four season, finishing as the number one ranked in three of them.]] In 2023, Tapia joined forces with [[Arturo Coello]] with the goal of dethroning [[Alejandro Galán Romo|Galán]] and [[Juan Lebrón Chincoa|Lebrón]] to claim the number one ranking spot. They started the year in the best possible way, defeating the world numbers ones in two sets at the finals of the [[WPT Abu Dhabi Master 2023|Abu Dhabi Master]], demonstrating their ability to challenge for the number one ranking that year.{{Citeweb|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/padel/world-padel-tour-coello-tapia-83756069|title=World Padel Tour: Coello y Tapia se consagran en Abu Dhabi|website=Sport}} Next, they were eliminated by [[Franco Stupaczuk]] & [[Martín Di Nenno]], who would be their main rival during the season, in the semifinals of [[Premier Padel]]'s [[2023 Ooredoo [[Valentino Libaak|Libaak]] in the final, and mantaining their invincibility in WPT.{{citeweb|title=Coello y Tapia trunca el sueño de los Megapibes|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/polideportivo/coello-y-tapia-trunca-el-sueno-de-los-megapibes-n/|publisher=AS}} They continued their strong run, at the next World Padel Tour event, the [[2023 Chile Open|Chile Open]], winning their third title of the year, after defeating Galán & Lebrón in a 3-sets final, in a match marred by controversial refereeing decisions in the second set.{{citeweb|title=El árbitro fuerza a Tapia-Coello a ganar dos veces a web|title=Oficial: Tapia y Coello son los N1 de WPT|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/padel/20230515/1002005800/oficial-tapia-coello-numeros-uno-world-padel-tour.html|publisher=Mundo Deportivo}} They invictos|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/balonmano/tapia-y-coello-siguen-imparables-e-invictos-n/|publisher=AS}}{{Citeweb|title=Tapia y Coello conquistan su noveno title won in a single season. ====2024==== {{see|Premier Padel 2024}} In 2024, following the conflict between [[World Padel Tour|WPT]] and [[Premier Padel]]/[[International Padel Federation|FIP]], which led the FIP to disregard 2023 World Padel Tour tournaments for ranking purposes, and with Premier Padel now established as the premier circuit, Coello and Tapia began the year as the world's number two pair, despite having finished the previous year in the top spot. In the first tournament of the season, the [[2024 Riyadh P1|Riyadh P1]], they would reach the finals where they faced and lost to [[Alejandro Galán Romo|Galán]] & [[Juan Lebrón Chincoa|Lebrón]] in three sets.{{cite web|title=Los números 1 Lebrón-Galán y Josemaría-Sánchez ganan en Riyadh Season They reached the final of the season's last event but were surprisingly defeated in three sets by Coki Nieto & Jon Sanz.{{citeweb|title=Coki Nieto y Jon Sanz logran lo ‘imposible’ con un triunfo {{see|Premier Padel 2025}} 2025 began just like the previous year, with Coello and Tapia reaching the finals of the season's opening tournament in [[2025 Riyadh P1|Riyadh]], this time against the world's number 3 pair, [[Franco Stupaczuk]] and [[Juan Lebrón Chincoa|Juan Lebrón]], and winning in three sets.{{Citeweb|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/padel/coello-tapia-arrancan-2025-mandando-114405026|title=Coello y Tapia arrancan 2025 mandando|website=Sport}} They did not compete in the [[2025 Gijón P2|Gijón]] and [[2025 Cancún P2|Cancún]] P2 events, along with other top-100 players, due to disputes between Premier Padel and the Professional Padel Players Association.{{cite web|title=Las claves del Cancún Premier Padel P2: bajas sensibles, favoritos y un clima extremo|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/padel/premier-padel/20250310/1002422859/claves-cancun-premier-padel-p2-bajas-sensibles-favoritos-clima-extremo.html|publisher=Mundo Deportivo}} They returned at the [[2025 Miami P1|Miami P1]], where they were eliminated in the semifinals by Lebrón & Stupaczuk, failing to reach a final for the first time in nearly a year (324 days).{{citeweb|title=Bombazo en Miami: ¡Stupa y Lebrón dejan sin final a Tapia-Coello un año después!|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/padel/premier-padel/20250323/1002430949/bombazo-stupaczuk-lebron-dejan-final-n1-ano.html|publisher=Mundo Deportivo}} At the subsequent tournament in [[2025 Santiago P1|Santiago]], they not only suffered their earliest elimination in Premier Padel events but also missed out on the final in two consecutive tournaments (among those they played) for the first time.{{citeweb|title=Tapia y Coello, en su peor arranque como pareja: los datos que lo confirman|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/padel/premier-padel/20250328/1002434422/tapia-coello-peor-arranque-pareja-datos-confirman.html|publisher=Mundo Deportivo}} They stepped up their game by defeating [[Federico Chingotto|Chingotto]] & [[Alejandro Galán Romo|Galán]] in the season's first 'SuperClásico' to win the [[2025 Qatar Major|Qatar Major]],{{Citeweb|title=Tapia y Coello están de vuelta: golpe sobre la mesa en el Major de Qatar|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/padel/premier-padel/20250419/1002448506/tapia-coello-vuelta-golpe-sobre-mesa-major-qatar.html|publisher=Mundo Deportivo}} and repeated the feat a week later to claim the [[2025 Brussels P2|Brussels P2]], extending their head-to-head record against 'ChinGalán' to 12–5 and reaching a 296-day unbeaten streak against their rivals.{{citeweb|title=La increíble racha de Tapia-Coello contra Chingotto-Galán: este es el dato que reafirma su dominio|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/padel/premier-padel/20250429/1002454189/increible-racha-tapia-coello-chingotto-galan-dato-reafirma-dominio.html|publisher=Mundo Deportivo}} However, at the season's eighth tournament in [[2025 Asunción P2|Asunción]], they suffered a shock quarter-final exit at the hands of the 16th-ranked pair, Juanlu Esbri & Salvador Oria. After the unexpected defeat in [[2025 Asunción P2|Asunción]], they embarked on a run lasting over a year in which they reached every final, starting with the [[2025 Buenos Aires P1|Buenos Aires P1]], where they defeated Lucas Bergamini & [[Paquito Navarro]],{{citeweb|title=Coello-Tapia y Ari-Paula triunfan en el primer P1 de Buenos Aires|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/polideportivo/coello-tapia-y-ari-paula-triunfan-en-el-primer-p1-de-buenos-aires-n/|publisher=AS}} followed by the [[2025 Italy Major|Italy Major]], where they were beaten by Galán & Chingotto, ending a 343-day unbeaten streak against their rivals.{{citeweb|title=¡Locura total en el Italy Major! Galán y Chingotto ponen fin a una racha negativa de 343 días|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/padel/premier-padel/20250615/1002483847/locura-total-italy-major-galan-chingotto-ponen-racha-negativa-343-dias.html|publisher=Mundo Deportivo}} In the four tournaments leading up to the summer break, they defeated Lebrón & Stupaczuk to win the [[2025 Valladolid P2|Valladolid P2]], securing their 34th title and surpassing the Galán & Lebrón pairing in trophies won,{{citeweb|title=Tapia y Coello siguen haciendo historia y superan a Lebrón-Galán|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/padel/premier-padel/20250630/1002491907/tapia-coello-siguen-haciendo-historia-superan-lebron-galan.html|publisher=Mundo Deportivo}} and beat 'ChinGalán' at the [[2025 Bordeaux P2|Bordeaux P2]] and the [[2025 Málaga P1|Málaga]] and [[2025 Tarragona P1|Tarragona]] P1s,{{citeweb|title=Tapia y Coello se toman la revancha de Roma ante Chingotto y Galán|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/polideportivo/tapia-y-coello-se-toman-la-revancha-de-roma-ante-chingotto-y-galan-n/|publisher=AS}}{{citeweb|title=Coello y Tapia meten la overtaking [[Fernando Belasteguín]] & [[Pablo José Lima|Pablo Lima]] (who had 36).{{citeweb|title=Coello y Tapia ya forman la segunda mejor pareja de la historia|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/coello-y-tapia-ya-son-la-segunda-mejor-pareja-de-la-historia-n/|publisher=AS}} In the first tournament after the break, the [[2025 Madrid P1|Madrid P1]], they reached the final but were defeated by [[Leandro Augsburger]] and [[Martín Di Nenno]], who beat all the top-3 pairs on their way to the title.{{citeweb|title=Leo Augsburguer y Di Nenno hacen historia en Madrid|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/leo-augsburgues-y-di-nenno-hacen-historia-en-madrid-n/|publisher=AS}} In the following four tournaments both Coello–Tapia and Chingotto–Galán reached the finals with the 'Golden Boys' winning the [[2025 Paris Major|Paris Major]] and the [[2025 Rotterdam P1|Rotterdam P1]] (their 40th title as a pair),{{citeweb|title=Coello y Tapia arrasan a Chingotto y Galán en París|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/coello-y-tapia-arrasan-a-chingotto-y-galan-en-paris-n/|publisher=AS}}{{citeweb|title=Coello (con Tapia) exaspera a Chingotto y Galán|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/coello-con-tapia-exaspera-a-chingotto-y-galan-n/|publisher=AS}} and 'ChinGalán' winning the [[2025 Germany P2|Germany P2]] and the [[2025 Milan P1|Milan P1]].{{citeweb|title=Chingotto y Galán, segundo triunfo del año ante Coello y Tapia|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/chingotto-y-galan-segundo-triunfo-del-ano-ante-coello-y-tapia-n/|publisher=AS}}{{citeweb|title=Galán y Chingotto cierran en Milán con un 6-0 ante Tapia y Galán|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/galan-y-chingotto-cierran-en-milan-con-un-6-0-ante-tapia-y-galan-f202510-n/|publisher=AS}} After not competing in the [[2025 NewGiza P2|NewGiza P2]], they wrapped up the season by competing in four more tournaments and facing 'ChinGalán' in every final. Although they were defeated by them in the [[2025 FIP Pairs World Cup|FIP Pairs World Cup]] finals,{{citeweb|title=Remontada Mundial de Chingotto y Galán|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/remontada-mundial-de-chingotto-y-galan-f202511-n/|publisher=AS}} they finished the regular season by winning the [[2025 Dubai P1|Dubai P1]] and the [[2025 Mexico Major|Mexico Major]],{{citeweb|title=Coello y Tapia vuelven a la senda de la victoria|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/coello-y-tapia-vuelven-a-la-senda-de-la-victoria-f202511-n/|publisher=AS}}{{citeweb|title=Coello-Tapia acaban con la insistencia de Chingotto-Galán|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/coello-tapia-acaban-con-la-insistencia-de-chingotto-galan-f202512-n/|publisher=AS}} mathematically securing the world number 1 ranking for the third consecutive year. With the win in Mexico, Coello and Tapia also became the third most successful pair in history, reaching 54 finals across 66 tournaments, making the finals 81.8% of the time (winning 41 of the 54 finals played, a 75.9% success rate), and amassing a total of 41 titles. '''Peter Reinhardsen''' (born 21 April 1999) is a Norwegian [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a defender for [[Sarpsborg 08]].

==Career==
Born in [[Kristiansand]],<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|new_id=pe554742}}</ref> he joined the academy of [[IK Start]] from [[FK Donn]] at the age of 11. He played for the [[IK Start 2|senior B team]] until the summer of 2018, when he changed to [[FK Jerv]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ikstart.no/nyheter/har-helt-sikkert-ikke-vaert-i-kristiansand-for-siste-gang|title=- Har helt sikkert ikke vært i Kristiansand for siste gang|date=4 January 2023|publisher=IK Start|language=no|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref> Reinhardsen played two years in the [[1. divisjon]] for Jerv, then the [[2020 2. divisjon]] season for [[Arendal Fotball|Arendal]].<ref name=nff>{{NFF|2815824}}</ref> He was welcomed back to Start in 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.eurosport.no/fotball/obos-ligaen/2019/start-henter-tilbake-lokal-spiller_sto8213134/story.shtml|title=Start henter tilbake lokal spiller|date=8 April 2021|publisher=Eurosport|language=no|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref>

Underway in the 2022 season, Reinhardsen found himself in an open conflict with Start. As Reinhardsen visited [[Sarpsborg 08 FF]] as a possible future employer, he was left out of Start's team.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.eurosport.no/fotball/obos-ligaen/2021/straffes-etter-besok-hos-eliteserie-klubb-kan-ikke-aksepteres_sto9146414/story.shtml|title=Straffes etter besøk hos Eliteserie-klubb: – Kan ikke aksepteres|date=16 September 2022|publisher=Eurosport|language=no|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fvn.no/sport/start/i/Q7xndA/konflikten-fortsetter-reinhardsen-har-stilt-krav-til-start|title=Konflikten fortsetter: Reinhardsen har stilt krav til Start|date=29 September 2022|work=Fædrelandsvennen|language=no|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.aftenbladet.no/sport/i/kE6Gma/advokat-hardt-ut-mot-start-mener-reinhardsen-henges-ut|title=Advokat hardt ut mot Start. Mener Reinhardsen henges ut|date=6 October 2022|work=Stavanger Aftenblad|language=no|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref> Reinhardsen proceeded to sign for Sarpsborg 08 in October 2022.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.aftenbladet.no/sport/i/abbqxd/reinhardsen-ferdig-i-start-klar-for-sarpsborg-08-fra-nyaaret|title=Reinhardsen ferdig i Start. Klar for eliteserieklubb|date=19 October 2022|work=Fædrelandsvennen|language=no|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref> Unusually, he vented his frustration with Start in a [[letter to the editor]] of ''[[Fædrelandsvennen]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fvn.no/sport/start/i/0QQO9M/reinhardsen-aapner-opp-i-leserinnlegg-kommer-med-hard-kritikk-av-start|title=Reinhardsen åpner opp i leserinnlegg. Kommer med hard kritikk av Start|date=20 October 2022|work=Fædrelandsvennen|language=no|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref>

Reinhardsen made his [[Eliteserien]] debut in the 2023 season opener.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sa.no/peter-23-det-kribler-i-bade-bein-og-kropp/s/5-46-1419460|title=Peter (23): – Det kribler i både bein og kropp|date=9 April 2023|work=Sarpsborg Arbeiderblad|language=no|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sa.no/far-mye-tillit-i-ny-rolle-etter-a-ha-slitt-med-a-fa-spilletid/s/5-46-1886206|title=Får mye tillit i ny rolle etter å ha slitt med å få spilletid|work=Sarpsborg Arbeiderblad|language=no|date=22 September 2025|access-date=17 June 2026}}</ref>
